Which is exactly where we're going.
Don't lose hope, pal. We're working on a way to get you out of that cell.
They aren't allowing you to leave yet, but being promoted from creature to guest is a good sign.
They aren't allowing you to leave yet, but being promoted from prisoner to guest is a good sign.
We found the hideout of a Free Families separatist movement!
Knowing that Patriarch Tkr is involved, I will try to identify his allies in this undertaking.
Meet me on the Funeral Service Ship if you want me to arrange a meeting with the Patriarchy Police.
Do you want to inform Patriarchy Forces about this separatist movement?
I'll set up a meeting with my contact.(male contact)
We'll need to discuss which side we're on, but for now at least act like you want to join their cause in order to regain your freedom.
Looking for something on the black market? Say no more.
('you' gender can vary)Sounds like you've given this quite some thought.
Allow me to interject. While I'm sure our dear Boron is curious as to what methods were used to stabilise such an anomaly, I believe it is in our interests to return it to its natural state.
(addressing male)And how do you suggest we fix it?
I'd advise against it. It's a slippery slope.
I find certain aspects of that game rather offensive.
This sounds awfully illegal, even for me.
Look at that thing! It's not even finished and you can see it'll put up quite a fight.
I don't suggest this lightly, but perhaps this is a valuable target to board. I certainly doubt it'll be easy.
Without those blueprints, the full potential of that ship will never be realised.
I'll see if I can find some info to point us in the right direction.
Yeah, it looks like we've got a visitor going about their business in our neighbourhood.
I'm not quite sure what this ship is trying to achieve here.
You might want to take a closer look at that one for a quick threat assessment.
I hate to bug you but, his excitement about looking at some fog aside, Boso seems to be unreasonably nervous about this visitor.
You might want to prioritise looking into this ship.
It's rather unlikely that they followed us here for the view.
Boso, would you happen to know why they would be following the station?
OK, well, that is very bad.
Let's try and resolve this in a way which doesn't lead to us being evicted.
You'd better deal with this sooner rather than later, before they get ideas about taking the station back.
Will they be able to use those traces?
You had better keep up appearances so as to not arouse suspicion, and if Boso has it under control, all the better.
What is it exactly that they're trying to achieve?
Yeah, we all wonder about that.
Let's go rescue the assistant.(female assistant)
This Paranid has been preparing a Torus wreckage exploration!
The Terrans have always been technologically ahead of the other civilisations.
There could be a wealth of interesting tech to salvage in this old chunk of a Terran station!
That's good for us, otherwise they wouldn't have much use for you, and we wouldn't be allowed a peek into this restricted piece of history.
Let's keep going and see if we can salvage something for ourselves.
I did hope that we'd dig up something more useful to us space-faring folks out here.
Nonetheless, it will certainly prove useful in our shaping of the Gate network.
(urgently)There's more to this than meets the eye!
(proud)Allow me to introduce myself: Dal Busta, political analyst, private tutor and bon vivant extraordinaire.
(musing about)Look, if you want these two factions at each others' throats right this instant, who am I to judge?
(musing about)Nobody likes pirates, and helping the Terrans wipe out the Yaki would certainly put an end to their shenanigans.
(musing about, then becoming serious again)All it will take is for someone to inform your precious Mission Command about this dire threat... but what if you tell them the exact opposite?
No Yaki threat, no Terran military response, no fuel for the Yaki hard-liners. It all unravels and the Yaki are back to square one.
Who knows, they might even end up needing some outside help with their Xenon problem.
(mischievous)I'll leave you two alone with your thoughts.
(eager; interjects)No, no, no! I respect your compassion, dear Boso, but this is a matter far beyond ethical considerations.

(addressing the player)You, my friend, have to ask yourself: Will your actions cause a great loss of military equipment? Could you potentially profit from that loss? And, most importantly, would you get away with it?
(smug)If I may be so bold, the answer to all of those questions is obviously a resounding "yes".
(dead serious)You've made your choice and he's made his.
(dead serious)Show him the consequences of crossing you.
The most obvious thing to do would be to coordinate your own attack against the Terran Protectorate with the surge in Xenon activity.
You could, however, also go in an entirely different direction. After all, without the Xenon around, these Yaki will be an easy target for expansion.
Or, if you're altruistically inclined, you could take that opportunity to destroy the Xenon stations in the system while their defenders are abroad.
As I said, there are many ways you could profit from this. The choice is yours.
I just had a tremendously refreshing conversation with a representative(female representative) of the Yaki, and I might have dug up another opportunity for you.
It's really just a side project. Something small to give you an objective when you find yourself bored.
If everything goes well, we could enable the Yaki to trade with their neighbours, and create a new market for your goods in this part of the Gate network.
All it would take is... the elimination of the entire Xenon presence in their system.
(calming, raised hands)Now, don't look at me like that. It's just a proposal, OK?
And before you ask: There won't be a reward. At least, not cash on the spot.
I just thought that if you're conducting military operations in this area of the Gate network anyway, you might as well get yourself another trade partner in return for your efforts.
All right, that's it. Have a good one. Dal out.
Ah, yes, that project. Time to give it a go?
Well, well, well. Mission successful, I'd say.
With the Xenon gone, the Yaki won't have to fear for their lives any more, but they also can't rely on the machines' protection.
I hope your traders are already waiting in the wings. Let's make the most of this!
(Slightly worried, small pause between sentences)It's Dal. We need to talk.
Someone just contacted me. Said she was a mutual friend.
(Confused)Have you been freelancing for the Terran High Command without keeping me in the loop?
(Brushing aside the previous question)Well, it doesn't really matter now. I suppose we all have our secrets.
The contact said she wanted to meet to get the ball rolling on a "covert operation", but she refused to discuss the details over the comms.
OK. I'm sending you the details.
Best not keep someone like her waiting for too long.
Ah, that's all right. If you feel like picking this up later, you can approach Delilah at the Special Operations Command Centre directly.
I assume you'll want some information about the political landscape you're about to get entangled with:
The Antigone Republic is a sovereign state, which only recently established itself during the shutdown.
Their capital is Antigone Memorial, a system which became disconnected from the central Argon government and subsequently seceded from the Federation.
When the Jump Gates began functioning again, the Republic expanded and claimed another handful of newly discovered systems before re-establishing contact with the Argon.
Naturally, things were tense for a while, but it's since been sorted out.
With that in mind, the Terran Secret Service's angle makes sense.
Due to their close ties, the Antigone Republic likely has access to all sorts of Argon communications, but they aren't under strict Argon supervision.
If you factor in the inevitable dose of human greed, it's not a giant leap to expect that confidential information will leak eventually.
(Worried)Still, I can't shake the feeling that there is more to this than just bribing some government worker for intel.
Best keep your wits about you.
Wait, why would Argon forces be stopping you in particular?
(Worried)This is not good. Stay on your toes.
(Very worried)They aren't buying your story. This is bad.
Slip away while the Argon patrol is distracted!
We're lucky the pirates attacked when they did, but I wonder why they would operate this far into well-guarded Antigone territory.
I suppose it matches the reports about the increase in their activity putting pressure on the Federation.
This is the wrong deployable. We need an Advanced Satellite(see {20201,20401}) to make the connection.
The satellite connected to the Secret Service.
Now, let's see this Saman Red.
Before you try to bribe him, perhaps you should sound him out on some pertinent topics.
(Urgent tone, interrupts conversation)Woah, hold up a minute there, partner!
The satellite has intercepted some encrypted communications between this office and the Argon Counterespionage department.
It took me some time to make sense of what I have here, but this is definitely some sort of sting.
(Worried tone)This guy isn't looking to sell intelligence; he wants to catch Terran interference!
(Panicked tone)We messed up! Abort this operation!
(Relieved)Oh, that was too close for comfort. I think it is best if we don't stick around!
It appears the station you were meant to meet the contact at just got destroyed.
The operation is still on; I'm sending the updated information.
(As if he almost forgot)Oh, by the way, make sure to grab an Advanced Satellite(see {20201,20401}) on the way.
From the look of this Terran briefing, you will need it later!
(Angry)The Protectorate suspected something was off about this!
(angry)They were using us as a proxy, knowing that nothing tangible could be traced back to them!
These Security Decryption Systems are quite rare.
Sometimes you can find them in the wreckage of destroyed ships, or you can craft one yourself, if you've got the right resources.
To craft one, you will need five AGI Heuristic Cores(see {20201,16501}), a Decryption Module(see {20201,10101}), and an Interface Unit(see {20201,11101}).
To craft one, you will need specific materials. I've sent you a list so that you can refer to it when you need it.
Be careful, though. Most factions don't really tolerate people using this kind of hacking equipment, so don't let yourself get caught with one of them.
(Weary)From what we've seen so far, we shouldn't expect our Terran friends to have our backs out here.
(Slightly worried)You know, the Argon Federation is careful about disclosing that relay station's location for a reason.
The Sandwell Archives hold critical information on Argon tech, message logs, payroll information, business transactions, and the like.
The fact that those servers are stationed in Republic space has been responsible for heated political stand-offs on more than one occasion.
Access to the Archives isn't being held to ransom, exactly, but the Antigone Republic guaranteeing its security and data integrity is a powerful incentive for peaceful co-existence.

Should the Terrans manage to breach Antigone security, not only could the obtained intel be used to weaken the Argon, but the political fallout resulting from a leak could potentially be even more damaging.
The terminal you're looking for should be located in the Security Office.
I can see the repair request logged in their internal system, but in order to get it to actually register as a job offer, we'll have to force their hand.
(Some urgency)First, get out of here before someone spots you.
Then, create a signal for one of their repair teams to find.
That leak will get them to notice the job offer.
You hacked into the wrong interface. Look for the repair terminal.
You ran out of Security Bypass Systems. You'll need another one to finish the hack.
(Casually, as if Dal almost forgot to tell the player)Oh, and make sure there's no Station Security around!
You'd be torn apart in your flimsy spacesuit.
We don't want to damage the station's hull, just breach their systems.
You'd better fall back while I finish things up.
We still need to work on finding that relay station.
Terrans are not known for their endless patience.
The station you were meant to hack into has been destroyed.
I'm sending you another suitable target now.
Looks like they're heading for the leak.
The database just confirmed that they accepted the repair request.
Follow them from a distance and they will lead us right to the station in question.
(Urgent)Woah, back off! If you spook them, this will all have been for nothing!
(Urgent)Looks like you spooked them. Let's get out of here.
(Urgent)If we get too far away, we'll lose them!
Deal with them, or shake them off, but do it quick! We can't afford to lose the Maintenance Vessel!
Looks like the Maintenance Vessel just dropped a satellite.
Best steer clear. You wouldn't want to end up on their radar.
(Urgent)Put some distance between you and the satellite!
Looks like we won't be able to just waltz right in and snoop around.
(Admiring)That's a lot of military ships they're keeping at the ready here.
Supplying the Scale Plate Pact with weapons and ships makes perfect sense, if you want to destabilise the Argon Federation.
I'm just having a hard time adjusting to the fact that we're in league with these people.
(getting worked up again in the second half)I realise that we need to leave personal grievances behind to play at this level, but still, these cutthroats tried to kill me!
(Calmer)Hard to get over that, you know?
(Resigned)Well, at least it seems like the Scale Plate Pact still thinks I'm dead.
The station we were supposed to supply has been destroyed.
(Congratulatory)Being the entrepreneur that you are, you already own a station producing these goods in Argon space.
Construction of your station in Argon space has just completed.
(Admiring)Not only that, but you've been undercutting Argon prices all along. Not bad!
Now you just have to sell your wares cheaper than the competition.
The market analysis report we received from the Terran Operatives turned out to be accurate.
We're already registering an increase in sales, and the Federation will be forced to adjust their prices downwards if they want to stay competitive.
That's one task crossed off. Now, let's see about the other one.
Working with the Scale Plate Pact still doesn't sit right with me.
Let me get in touch with some people.
I will see if I can quietly establish contact with the Antigone Republic, just in case.
You keep going with this. I just want to make sure we keep all our options open.
OK, I let them know we're in position.
Here come the Scale Plate Pact ships.
They are attacking! That's our cue!
Looks like they're on high alert. They must know something is up.
We'll have to wait for the attack before we can try to slip through.
(Slightly relieved)Good. We made it this far!
It seems the marines really did clear out.
Get moving, though. Our associates won't be able to sustain an attack this intense for much longer.
(Admiringly, heavy emphasis on "lot")Oh, that's a lot of data.
Good work. Now, let's get out of here before anyone sees us.
(Surprised)Our breach did raise some red flags after all.
(Worried)Guards are on their way to intercept us.
(Urgent)Better floor it! Suffice to say, they really mustn't catch us now!
Before you hand over everything that we've just lifted from those servers, the two of us need to sit down together, too.
(Very serious tone)There are a few things I want to run by you. In person.
While you were getting here, I reviewed all our options.
This is a political minefield we've got ourselves involved in here, and I felt we needed a complete picture.
We could hand over the intelligence to the Terran High Command. After all, we were contracted by them.
Alternatively, we could turn to the Antigone Republic, let them know what has happened, and return the intel lifted from their servers as evidence.
Finally, I could destroy the information we pulled off those servers. We back out and pretend this whole mess never happened.
We adhere to the initial plan.
You meet with Delilah, and you turn over all of the intel to her.
The Terran Protectorate gains their leverage and we get paid.
From what I have gathered they'll use the data to sow distrust between the Argon Federation and the Antigone Republic.
The manufactured tension would lead to a complete cessation of trade between the two factions, but the Terran Protectorate won't use this intelligence to escalate the situation.
The Terrans' first priority is still the Xenon, so this leverage is more like long-term insurance to keep their rivals weak.
We contact Saman Red, the Antigone Republic official.
He is already involved in investigating the Protectorate, so all we need to do is hand over the evidence of Terran involvement.
The Terran Protectorate won't be happy, but I think I can twist this so that they won't trace the leak back to us.
The Antigone Republic and the Argon Federation will remain close allies.
But, should Saman go public with this, I can't imagine the Argon Federation taking such Terran interference lightly.
There's a very good chance these tensions will escalate into open war.
Some would argue it's the right thing to do, but we wouldn't get paid for our work, and the ensuing open conflict would be unpredictable and result in many lost lives.
The Terrans don't know for certain that we managed to access the servers, just that we docked at the station.
All we have to do is tell them we didn't get anything from the servers, and quietly erase all the data we did get our hands on.
Sure, we won't get paid, and the Terrans will probably just hire someone else to do their dirty work, but we come out clean.
More importantly, the relations between factions won't change, for better or for worse. Business as usual.
(Anxiously awaiting decision)So, what are we going to do?
Just go through with the final debriefing.
(Worried)I hope you made the right choice.
You'll need to meet with Saman Red, then.
While you get over there, I will call and fill him in.
I'll tell the Terrans that their Sandwell Archive Pass didn't manage to pull off any info.
(Nervous and worried)Hold on for dear life! We're about to blow this whole thing wide open.
Let me take these files off your hands.
(Slightly relieved)You know, for what it's worth, I think this might have been for the best.
(Slightly worried)Nevertheless, perhaps it would be wise to watch your back for a bit. You never know.
(Slightly mournful)Target eliminated. The scanners are not picking up any signs of life.
(Moody)This whole mess just goes to show that it doesn't pay to be too curious...
A whole lot of Argon data just leaked, and it looks like everyone blames the Antigone Republic.
Things are moving faster than expected. Relations between the Antigone Republic and the Argon are deteriorating rapidly.
I'm sure the Terran Protectorate is gleefully watching from the sidelines as both states grow weaker.
The Argon Federation will never know who is truly responsible.
(Tense)I'm picking up several Scale Plate ships heading straight towards us.
Looks like the Terrans didn't trust us to clean this up right.
You need to shoot those guys down to make sure Saman gets the time he needs for his broadcast.
Plus, if they report back to the Terran Secret Service, they'll connect us to Saman.
We still need to cover our backs. Make sure this Scale Plate scum can't rat us out!
From what I'm able to pick up from Argon communications, it seems like Saman still managed to finish his broadcast.
(Mourning, admiring)Instead of abandoning his broadcast and getting himself to safety, he chose to stand by his convictions.
The Argon Federation is mobilising their fleets.
It seems like this incident was the spark that ignited the powder keg.
There should be plenty of business opportunities here, for anyone shrewd enough to seize the moment...
(Curious)How are things going? If we don't make sure we're covered on this Terran business, it will come back to bite us in the bastu.
(2/3)The real question is, what is stopping us from relieving them of their cargo right here, right now?
(3a/3)Sure, we got an arrangement with Gride, but these guys don't seem to be part of the same crew as her, if you know what I'm saying.(mischievous, talking to player)

(3b/3)With Gride gone, Buccaneer leadership is already in a shambles. Time to take out the trash!(gung-ho, talking to player, "Gride" refers to the female character "Gride Orrian", same as {30220,101}, "Buccaneer" refers to the faction "Duke's Buccaneers", same as {20203,2401})

(3c/3)Our good friend, the Duke, might take offence if he learns about it, but who says that he has to? He seems rather busy with taking over the world.(talking to player, give your best megalomaniac impression when saying "taking over the world")
(1/4)Uh, yes, supremely evil, of course.(a bit perplexed)
(2/4)Well, you heard the Boron. Consider whether taking these wares into your custody would be a profitable... I mean, the morally right thing to do.(talking to player)

(3a/4)This seems to be an independent branch of the Buccaneers, so I'm sure that Gride would turn a blind eye to whatever you're about to do.(lowered voice, talking to player, "Buccaneers" refers to the faction "Duke's Buccaneers", same as {20203,2401}, "Gride" refers to the character "Gride Orrian", same as {30220,101})
(3b/4)I'm fairly sure that this stash is just one of their many contingency plans, though. You know how they are.(lowered voice, talking to player)
(3c/4)Remember that whatever you do here will reflect on your standing with the Duke's faction as a whole, so plan accordingly.(lowered voice, talking to player)
(4/4)In case you're wondering, all the goodies are piled up in the storage modules. Cracking them will require some serious firepower.(talking to player)
Partner, I've got the feeling you have just been hustled.
(1/2)These guys might not be the smartest, but going to great lengths obfuscating that there's two of them sure shows they have some savvy.

(1/3)Sure, if you seize this opportunity then you could help the people of Avarice by offering Protectyon at a significantly lower price but, if you really wanted to, you could also keep the price up to increase your own profits.(stress on the 'really', "Avarice" same as {20005,9033})
(2/3)Now, I am not saying you should! I'm just saying...
Nonsense! You should never pass up an opportunity to gain such insight into this place's socio-economic structure!
Besides, in a system owned by the Syndicate, who is the real criminal?
Wildcard, eh? Now we're getting somewhere!(dal and boso, Wildcard is a new nickname the player just earned)
It sure will! If we get our hands on this, we'll have a real edge in a competitive market.(dal and boso)
The fewer people that know about this, the greater our advantage!(dal and boso)
However, why would the Ministry Science Division work on concealment rather than detection?(dal and boso)
Really makes you wonder.(dal and boso)
Not the most exciting surprise. But preferable to the excitement of an unexpected Xenon enclave, I suppose.(somewhere between matter of fact and casual)
(1/2)Indeed. The Royal Steward seems somewhat overwhelmed by the news.
(2/2)Maybe it's a good idea to just listen to him. Understanding his fears might help calm them.
I imagine that there might yet be other opportunities arising from establishing productive ties with royalty.
(1/4)I am certainly very glad to see that our friends are doing well.
(2/4)It is admirable how the Provinces returned to the Queendom without any resistance.
(3/4)Though... I cannot help also feeling a little sad.
(4/4)Instability gives people like us an edge. I don't think there is much to work with here.
Royal diplomacy! I am quite eager to find out what the Queendom is trying to achieve with its restored place in the Commonwealth.
That's strange. Why would the Boron emissary corps be charged with food service to Boso?(Pause before and after "food service")
This guy! I knew this was a ridiculous mission!
With your permission, then, we can get back to deciphering the Queendom agenda.
(1/3)That is an interesting arms deal.(emphasis on "IS")
(2/3)It's possible that they want to support the Free League as they claim. But it's just as plausible that the Boron military is afraid of having fallen behind during the isolation.
(3/3)They might just want a live-fire field test of their military hardware, before they find themselves in a real conflict.
(1/2)Our good old Paranid friends; always suspicious.
(2/2)This is just a diplomatic wrinkle in an otherwise smooth path to business as usual. Nothing to learn here.
(2/4)Emotional breakdown? If you ask me, some of these Boron are just a little bit too soft.
(3/4)Damp-lipped aquatics aren't necessarily going to have the mental toughness for the territories beyond their cosy Queendom.
(1/2)Typical bleeding-heart Boron. They need to be careful about sponsoring covert missions in other people's territories.
(2/2)Triggering a diplomatic incident might be awkward. But there's also a chance that other powers might see this as a way to manipulate the Queen.
If you want to save the credits and still avoid trouble, consider building far from core space, where your construction is less likely to be detected.
OK, so the Queendom is open for business! That should draw some Teladi attention.
(1/2)Obviously there's a hidden agenda here. The Boron don't seem to have been in a real fight for decades. The military must be itching to see how they measure up alongside the hardened Argon fleet.
(2/2)If the joint exercises shed light on a disadvantage, the Argon treaty may buy the Queendom some time to remedy that before facing a major attack.
Tragic as it is, it remains business as usual. Nothing to learn here.
Good luck with that. But I don't think there is much for me to learn. I'll dive right back into evaluating the capabilities of the Boron military, before anyone else puts an analysis on the market.
My sources have informed me that one of the local syndicate leaders has a base on a confiscated ship, which is residing in a scrapyard.
This must be it...(referencing the XL battleship)
It was confiscated from the Riptide Rakers because of the danger it posed; it could be retrofitted into a battleworthy cruiser.
I wonder why the Syndicate didn't make the effort to mount those weapons themselves.
Just imagine it being fully armed, it would be of unmatched firepower; a real game changer.
Hey there, nice place you have. This will be very suitable for my work.
I already checked, and no there aren't.
The name's Dal. Nice to meet you.
I'll go get the rest of my things.
I find the sound of your tank helps me concentrate.
Yes, I'm on it...(reply to Boso asking about Dal's scheming)
I would recommend going along with him until we know more.
A word about Sobert: I don't know what he is up to yet, but he is not a diplomat.
If they are, they're potentially very valuable.
These documents might just be from before The Dark.
I recommend making sure it gets delivered to the AF, they're the best candidate to keep the lid on it until it expires.
This Unbihexium situation is on an entirely different scale from what we're typically dealing with; it's on an extinction-level spectrum.
I can't quite put my finger on it, but I don't think that Teladi is a Health & Safety officer. Let's keep an eye on him.
Congratulations on your new ship. However, be aware that it most certainly comes with strings attached.
I wouldn't be surprised if Sobert got back to you with a request soon. In fact, I'd be surprised if he didn't.
But that's not a bad thing - it broadens your opportunities!
Hey, partner! Now that you've dipped your toe into foreign affairs, you may wish to consider hiring specially trained agents who offer their services at major stations.
Naturally, after all this time in the business, I've come to rely on a few trusted providers. One of them has recently reached out to me and I'd like to recommend their services.
Excellent. I've relied on this agent's services for quite some time and have never been disappointed.
This will increase the chances of your success.
Well now - you still manage to surprise me occasionally!
I haven't had much experience with the agent you just commissioned, but I trust your judgement.
Just remember: staying vigilant is paramount.
Hello! I've been meaning to talk to you about a scheme I've been poring over for a while... one that'll require hiring an agent.
I see you've already started making connections on your own. Good!
First, you'll need to assign a ship that is currently docked at your headquarters to the agent.
Since this is the first time you've hired an agent, I've taken the freedom to arrange such a ship for your convenience!
Not everything can be solved by military intervention. Some issues require subtle coercion, economic manipulation, or other covert manoeuvres.
Always maintain plausible deniability - which is why you hire agents to handle this delicate work!
Of course, many of these operations require some amount of influence to succeed.
Think of it as a shadow currency - and like any currency, you need to start building your reserves.
Time to cultivate some influence and establish yourself as someone worth knowing!
Alright! Your agent has completed the mission and returned to base. The operation went smoothly and boosted your influence considerably.
This opens up even more sophisticated operations - check out what's now become available!
You'll notice that these operations require your agents to be either skilled negotiators or outright spies. While espionage is riskier, it's less costly and offers greater rewards.
As your agents take on more missions, they'll gain experience and improve their success rates.
You don't have to limit yourself to hiring just one agent - different objectives may require different skill sets!
If you can provide accommodation, you can hire new personnel into your service.
Don't hesitate to ask for recommendations on suitable agents.
You know, one shouldn't judge a book by its cover - but let's be honest, it happens all the time!
Use that to your advantage and endow your agents with high-value, high-prestige ships.
You will find that this expedites your objectives substantially!
Hello partner. You're gaining influence and are starting to get noticed!
This might be a good time to carefully begin interfering with the relations between foreign factions.
It didn't escape my attention that you've been proactively manipulating factions for some time! But have you heard of Protocol Null?
It allows your agents to do their work independently, creating a constantly shifting political landscape.
If you like, we could ask Boso Ta to cook up a research plan. Let me know!
Hello. The Protocol Null research has concluded - congratulations! Now you can send an agent to put it into action.
And don't worry, partner - if things start getting out of hand, you can always pull the plug.
Yeah, I've got a lead on a promising new agent. Sending the intel your way now.
I'm sorry, everyone is maintaining a low profile. I don't have any new leads yet.

page.title: Argon NPC Male 36 / Flight Attendant
page.descr: Lines for Argon NPC Male 36 / Flight Attendant- Onboarding

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 22 / Segaris diplomat
page.descr: Lines for Segaris Faction Diplomat
page.t: (Accepting invitation)The Segaris Pioneers gladly accept your invitation. I will arrive at your embassy shortly.
(Diplomat Arrival Confirmation)I have arrived at your embassy.
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)We had hoped that we'd found an ally in you...
(Player requests military support)We are prepared to offer you military support soon.
(Faction military support has ended)I'm afraid that we will have to withdraw our military support for the time being.
(Promotion ceremony - intro)Thank you for making the time to come and see me in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)Many among us have been watching your work with great interest, and wanted to reward you for it.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)We're happy that you've continued to work alongside us, and we wanted to reward you for your continued aid in these hard times.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)As such, I'm pleased to present you with a new rank as a token of our appreciation.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)It is a real honour to present you with this rank, as a demonstration that we consider you to be one of us.
(Promotion ceremony)Of course, we will also reward you with benefits.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)These benefits are linked to your rank, so they will be lost should you turn against us.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)But given how you have helped us out in the past, I do not see that being a real worry.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)I hope you find these rewards fitting to the work you've done, and that you are able to make the most of them.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)Oh, and expect some of our organisations to reach out to you for help in the near future.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, we really appreciate what you have done for us so far.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We look forward to working with you more in the future.

(Diplomat Arrival Confirmation)I have arrived at your embassy, and am looking forward to doing business with you.
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)You will regret crossing the Vigor Syndicate!
(Player requests military support)We will dispatch a few raiders to provide military support.
(Faction military support has ended)While aiding you in combat has been a welcome diversion, our forces need to get back to what really matters...
(Promotion ceremony - intro)Thank you for making the time to come and see me in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)Many among us have been watching your work with great interest, and wanted to reward you for it.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)We're happy that you've continued to work alongside us, and we wanted to reward you for your continued aid in these hard times.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)As such, I'm pleased to present you with a new rank as a token of our appreciation.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)It is a real honour to present you with this rank, as a demonstration that we consider you to be one of us.
(Promotion ceremony)Of course, we will also reward you with benefits.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)These benefits are linked to your rank, so they will be lost should you turn against us.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)But given how you have helped us out in the past, I do not see that being a real worry.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)I hope you find these rewards fitting to the work you've done, and that you are able to make the most of them.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)Oh, and expect some of our organisations to reach out to you for help in the near future.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, we really appreciate what you have done for us so far.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We look forward to working with you more in the future.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 24 / Riptide diplomat
page.descr: Lines for Riptide Faction Diplomat
page.t: (Accepting invitation)Our people are honoured by your invitation. I will be aboard your station shortly.
(Diplomat Arrival Confirmation)I've made it to your embassy.
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)We cannot work alongside someone who treats us so poorly.
(Player requests military support)We'll see what sort of military support we can muster.
(Faction military support has ended)There is nothing else the Riptide Rakers can do for you at the moment, militarily speaking.
(Promotion ceremony - intro)Thank you for making the time to come and see me in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)Many among us have been watching your work with great interest, and wanted to reward you for it.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)We're happy that you've continued to work alongside us, and we wanted to reward you for your continued aid in these hard times.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)As such, I'm pleased to present you with a new rank as a token of our appreciation.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)It is a real honour to present you with this rank, as a demonstration that we consider you to be one of us.
(Promotion ceremony)Of course, we will also reward you with benefits.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)These benefits are linked to your rank, so they will be lost should you turn against us.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)But given how you have helped us out in the past, I do not see that being a real worry.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)I hope you find these rewards fitting to the work you've done, and that you are able to make the most of them.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)Oh, and expect some of our organisations to reach out to you for help in the near future.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, we really appreciate what you have done for us so far.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We look forward to working with you more in the future.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 27 / Hatikvah diplomat
page.descr: Lines for Hatikvah Faction Diplomat
page.t: (Accepting invitation)The Hatikvah Free League welcomes the opportunity to widen our diplomatic circle. I'll be arriving shortly.
(Diplomat Arrival Confirmation)I have arrived at your embassy.
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)We are no longer willing to deal with unreliable partners!
(Player requests military support)You are asking us for military support? I'll see what support our trading league can muster.
(Faction military support has ended)The Hatikvah Free League needs to withdraw its military support for the time being.
(Promotion ceremony - intro)It's good that you came in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)Hatikvah have been watching your exploits with great interest. They're certainly something worthy of recognition.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)We're happy that you've continued to walk alongside us, and we would like to reward you for your efforts.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)I'm pleased to present you with a new rank within the Hatikvah Free League.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)It's an honour to present you with a new rank within the Hatikvah Free League.
(Promotion ceremony)Of course, this rank comes with a number of benefits.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)These benefits are tied to the rank, so if you lose the rank, the benefits go too.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)But with your record, I'm sure we don't have to worry about that.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)These rewards befit the work you've done. Make the most of them.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)Oh, and you may also find that certain organisations within our community now have interest in you joining their ranks.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, I thank you for your efforts.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We look forward to your future accomplishments.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 28 / Yaki diplomat
page.descr: Lines for Yaki Faction Diplomat
page.t: (Accepting invitation)You want us to join your diplomatic network? Why, of course we accept! Expect my arrival shortly!
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)We should have stuck to machines for allies. More predictable.
(Player requests military support)We'll do our best to provide military support.
(Faction military support has ended)Our military support must come to an end... for now.
(Promotion ceremony - intro)I appreciate you coming in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)It's good to know that someone out there has not turned their back on us.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)Your support has helped our people tremendously with surviving in these harsh circumstances.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)As a token of our gratitude, I want to present you with a new rank.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)I am honoured to pay you back in small part, by welcoming you into the fold with this new rank.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)Should you betray our trust, we will not hesitate to take these benefits from you.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)But since you were one of the few people to actually give us a chance, I doubt you would do that.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)I hope these rewards adequately convey our appreciation for all you have done so far.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)Oh, and some Yaki groups have expressed interest in hiring your services, so do not be surprised if they contact you.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, we thank you for helping us in these difficult times.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)I am curious to see what challenges you will help us overcome in the future.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 21 / Lissa Ygon
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 21 / Timelines Hub character Lissa Ygon
page.t: Sorry, I am busy right now.
Looks like you're having a bad day.
Not quite. It's an impedance bubble. Kind of complicated to explain.
Look, we don't have much time. You're basically stuffed. Flaming death the moment this bubble collapses.
I can get you out, but you'll never have this life again.
Everything will change and I can't promise that you'll like all the changes.
Oh this is useless. I've gotta go.
Welcome to the Facility! How do you feel?
Don't push yourself. Take your time. I'm Lissa. This is Tammancktall and MD... uh... Mission Director.
Where isn't really the issue. It's good you're sitting down. You're in the year 2042.
Not exactly. It's complicated. The high-ups know the details, but to be honest, I don't really get it myself.
Yes. I told you that your past life is now left behind. You will never go back.
But you're here for a reason. The same reason as the rest of us.
This is the Mission Hall, where we execute missions on behalf of the high-ups.
Harper. The missions are not time travel, but they seem like time travel.
And we don't get to leave the Facility, except on missions.
I know it's not ideal, but it beats flaming death, right?
Great. Just relax and recover. Explore the Facility.
There's a room designated for you.
Let me know when you're ready for your first mission.
Hi Donel. Have you come to start your first mission?
Great! Well this is the mission interface.
Hop in, and once connection is established, the Mission Director will be able to guide you through the next step.
Well, let me know when you're ready.
Congratulations! You've completed your first mission!
Oh shush, MD. This one is just fine.
Well, you're not a newbie any more, Harper.
The missions are the most fun there is to have around here, so do complete as many as possible.
Are you OK? Try not to move too quickly.
I'm sorry to say "where" isn't the biggest issue. You're in the year 2042.
Just rest a moment. I'm Lissa Ygon.
This is Tammancktall, Mission Director, and over there is Harper Donel.
You were in a bit of a situation and we got you out of there. But there was only one way to do that - and that was to bring you here.
Your old life is gone, I'm afraid. But this place isn't so bad.
Just let things sink in for a bit. You can talk to us at any time.
You're not dreaming, Kaori. The ball is the Mission Director.
Erm... That's kind of the gist of what we do.
Harper. Do you have a minute?
I'm worried. I think the Facility is driving people apart.
Tammancktall and Kaori seem to be forming gangs. I don't know where all this will end.
These "Quettanauts", who seem to think this is all a game.
And then there's Tammancktall, who's convinced we're agents of the gods or something.
And I don't know what Sae t'Plt is up to. But she seems to stay away from everyone.
I really have no idea, Harper. But it seems like a good idea to just make the best of it.
You're a good listener, Harper. I'm glad you're here. I don't know what I'd do without you.
Hey Harper. This place isn't so bad when you get used to it.
The missions are everything to me.
I don't exactly know how, but I really think we're doing something worthwhile here.
Pa, Sae, this place is too small for your quarrels.
Ladies! Can we just take a breath?
None of this helps to create a work and living space where everyone feels safe.
I don't think it's fair to describe the situation like that.
We all chose to be here.
OK, OK. I'll talk to MD. But at least you two have found something you agree on.
We never existed? No-one we ever loved existed?
Nothing that ever happened to us was real?
This is real at least. I'm glad you're here, Harper.
Where did you hear that name?
No - I can't. We agreed. We don't talk about Mitsuno.
And don't raise this with anyone else. Especially MD.
Hi Harper. I hope your missions are going well.
Hello Harper. I have some admin to do. I'll get back to you later.
What would MD say? Missions, missions, missions!
I have. That is a weird one.
There's so few of us here. It's strange to think someone we know is vandalising things.
I suppose we're all Quettanauts now.
Kaori's becoming a real leader here. People are looking up to her.
It's kind of satisfying to think we're just playing a game - however important it is.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 22 / Mitsuno Sheppard
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 22 / Timelines Hub character Mitsuno Sheppard
page.t: Sorry, I am busy right now.
Sae t'Plt, Harper Donel, it's good to meet you at last.
I'm Mitsuno Sheppard. I've been watching you both.
Are you ready to get out of here?
I was the first recruit on this branch of the Facility, just a few months ago.
It seemed obvious to me from the get-go that we're just lab rats here.
So I explored the space, found a hiding place and kitted it out.
As you can see, I've got a bit of a workshop going on.
And I've cobbled together a mission interface, without any of the restrictions you have in the Mission Hall.
This is where I have been hacking the mission comms from. So far I have been able to do this without detection.
I've been looking for the right recruits. People who aren't swallowing the propaganda and who want to go home.
You two seem to be the best of the bunch.
The portal MD uses in the Mission Hall; that's got to be the way to the Facility's Command Centre.
We get into the Command Centre, take it over, and use whatever powers this place has to send us all home.
The Argnu can stay here if they want, but it's time we escaped.
I'm not ready yet, but I'll need help scavenging the items we need to get through the Mission Hall portal.
I should warn you that I have no idea what's on the other side. We have to be prepared for anything.
I don't like widening our circle, but we could use the backup if anything goes wrong.
It depends how long it takes Harper to get what I need.
I'll send you a message using the in-mission comms when I have prepared everything.
Great, you're here. Are you ready?
I have a device for hacking the portal and hopefully anything else we come across.
Get to the Mission Hall, and I'll meet you there. I need to get there without being seen.
When this fires up, move quickly. Keep your eyes open. We don't know what we'll find on the other side.
You lead, Harper. I'll bring up the rear.
Harper, if we need to go back, I'll hack the portal. But for now stay focused. Find the Command Centre.
It's too late to go back. This is our only chance to get out of here. Find the Command Centre.
Mission Director. Do you control the Facility? We're getting out of here.
Damage? You haven't seen how much damage we can cause!
We just want to go home!
Fun? Take us home now, or I'm blowing up the egg.
Thanks for doing this, Harper. I can't really be seen.
The items should be pretty easy to find.
I need a Programmable Field Array, an Interface Unit and... um... a cosmetics kit.
Yes. A cosmetics kit. You should be able to find one in my room. Here's my room pass.
Harper! Do you have the items I need?
Well do have a hunt around. Unless you have any other ideas of how we're going to get into the Command Centre?
Excellent Harper! I have some work to do now.
I'll send a message through your mission comms once the device is ready.
OK, thanks. Do find the rest of what I need, and we can try to get out of this place.
You should be able to find the other items around the facility.
Try the recruit bedrooms. These are the kinds of things that get stuffed in a cupboard in case they come in useful later.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 23 / Kaori Chen
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 23 / Timelines Hub character Kaori Chen
page.t: Sorry, I am busy right now.
That was a trip! Where am I?
OK, this is weird. A talking, floating ball and a three-eyed alien. What did you do to me?
Frag! Real aliens! Are there more?
Creature from another world. I am Kaori Chen of Earth. On behalf of the people of my planet, I welcome you.
Hi, you're Harper, right? I'm so glad you brought me here. I've done five missions already!
And aliens - uh.. I mean "otherworlders" everywhere.
I met the Split lady. She's kinda grumpy, but cool.
Anyway, thanks for bringing me here Harper. Definitely beats 25 years... er, jazuras?... in jail!
Gotta go - more missions to do!
He's super competitive. I hope we recruit more.
Totally settled. And I think I've figured this place out.
I think we're definitely just playing a huge videogame.
Seriously, we get mission ratings and if we die, we just get a new life.
I know, right. And the data they're parsing must be enormous.
And here we are. Quettasurfers in a fully immersive experience.
Yeah - maybe we need a different name. I'll think about it.
You get some pretty hot scores, Harper. You think MD would rack up a leaderboard for us?
Definitely. We use it all the time.
This is Harper Donel, one of our highest ranking competitors.
It's great, isn't it? "Quettanauts. Explorers of the near infinite dataverse in search of action, intrigue and high scores".
I think you're reading too much into this, Tammancktall.
If it's so important, maybe you'd be better off working on your scores.
You can believe whatever you want to believe. I'm not stopping you. But I don't see MD cheering your results.
You do your reverence, Tammancktall. The Quettanauts are just here to win.
No worries, Harper. Catch up with you later.
He's really aiming for high scores.
Oh - and he keeps trying to bet food rations on mission outcomes!
Gotta go now and kick some Teladi tail.
Fragging amazing! I can't believe this place!
I've seen so many otherworlders! Everywhere! I wish I could tell the people of Earth what they're missing!
Have you seen the Boron yet? Slimy!
I had no idea the galaxy was so full of life, industry and activity.
And the ships they are putting me in are fantastic - and non-polluting too!
To be honest, sitting there in a cockpit feels like being in a videogame. But so real!
Better than any videogame I ever played on Earth.
It's wild! Can you believe it?
We're just code snippets brought to life!
I KNEW it was all a game! I didn't realise the lose condition is the heat death of the Universe!
Just aced mission Delta Epsilon 59! Taking a break and then back to the interface!
I just wiped out a whole Kha'ak fleet! Gotta keep this one in my log!
You're in danger of beating my scores, Harper! Great work!
Hey there, stranger. It's good to meet you at last.
Oh that. I gave up trying to stop people calling me that generations ago. I have literally never been fertilised and have zero grandchildren.
Yes I'm very... very old. But, barring kinetic damage, kind of immortal. And you can call me Kaori.
Where to begin... I have to tell you a story.
I thought I was born on Earth, around 900 jazuras ago. But the truth is, I wasn't born at all.
I was made. I was 24 years old on the day I was created.
I woke up in the strangest place. A space rock, housing a mysterious facility.
There were a team of us - synthetic beings - and we were tasked with what seemed like time travel missions.
We were launched into unfamiliar times, to unfamiliar corners of the galaxy. Often in unfamiliar bodies.
Sometimes we executed the same missions again and again. At first, without really knowing why.
Or who we were doing these missions for.
We discovered our masters were the Sohnen. A species of unimaginably advanced technology and intelligence.
But not so hot in the looks department.
What felt like time travel to us, was more like a game.
We were thrust into scenarios, surfing huge amounts of data. Quettabytes of data.
All so the Sohnen could predict, by extrapolation, the future of the galaxy.
Each mission we undertook added to the accuracy of their predictions.
And then... years later... they told us the job was done.
The Sohnen then gave us a choice.
We could either return to the data and live out our lives in what we called "the dream".
Or we could keep our synthetic bodies and exist in the real universe.
Over time, we rescued lost and abandoned spacefarers, and populated Mitsuno's Remembrance.
A peaceful corner of the galaxy, where species can coexist.
Ha! Yes - another gift from the Sohnen. In addition to an immortal synthetic body, the Sohnen gave us teleportation drives.
Just like this ship, the Xperimental Shuttle.
The Sohnen agenda spans the whole universe and all of time.
So they didn't pay attention to the simians evolving on Earth.
Then, out of nowhere, the simians miraculously created a Jump Gate.
I think the opening of the Earth Gate created a margin of error in their predictive algorithms that was intolerable to the Sohnen.
The missions were just a means to bring down that margin of error.
Likewise, Boso Ta. In my very long lifetime I haven't encountered anyone able to decode Sohnen technology. Your work is truly remarkable.
No, I haven't. But I can tell you something about this asteroid of yours.
The asteroid is unmistakable. This is where I was born, and where I worked for the Sohnen for many jazuras.
I like what you've done with the place.
And this is why you're sitting on a priceless trove of Sohnen technology.
Maybe. But I have a request.
My teleportation drive has been out of action for so long.
I need to communicate with the rock to see if it can repair my drive.
May I use your systems to do this?
OK. That was interesting. It seems I'm still useful to the Sohnen after all.
It gave me a mission. I can't say more. But I'll be teleporting out of here any moment now.
This is not the way, Boso. When the Sohnen call, you answer.
Boso Ta, stranger, you have been more than helpful. I won't need a ship where I'm going. Consider the Xperimental Shuttle a gift from me to you.
Oh don't you start calling me grandmother!
This body has never even had a womb!
In fact, please do not call me Grandmother.
Although my drive has been fragged for a long time.
I have been sending out signals with a Sohnen signature, in the hope of detecting a response from Sohnen tech.
If I can get my hands on Sohnen tech, I might be able to fix my teleportation drive.
No problem. Come back when you have time.
Thanks for rescuing Kal. She's a bit feisty, that one.
Sure. Come find me when you want to pick this up again.
Your scientist, Boso, may have the tech I need. You must escort me to him.
But please... take care of my people.
Actually, you might be able to help me with that.
You're an experienced and resourceful explorer. Perhaps you can keep an eye out for any Sohnen tech?
Let me know if you find anything likely. I'll be able to analyse it with my systems.
Of the thousands of Quettanauts, surprisingly few chose reality.
The rest were lost or killed. At least, I haven't heard from any of the lost in a long while.
And of them, I think I'm the last.
This Boso person might be useful to us in finding Sohnen tech.
He seems to have a wealth of scientific knowledge.
Holy frag! I think you've found it!
This station definitely has a Sohnen tech signature.
Please come and get me. I need an escort to this HQ, and there's no-one I trust more than you.
I can't believe I'm finally gonna get my teleportation drive fixed!
I know this place. It definitely has the tech I need.
Holy frag! What happened to this guy?
So I have friends with magic bubbles. Good to know.
If you're going to ignore me, I'd rather you just disappear with your magic bubble.
Now that DOES sound like something I could get behind.
You're not exactly selling this bubble, dude.
You're not exactly selling this bubble, girl.
But I have family. Can I even say goodbye?
I see. Goodbyes are not an option.
Don't sugar coat it, Harper. Tell me how it really is.
You know you're just a stranger with a magic bubble. You're not my best friend.
Honestly. You're kind of shady. I think I'll take my chances with the enemy I know.
This is all a lot to take in so quickly.
Is there anything else I need to know?
Come on, Harper. Let's get out of here. The food sucks anyway.
But you don't really know that, do you Harper?
Ah, frag it! Take me away from this place. We'll figure it out together.
Aren't you a charmer?! Go on then. Beam me up to your time machine.
Look. You need to work on your social skills, but I hope there's room for two in your bubble. I'm in.
Yeah. My mum always told me never to get into time machines with strangers.
Get out of my cell you sociopath, and take your bubble with you.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 25 / Ban Danna
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 25 - Ban Danna
page.t: Kyle Brennan? This is Ban Danna speaking.
You did a great job taking out that Xenon infrastructure.
But unfortunately it won't slow them down much. Your most important task still lies ahead!
The machines have finished the construction of their most advance piece of tech yet.
That is bad news. The M0 is a weapon of mass destruction that can wreak havoc on a planetary scale.
But still, your Xperimental Shuttle makes you the most ideal candidate to face this threat head-on.
Now, first we need you to investigate the situation for us.
But be careful! Expect to be met with some serious resistance.
I'm still in disbelief that you managed to rally all of our allies. Can't have been easy to get everyone on the same page.
Our combined forces are gathering close by.
Even the Split have agreed to a temporary ceasefire with the Queendom of Boron!
Everyone is waiting for your signal.
These Xenon ships are guarding the entry!
You need to take them out!
Well... it is your choice, I guess.
They are taking up pursuit though.
Once you have cleared the way, we shall move in as one fleet.
These systems are absolutely infested with the machines.
I must admit, when you first surfaced in our space, I was sceptical about your intentions.
Stranded in this weird ship prototype that no-one's ever heard of before... Telling tall tales about Earth and riling up the Goner...
I even asked some of our Argon Secret Service officers to run a complete investigation into you, but to my surprise absolutely nothing came up.
So, we had no choice but to take you by your word - and it is a good thing we did!
Your actions have proven your character, and only thanks to your warnings did we manage to face the threat of the Xenon head on.
I am nervous. We have no idea of the true capabilities of this behemoth superweapon.
The fate of all organic life rests in your capable hands.
And there it is! The mother of all Xenon weapons.
Be careful on your approach. Those rotating turrets can rip your ship to shreds... easily!
They have you in their sights!
It's scary, but try approaching it head-on!
Reconnaissance tells us that its turrets have less frontal coverage, and you are much too small to be targeted by its main battery.
But, perhaps stay clear of the main barrel... just in case.
They are trying to protect the M0!
Destroy them before you take out the turrets.
Get back closer to the ship's hull. The turrets are less likely to hit you there.
Great! I have marked several turrets for you, that you will need to take out to be able to move more freely.
Okay, now turn your attention towards those four rotating arms.
They are the obstacle that is keeping our fleet from engaging.
I need you to take them out, quickly!
The Xenon are trying their damnedest to stop you from disabling those final two arms!
The turrets affixed to the rotating arms are absolutely deadly.
Stay out of their line of fire!
M0 defences are down. I repeat: defences are down.
Commonwealth fleet, you are free to engage.
More Xenon forces are approaching our position!
Destroyers, focus fire on the M0!
The shielding is down and the ship is about to overheat!
Kyle, an air vent is exposing a critical weakness...
This is your opportunity! Give it all you've got!
Well done Kyle! Well done everyone!
We will decommission the last remaining machine stragglers after we have properly regrouped.
The M0 seems to correct its course.
Their sacrifice... it cannot be in vain!
Double down! Show them all we've got!
And Kyle... when we are done here I expect to see you at Argon Prime space port.
The first round of Spacefuel is on me!
An entire fleet is approaching your position!
We need to disable this monster! Fast!
You are taking too much fire!
A couple more hits and you are done for!
Kyle, you need to land that shot!
That's the last of them, I hope. Now where's--
Just in time. There's something I want you to see.
Since our arrival, we've been receiving messages like this one.
Your father? It sure sounds like him.
We've been fighting off wave after wave of them. Julian, Saya, Bret, stick together.
The signal is faint, but we're trying to pinpoint his location.
Julian! We've got a lock on Kyle's position!
We've triple-checked it, there's no doubt. He's on that battleship.
Get me details on those destroyers!
Agreed. Julian, we can't help you directly. I need every single ship to deal with those destroyers. The best we can do is draw attention away from you.
Get close to that monstrosity. We think we can teleport him out of there if you hold these precise positions. Can I count on you?
Activating the transporter array. Stay in position or we lose focus.
It's working! We've almost got him! Just a few more--
No no no, we're losing him! Need to...
Damn it! Too late. Signal's lost, he's still on their ship.
Get to a safe distance while we figure out what happened.
Billions of innocent lives would be lost.
We think we know what went wrong. No time for details, I need you to take out the marked targets. They're interfering with the transporter array.
The interference is gone, return to your positions!
Activating transporter array. Signal locked, solid progress.
Julian's right. Stay in position and we'll have him out in time.
That must be what's blocking the transporter! We're about to lose him again!("transporter" refers to teleportation technology)
Get out of there, it's overloading!

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 26 / Calm Competent Crewman
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 26 - Calm Competent Crewman
page.t: (Promotion ceremony - intro)Thanks for taking the time to see me.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)You've been making a bit of an impression here!
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)You continue to impress, my friend!
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)The station reps have decided that a formal recognition is in order.('reps' short for representatives)
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)The station reps have unanimously decided to give you a worthier title.('reps' short for representatives)
(Promotion ceremony)This isn't just a formality, though.
(Promotion ceremony - barter hint 1)You may already have more barter offers in your mission interface.
(Promotion ceremony - ship barter hint)Keep an eye out for ships, specifically.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)I think I've been blathering on long enough.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We really appreciate your help, and hope to see you around.
(Start of greeting)On behalf of the people I represent: (keep space)
Station defences are down, great work.
This is the captain of the Argon destroyer "Harrogate".
We are being overwhelmed! Abandon ship!
They have nothing to meet our firepower!
Target destroyed! Job well done, everybody!
Wing leader, this is Patrol Command.
Our scouts have come across a Xenon capital ship heading towards our territory.
We don't currently have the firepower on hand to stave off that attack, but a fleet is being redeployed as we speak.
You and your team need to buy us time.
Get in there and take out the engines, take out the turrets.
Captain, reports indicate that a blockade is forming.
Captain, reports indicate that a blockade is forming. I'll keep contacts away from you.
I'll help with the transport, Captain.
Passengers delivered. Lifting off for my next run.
Third done. Will keep radio silence for now, Captain.
Captain, blockade up ahead. I'll try to fly through them.
Blockade up ahead. They've received reinforcements.
Damage sustained. This blockade is going to be a problem.
Blockade breached. It looks like they don't want to engage the station's defences.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 24 / Military Ship Captain
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon Female 24 / Military Ship Captain
page.t: Crewman, what do you think you're doing here? I ordered all hands to abandon ship! Go!
I'm quite busy here crewman. Get out of here!
If you want to be useful, go and help the rest of the crew. Put those hotshot skills to use.
Analysis shows substantial damage to critical systems. Total destruction is inevitable.
Further analysis shows that destruction can be delayed.
Engineering, help with repairs at the station. I'll help with the transport.
Passengers delivered. Lifting off for my next run.
Third done. Will keep radio silence for now.
This is our last run. Get on board.
Blockade up ahead. I'll try to fly through them.
Blockade up ahead. They've received reinforcements.
Damage sustained. This blockade is going to be a problem.
Blockade breached. It looks like they don't want to engage the station's defences.
Reports indicate that a blockade is forming.
Reports indicate that a blockade is forming. I'll keep contacts away from you.
Starting operation now. Transporters are undocking.
Protect them while they deliver materials to the auxiliary ship.
Transporters are entering the cloud, stay near them. Sensors indicate Xenon activity. And remember your briefing: travel drive will not work once you are in the cloud.
Transporters are docking. Protect the auxiliary while it extracts the samples.
Extraction complete, auxiliary is moving out.
Holy Order Fleet is detected in the vicinity, be careful, they may be interested in our operation.
The Holy Order ships are entering the cloud, their intentions are unclear. Be ready to intercept if they prove to have ill intentions.
Holy Order bombers are attacking auxiliary, protect the ship at all costs.
Auxiliary is out, we'll take it from here, good job.
A Xenon capital ship showed up on our sensors, and it appeared to go straight for the auxiliary. We're dispatching the bomber wing to take it down, but you'll need to provide some cover for them.
All set. We should be able to cut through the interference with these.
Let's see if this does what the scientists promised...
Guess it does! Let's make sure this reaches the fleet.
Argon station, help is on the way. Hold out until we arrive.
Any freelance commanders in the region? Help us fend off the Paranid. You'll be doing the right thing.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 25 / Seasoned Miner
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon Female 25 / Seasoned Miner in Timelines scenarios
page.t: Bastu! That was our last mining drone!
Just one more quick haul, and we can make it back in time and still hit the quota!
Why did I let them put this brute in my crew...?
That should get us back to base before the next assault.
In a different life, you could have been some kind of racer, Erfmancklest.
Hands on deck, little brother! Eager to leave your mark on this sector?
There's been a rare lull in Xenon activity, so it's now or never!
Hop into your mining ship and lift off, so we can get going.
Don't act all oblivious. I know you're always playing that Flight School game late at night.
To find asteroids that are rich in Ore, you first have to activate Scan Mode.
Fly up to the nearest asteroids, and check if any of them get highlighted in orange.
Once you're close enough, small resource spots will start to appear.
Try lasering one of them, but first make sure you have your mining equipment selected.
... or you can blow it up outright. That works too.
Now attract the asteroid chunks with the container magnet until they're packed in your cargo hold.
Back to the station, so we can store that first haul!
Just try to be a bit conservative with the acceleration, and slow down early enough.
Watch out for the extra mass. Once fully laden, you'll notice that your ship will take significantly longer than normal to come to a standstill.
Thrusters, ship alignment... You know the drill, right?
Sell the minerals to the station to free up cargo space for another haul.
Try to squeeze in another run if you can, before the Xenon come back in force.
Time to tidy up, little brother!
The North Gate reports mounting Xenon activity. You'd better finish up your current run and get to safety.
About as good as I did the first time.
Let's try that again, shall we?
With a bit of practice, you'll be fulfilling your quotas in no time.
Wait a minute. Something's wrong with the gates...
Today's your lucky day, Kit. You get to be in charge of the miners.
As you ramp up your activity, be ready to respond to Kha'ak encounters.
Funanori Station is a real drain on the sector's resources, so the calm periods are growing shorter and shorter.
Kha'ak pressure increasing, and it doesn't look like they've reached their limit.
Collect as many resources as you can. But please... minimise casualties.
Looks like the skies are going to stay inhospitable for a while.
You gave those Kha'ak a real fight, shift 7!
With all these resources, we can stay holed up for a while as we work on Funanori Station.
Play the protector, or jump into a miner yourself if you think you can do better.
But don't forget to give orders to the other ships. They depend on you.
Our schedule has been compressed, little brother, or should I say, Prospector Hammond?
The Xenon are making this phase of the project especially difficult. The Lord Prospector is only allowing seasoned miners like you to leave the hangar.
Don't worry, the front line still holds. This is only a precaution.
Chikkusho, a few Xenon have slipped through our defences!
The situation's only going to get worse. You have to decide whether you want to show off your superior manoeuvres or just wait it out on the dock.
You're uninjured. That's all that matters.
Thank goodness you made it back in one piece!
Those Xenon barely slowed you down!
Gather as much Ore and Silicon as you can, and remember to sell to the refinery stations to make space for another haul.
Your calculations were correct; our scans do indeed identify this as the Nividium asteroid impact site.
Funanori Station is giving us the green light to begin resource extraction.
Please help us identify suitable Nividium asteroids, if you'd be so kind.
If you break them down, the Nagatabi's mining drones will expedite the collection process.
Should you wish to issue direct commands, the entire mining fleet is at your disposal, Sir.
Chikkusho! Pardon me, Sir, but it appears that some of these asteroids contain dormant Kha'ak!
Should you decide to intervene, a fighter ship is available on the Nagatabi's dock, for your convenience.
Now that we've intruded into their territory, Sir, the Kha'ak will only keep on coming.
Once you think that we've collected enough Nividium, do consider pulling out and directing the fleet towards Funanori Station.
More Kha'ak are homing in on our position, Sir.
The project desperately needed these resources...
Thank you for your guidance, Lord Prospector.
We wouldn't have made it without you.
This Nividium effectively ensures the project's success.
The people of Getsu Fune will sail once more!
We're far away from the next allied station, Sir.
If your miners stop working because they're full of cargo, you can make them transfer any mined Nividium to the Nagatabi.

page.title: Mission Argon Female 26 / Nyana Gunne
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon Female 26 / Nyana Gunne
page.t: This is Nyana Gunne from the Truth About Earth Foundation, and we could use some help.
We want to get our research and some of the artefacts we have collected to safety. Will you help us out?
Given the circumstances, I can fully understand. We will try to find a different solution.
Actually, Martinus, there's a small change of plans. I've been asked to join the station administration to help with the coordination of the evacuation. I'll just get on one of the transport ships.
I'm a Gunne, I can't just abandon the people when they need me the most. But don't you worry, I'm sure this isn't the end of our story. Now off you go, make sure our findings reach the masses.
Wonderful, that is great news. Thanks again for your help.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 27 - Martinus Sandas
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 27 - Martinus Sandas
page.t: Martinus Sandas. Pleased to make your acquaintance.
Let me quickly check if I have everything...
Ah yes, we should be good to go.
You can't be serious. We just made it through a wave of Xenon, and lately the attacks are increasing at a worrying rate.
I don't like this, but now is not the time to argue. Just promise me you'll stay safe and get out of here as soon as possible.
I'm aboard your ship, we can leave whenever you're ready.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 28 - Julian Gardna
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 28 - Julian Gardna
page.t: Come on, Saya, after everything he's done for me?
Enough. Bret, it's good you're here.
We lost my old man's trail a few sectors over... I think the Kha'ak took him.
Kha'ak! They're jumping in right on top of us!
Understood. Bret, we've got your back.
Right, looks like our old friend Ban Danna has his hands full.
Bret, your ship looks a little beaten up.
Dock at the Argon One for automatic repairs, once you have a moment of calm.
What do you need us to do?
What's happening? Why'd those lasers stop?
They won't miss again. If they hit the planet...
And the shockwave would destroy everything in this sector, too.
Would explain why they froze when we almost had him.
On our way. You ok, Saya? You took quite a hit.
Ohh, that was way too close.
See that weird glow? It was there the last time we activated the transporter array too.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 29 / Race Announcer
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 29 / Race Announcer
page.t: ... and with that commercial break out of the way, let us all welcome our next contestant!
The winner of the zuran year 579 Core Cracker Olympics...
... breaker of hearts and records, the Debris Devil himself...
... stepping out of the elevator now is none other than ERFMANCKLEST!!!
Even legends can have bad days, folks!
Another solid performance by our resident crowd-pleaser Erfmancklest!
The crowd goes wild! He simply cannot stop setting records!
Is there no end to Paranid ingenuity?
It's going to be pure asteroid blasting today, folks! Leave the rubble or lose the record!
Do you think they're hoping we didn't see that nudge?
There he goes, taking the inside line and, yes, cleanly overtaken.
I'm sure he must be happy with that!
Right here in the beating heart of CEO's Doubt, we're back once more for another adrenaline-fueled race in this year's Nebula Open Cup.(CEO's Doubt like {20005,6033})
Today's thrilling event is proudly brought to you by Swamp Fizz, the refreshing burst of energy to get you through your day.
And would you look at that, it's shaping up to be a stellar day for racing!
The racers are geared up and ready to unleash their ships along this high speed course.
Today we have a new racer, ready to take on the established giants here.
Fantastic to witness the return of so many seasoned racers to the tracks of CEO's Doubt.(CEO's Doubt like {20005,6033})
These long straights really let the racers open up and show what their ships can do.
As the racers come around the station, make sure you give them a wave!
This course was first set up by young Teladi, racing their modified transports. What a long way it's come!
What a race! A true underdog story if ever I saw one!
What an exciting race, a true struggle between great racers.
That finish must have been disappointing for our new racers, better luck next time!
Welcome to race-day excitement at its finest.
Today at the Nebula Open Cup, we're brought to you by Hatibmanckabssit's Togs: your go-to for the slickest threads this side of the schism.
Today we are back again at Cardinal's Domain for what looks to be another thrilling race.(Cardinal's Domain like {20005,3011})
This course has become the stuff of legends, with young daredevils zipping past the station's towers and burning down the lengths of the station.
It's not just a race; it's a showcase of skill, speed and, of course, the ultimate in racing horsepower.
It looks like we have all the racers on the line, ready to show what they've got.
We have Otmancketvahs's Zeus visiting Cardinal's Domain today, giving us a bit of a different course than usual.(Cardinal's Domain like {20005,3011})
As the racers power around this track, you can feel the effort that went into making these machines the best they can be.
A daring overtake coming out of turn three there.
What a race! These pilots have left it all on the track, and Cardinal's Domain will remember this one for cycles to come!(Cardinal's Domain like {20005,3011})
A hard-fought battle till the very end! The competition was fierce, but the pilots held their ground!
A valiant effort by the newest pilot on the track, but the cosmic winds weren't in their favour today.
A warm welcome to the heart of Freedom's Reach for another thrilling race in the Nebula Open Cup!(Freedom's Reach like {20005,9036})
Today we're brought to you by Aurora Casino, space spins and cosmic wins!
Brace yourselves for another riveting race that promises to push our pilots to the limits.
The course is a labyrinth of twists and turns, a true challenge that separates the racers from the BoFu haulers.
And look out, because today we've got some extra excitement.
The legendary Kaylah Daniels is dusting off the cobwebs and emerging from retirement to test the mettle of the new Dart racing ship!
We haven't seen anything like this for a long time, and the thrill is palpable as we witness the return of a true racing icon.
Get ready for a spectacle, folks!
That seems particularly headstrong in the corners, but this is where Daniels' shows her experience, keeping the power down where she can.
Hold your breath folks! We have a collision on the approach to corner four.
