It's a tight turn there! These racers are threading the needle, and it's a sight to behold. Precision at its finest!
I never thought I'd see the day! It was a tough race, but Kaylah Daniels' record is smashed!
And there we have it: a hard fought race, all the way to the end, but in the end the Dart is quite simply in a league of its own.
A tough break for some of our racers, but racing is a fickle mistress and today just wasn't their day.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 30 / Nathan R. Gunne
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 30 / Nathan R. Gunne
page.t: --on her way! I repeat, this is Commander Gunne! The Dragonfyre is on her way!
Noted. Were you able to contact the rest of the fleet?
It'll have to do. We need to regroup to stand any chance.
Set course for Luna, let's see how bad--
This is Gunne. We hear you, pilot. Report!
Can you modify it? Change the effect, the targets, anything?
We'll use it now. As it is.
We turn it on, all Terraformers in the system will pursue us, right?
So we draw them away. Through the gate.
That's why I'll stay behind and destroy the gate once they're through.
What? Naomi, this is our only chance! It can work! You can't--
Comms! Prepare to broadcast the Terraformer signal.
Commander Gunne to all ships. We have found a way to save Humanity.
Everyone who volunteers for this task needs to know the consequences. We will be relentlessly pursued by the entire Terraformer fleet.
If we survive that, we are going to be stranded on the far side of the gate, never to see Earth again.
Anyone who wishes to remain and help Earth rebuild, should do so now. You will have a few minutes to get clear of the fleet and find the nearest station. There is no shame in this.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Female 27 / Naomi Kelly
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 27 / Naomi Kelly
page.t: Combat speed. All batteries focus fire on the big Terraformer.
This is the Dragonfyre, hope we're not too late!
I don't like it when you risk your neck in a fighter, Nate.
Negative, comms are still scrambled. I only have last known locations.
That was the last of our destroyers.
No hostiles on sensors. Comms are clear again.
Um. A binary stream, Terraformer code.
I don't know. Maybe. Yes. I think so.
With our computers? A few days.
They'll wipe us out and come back.
I know that it can! That's why you can't stay behind. You'll be needed on the other side. To give the fleet a fighting chance, and for what comes after survival!
My thesis was on gate design, I know where it's vulnerable. Once the singularity collapses you'll have a window to destroy the far gate as well.
Nathan Ridley Gunne, you know this is the correct choice. Quit stalling and execute this Hail Mary!
We should prepare. As soon as they see us, it'll be on.

This is Lieutenant Commander Naomi Kelly to Earth Fleet. The last of the Terraformers are about to pass through. Once I pull the trigger you will be on your own, isolated in uncharted space, relentlessly hounded by the demons we created.
But I know that you can make it. You're the strongest people I've ever known, and you have the bravest, most devoted and inspiring leader of our time.
Thanks to all of you, humanity will have a chance to rebuild. We are never going to forget you.
This is a call from the Argon Confederation to all willing and able pilots to aid us in defending our space from the Xenon.
My job here is to help coordinate our efforts against the Xenon and given the threat, we're in need of as many volunteers as we can get.
This is going to be a major operation, so check your fire, and keep a level head.
Due to our efforts, Xenon activity has been greatly reduced throughout our space.
Thank you for your help in this conflict.
As you may have seen, Xenon activity is on the rise and we are struggling to hold them back.
There is a great need for pilots like you.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 31 / Military Pilot
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 31 / Military Pilot
page.t: --fleet command, please come in! Can you hear me? This is--
Oh thank god. We don't have much time. I'm sending an important data package.

It's some kind of signal that makes Terraformers go berserk or something! The Captain wanted to use it tactically but the entire enemy fleet stopped what they were doing and bore down on us. They tore our battleships to pieces in minutes!
I think I'm the only one who got away. Captain's orders. I can't believe...
I can't believe I actually made it! I was sure I'd--

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 32 / Kyle Brennan
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 32 / Kyle Brennan
page.t: Stop them... You have to... stop...
There's... no other way. Do it... now!
... not much time... I can't hold... any longer...

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 33 / Bret Serra
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 33 / Bret Serra
page.t: In the settlements of The Reach, a peculiar sort of nobility holds sway, one characterised by a rather sedentary nature. Consequently, it's not uncommon for descendants of notable families, particularly those lacking immediate inheritance prospects, to seek out adventure and renown elsewhere. Upon their return, laden with treasures and tales from across the cosmos, they're embraced by their families once more, despite some disappointment regarding their initial departure.

Dear Mother and Father, I hope this message finds you well. It has now been precisely two months since I left. I regret leaving without saying goodbye, but it just seemed easier. I've been working here in Hatikvah's Choice and some interesting trade propositions have come up with a group that call themselves the Hatikvah Free League, so I'll set a course for winds of fortune. I'll let you know how that goes...
Jules, Saya, keep your positions. I'll take care of this.
Promise to take care of each other.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Female 28 / Saya Kho
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 28 / Saya Kho
page.t: Guys, I hate to interrupt, but--
Hello, Bret. You actually made it.
When it aligned with his interests.
We'll get him back, Julian, I promise. For now, let's focus on the battle ahead of us.
We need to get Kyle out of there.
I don't know how long I can hold this...
Do you think Kyle is somehow connected to their command computer? Or brains, or whatever they have?
Then getting him out may stop their mothership from firing that giant laser again!
Shield generator's damaged, but I'll be fine.
Some kind of repelling force field?

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Female 29 / Myrna Rae
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 29
page.t: Sorry, I am busy right now.
(reaction to friendly fire)Hey, will you stop firing?
(reaction to friendly fire)You're wrecking my shields!
(reaction to friendly fire)Why are you shooting at me?
Hyperion Gravidar signature acquired. Back on track!
Come on... yes! Folks, the Hyperion is on my Gravidar again!
Look at that beauty! The Hyperion, three-odd decades of history, pristine like on the day she was commissioned!
The Hyperion - just like a Shrike out of the mist! Suddenly, she's here, suddenly, she's gone!
And there she is again! She should've been decommissioned and abandoned after all that time. But apparently not!
Whoa! Is she trying to shake me off? Not happening - I'm staying right on her tail!
Konnichiwa! Of course, that's the whole point! Name's Myrna Rae, I'm a, uh, hands-on historian. I'm casting for posterity!
Well, I'm on the heels of an old ship prototype that shouldn't exist. I feel everyone should know about it!
Oh, so you did listen in on my casts!
Yes, the Hyperion, an old Paranid prototype from long ago. It took me ages to track it down!
Except that it's still active; someone or something is commanding it. I wasn't prepared for that.
No, not really. Well... kind of... maybe? Possibly!
Listen... ok. Yes. I need assistance. Will you help me?
Fair enough. I guess I'll manage. But please do contact me if you change your mind!
Oh, that's brilliant! Let me upload the tracking info to your onboard computer, and let's get on with it!
Here's the rundown: most ships' energy signatures are so similar that it's hard to detect and differentiate them, especially hours after they've passed.
Fortunately, the Hyperion isn't like most ships! Its energy signature is quite unique.
However, my onboard AI core still needs to perform complex Fourier transformations to tease the signal from the noise.
Here's how we'll do it: you scan a gate or a transit accelerator and send me the data via an encrypted channel.
I'll pass it through the AI core, and once it's done its analysis, we'll know whether the Hyperion has recently passed through.
To summarise: scan, send me the data, wait a bit, and I'll let you know. Simple as that!
Myrna here. Please scan local gates and transit accelerators and uplink the data.
Hello again. Scan all gates and accelerators in this sector. Myrna out.
That's odd! She must've gone somewhere, now, mustn't she? Are you quite sure you've scanned all possible routes out of the sector?
Alright - my AI core has stopped crunching numbers! Now let's have a look...
Hum. The AI core estimates a less than three percent chance that the Hyperion went through here. I'd say, try scanning another one.
Nope, results turn up blank. The old ship didn't pass through this one. Let's try elsewhere.
Gosh! 98-odd percent the Hyperion went through here! Back on track!
Yes! It's a winner! The ship for sure passed through this one. Let's go!
Myrna here. Alright, new sector, old procedure, you know the drill: scan gates and accelerators, uplink your data, and let me crunch the numbers. Let's do this.
Oh gosh oh gosh! We've found her! Would you look at that! There she is, the Hyperion, right under our noses! Absolutely brilliant!
This is Myrna Rae calling the pilot entity of the Hyperion. Do you copy?
Somebody is listening, but not answering.
I wonder if it's the ship's AGI or a sentient.
What do we make of that?
Hum. Wait a minute. Hyperion is not its original name.
And if it's an old Paranid onboard AGI, or even a live Paranid, maybe we should sprinkle in some of that sacral terminology?
Behold! We extend our greetings to the dignified vessel of the Paranid Empire, the sacred, uh, galleon Trinity!
Blimey! The Olmancketslat? The last known commander of the Trinity?!
I do. I think I understand, Olmancketslat.
You were trapped in this sector when the gates fell, almost 30 years ago.
Now you are seeking communion again, but the Paranid Empire, once an unwavering bastion against the forces of entropy... it has splintered.
I understand that perfectly. Truly, I do.
The Godrealm of the Paranid has changed from when it was known as an Empire, that much is true.
But as far as I can tell, it's still the most similar to its former self.
The Holy Order of the Pontifex is closely tied to a strict interpretation of the Paranid dogma that appeared some time after the Fall of the Gates.
The name may have changed, but the spirit remains.
The Realm of the Trinity seems removed from the first incarnation of the Paranid Empire.
But it might be wise to start your search for communion there.
I'm certain you'll find your answers there.
Olmancketslat, this is such an important decision for you, and I don't want to rush my answer.
Would you mind giving me a little time to deliberate?
Relations between our peoples haven't always been... easy, even though Paranid doctrine calls for empathy towards what it deems "inferior species".

It may be a small solace for you to know that, while the Paranid Empire experienced a dramatic setback, after the creation of the Alliance of the Word, your people and mine have become somewhat closer.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 34 / Sobert
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 34
page.t: Sorry, I am busy right now.
(Agent was hired)I am looking forward to seeing what we can achieve together.
(Player-owned hello, on HQ)Ready for assignment, Sir.
(Player-owned hello, on HQ)Ready for assignment, Ma'am.
(Player-owned hello, on mission)I was not briefed that you might take part in this operation.
(Fire Agent 1)Are you sure you want to let me go?
(Fire Agent 2)Affirmative. It was an honour working with you.
(Going on mission)Departing to execute the mission.
(Returned from mission, success)Reporting back for duty. The mission was a complete success.
(Returned from mission, unsuccessful)Barely made it out of that one alive... The mission failed.
(reaction to friendly fire)Hey, will you stop firing?
(reaction to friendly fire)You are wrecking my shields!
(reaction to friendly fire)Why are you shooting at me?
This is attaché Brend Sobert aboard the diplomatic vessel Berenice. I'm being attacked by unknown forces and require urgent assistance.
This is Brend Sobert aboard the Berenice. I require assistance. Use of lethal force authorised in accordance with article 9.4 ICSC.
To any capable ship in range: I'm attaché Brend Sobert returning from a diplomatic mission. I'm under attack and require immediate assistance.
I'm assistant attaché Brend Sobert of the Argon Federation.
I'm assistant attaché Brend Sobert with the Terran Protectorate.
I'm consultant Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Teladi Company.
I'm consultant Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Ministry of Finance.
I'm consultant Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Queendom of Boron.
I'm Split-Argon relations expert Brend Sobert on a mission for the Split Patriarchy.
I'm two-eyes liaison Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Godrealm of the Paranid.
I'm two-eyes liaison Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Holy Order of the Pontifex.
I'm two-eyes liaison Brend Sobert acting on behalf of the Realm of the Trinity.
I was held up by this attack group. They told me to prepare for boarding. I declined. Then they disabled the Berenice's engines.
Surprisingly, no. They appear to be waiting for something.
This mission falls under full diplomatic protection - ICSC Article 9.1.
Under 9.4, your assistance - including lethal force - is explicitly covered. Help me, and you'll be compensated.
Citizen, please accept my sincere thanks! It was very fortunate that you acted so quickly.
You prevented an attempted hostile takeover of a diplomatic courier mission.
Yes. They're sealed in a magnetic stasis field - makes them difficult to transfer between vessels. We'd need a proper relief ship for that.
I'm grateful, citizen. Yes, a prototype with some mods, same as the Berenice.
I am transporting historic materials bound for the archives.
If I may trouble you - would you instead fetch my Envoy class, while I wait here?
Citizen, I'm so very glad you've returned! And you too, esteemed colleague Saringias. Always a pleasure!
Well, I never said that. I said "historic materials", which is true. But let's not delay.
Once we've transferred the material, we should destroy the Berenice.
No need to hand a diplomat vessel with sensitive gear over to the Ektoberyll.
Our unpleasant "friend" d'Aldrino mentioned an incoming strike team. Better we're gone before they arrive.
Citizen, I'm cutting the main engine.
But that's unrealistic. You can't just destroy 126 - unless you throw it into another star.
The Envoy's Podkletnovs seem to have elevated Planck-time latency, and the 126 doesn't like that.
The mag-stasis should stabilise things in a few seconds.
The Argon Federation, on the other hand, has been stable since long before The Dark.
Maybe so. But the Ministry can't protect it for that long.
Feels like we're sitting on a powder keg. I'll admit that my palms are getting sweaty.
Cutting engines once more. Stay sharp.
Saringias, citizen - the 126 has calmed down. I'm re-lighting the engines.

Dr. d'Aldrino, let me, too, be perfectly clear. The experiment conducted by the Ektoberyll constitutes a breach of both the WMD Testing Treaty of 689 NT and the Stellar-Scale Weapons Moratorium of 749 NT.
Both are ratified by the Argon Federation. The material in question has been lawfully confiscated under Federation jurisdiction and will not be returned.
Citizen, was that supposed to be helpful?!
Citizen! Remember, collateral damage isn't victory!
Hey! I don't know about you, but I don't have a death wish. Focus!
Careful! Believe me, you really don't want to see what happens if the 126 destabilises!
Citizen, careful! The stasis field is already compromised!
D'Aldrino, destroying the Envoy means destroying the 126 - and the entire sector.
Ma'am, you've crossed the line, from merely unethical to openly criminal. Is that what you wanted?
The 126 has stabilised, I'm re-lighting the engines. We're on the final stretch.
And I, esteemed colleague Saringias, feel sorry that we didn't get d'Aldrino...
Citizen, I'm truly grateful for your invaluable assistance.
My esteemed colleague may have preferred the 126 to remain under Ministry stewardship - but rest assured, the Argon Federation honours ICSC treaties just as strictly.
I've been authorised to offer you an Envoy class ship - on permanent loan - in recognition of your service. She's yours to command as you see fit.
And naturally, should the AFIS or the Diplomatic Corps require the unique capabilities of a vessel like the Envoy, you'll find yourself at the very top of our... rather exclusive list of contractors.
Citizen, it's been a pleasure. Until next time.

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Male 35 / Business Partner
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 35

page.title: Mission Argon NPC Female 30
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 30
page.t: Magnetic containment nominal. One-twenty-six stable. Primary coil charge complete. Discharge in five... four... three... two... one...
This is d'Aldrino speaking. Accelerate, pass on, for your own good! Don't make this your business.
Hello. I'm Dr. d'Aldrino, overseeing this mission. This is a legal operation under the Ektoberyll code of conduct. Do not interfere.
d'Aldrino to squad leader. Fall back. The situation is getting out of hand. I'll be requesting a strike team to handle this. I repeat: fall back.
This is Chief Scientist Dr. Franca d'Aldrino.
The material in your possession was illegally extracted from our custody under the guise of a diplomatic mission.
We'd prefer not to use force to recover it, so I'm saying this only once: release the material and retreat.
The statutes of the ICSC are quite clear: in the absence of jurisdiction, force is permitted under specific circumstances. This qualifies.
d'Aldrino to strike team leader. Authorisation to attack.
I'm not the criminal here, you are!
Just give up. If you win now... you'll lose worse, later.
You're stalling the inevitable. That's all you're doing. Science will win.
The Ektoberyll is more powerful than you realise.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 1 / Paranid Story - Buccaneer
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 1
page.t: He's sent me one of his lackeys.
Come a little closer, (emphasize 'lackey')lackey, and we'll have a chat.
Let me answer your question with another question, my dear.
How far would you be willing to go to be sure that your allies were up to scratch?
And since we're having such a nice, confidential chat...
How much would you be willing to sacrifice in order to defeat your worst enemies, and understand your true purpose.
If you had riches, power, respect, what would it take for you to give them all up?
Well, at least your... (slight pause before 'friend')friend does seem reasonably competent.
Competent enough to run a small errand for me.
I seem to remember that you came here to ask questions about the Paranid.
I'll answer... (slight pause before 'two')two questions of yours.
We'll call it an advance payment.
To an outsider, it might seem as though this war has just been going back and forth, with no prospect of a resolution.
That's not an entirely inaccurate assessment, but it's not the whole picture.
It's no accident that military supplies for this conflict have become one of the safest investments at this end of the gate network.
You see, the two factions aren't (emphasize 'really')really fighting over territory or resources.
In the minds of their leaders, elimination of their opponents would actually be a tragic outcome.
That's because they're fighting for the hearts and minds of their people.
If one Pontifex backed down, even just a little, he'd be sacrificing his legitimacy.
I imagine they must be quite desperate for an outside solution by now.
(if Paranid)That's a rather curious question, coming from you.
(if Paranid)You must have spent far too long away from your kin.
Someone looking at it from the outside could easily come to the conclusion that civil war was a natural state for Paranid society.
It seems almost like some sort of expression of their psyche; always questioning and challenging one another's beliefs.
Nothing could be further from the truth, however.
What they so desperately want to resolve is what to them is an almost tangible geometric impossibility, namely there being two Pontifices.
The current situation is utter sacrilege, tearing at their stoic demeanour and rending their perception of their own culture.
It's an aberration in history that needs to be erased at all cost.
Oh, how nice of you to ask.
I was a pilot myself, you know, back in the days before the gate shutdown.
I served one of the greatest minds who ever lived.
What I wouldn't do to bring them back.
Ah yes, sorry about that dear.
In my line of work, you can never be too careful about who you... (slight pause before 'associate')associate with.
If you ever find yourself facing the kind of impossible odds I'm up against, you might look back fondly at our little encounter.
All this interrogation is making me dreadfully tired.
You'll get your answers eventually, though. Don't you worry.
Now, about that little errand I mentioned.
Nice to see you're so eager.
You should receive your instructions right about(stretch word 'abooout')... now.
So, that concludes your side of the bargain.
If I remember rightly, that means I owe you a few more answers.
The item you brought me has some... (slight pause before 'sentimental')sentimental value.
There is someone I'm yearning to see for one last time.
You've proven yourself to be pretty dependable, so let me add another piece of the map to your little scavenger hunt.
If you do indeed find what you seek out there, at the end of the galaxy, then I might just let you meet that person too.
It's good to see you again, dear.
I trust my Duke already gave you an introduction to his... (slight pause before 'diplomatic')diplomatic effort?
Well, we're about to... (slight pause before 'improve')improve that plan of his quite dramatically.
You see, the countless years of isolation have clouded my Duke's ambition.
Even though his earlier attempts must have thrown the wretchedness of those unenlightened three-eyes into sharp relief...
He still refuses to rid himself of that poisonous illusion of (spit word 'peace')peace.
Will you help me show him the truth?
We'll provide the flames from which my Duke will be reborn.
You'll find a toolbox on the docking area.
Its contents might prove useful to you.
Remember the cipher you went and got for me?
With the help of that, the monument's gates should open for you.
And as for the other items...
This structure must surely contain a few points which are quite...(slight pause before 'vital')vital to its integrity.
I trust you will know what to do, once you come across them.
Return to me when you're done, so that we can enjoy the spectacle together.
Now, let us reap the rewards from all our efforts.
(flaring up)I'll just have to deal with this myself.
(grandiosely, sardonically)You've all fallen for my trap!
(grandiosely, maliciously)Your deaths will put an end to this charade!
(grandiosely, maliciously)The realms of the Paranid will fall one by one!
(tranquil, directly to player)Well, my dear, this is it. A good way to go, I think.
My dears, you are witnessing the birth of a new era.
It appears that we're needed elsewhere.
(Paranid Diplomatic Mission - Unification Sinks - Gride Orrian)
(Paranid Diplomatic Mission - Escalation Sinks - Gride Orrian)
I was devastated when you didn't call me after the grand spectacle.
Luckily, your friends are being very hospitable to me.
I'm particularly fond of your cute Boron.
You see, it's truly invigorating to know that my Duke is back to his old self.
I'm sure you have heard some of the grand tales by now.
The entirety of the southern network, Paranid, Split and Boron alike, trembled in fear of the Buccaneers.
My Duke commands a sizeable fleet now, but what is a true pirate without a lair?
We once had a grand, impervious haven to call our own, and with your help, so it shall be again.
Don't you worry. There will be a reward, as always.
I knew I made the right choice, relying on you again.
Now, I don't mean to sound too demanding, but...
My Duke's new haven still requires a capable station manager.
I'm sure that won't be a challenge for someone as resourceful as you.
(militaristic)Aha! The hero of the day makes his appearance.
(militaristic, addressing female player)Aha! The heroine of the day makes her appearance.
(militaristic)Are you ready to give those three-eyes what they deserve?

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 2 / Diplomat Intro - Hatikvah Manager
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 2
page.t: I apologise for the state of the place. Things are rather hectic at the moment.
We've signed a number of promising new trade contracts, but circumstances have left us spread a bit thin.
(responding to comm)I hear you Dal. I'll be there in a minute.
We've prepared a freighter for you to fly over to one of our new partners.
Honestly, as long as you can deliver those goods on time, I'll be happy.
If you do that, the ship's as good as yours.
If you screw us over, well, the worst we can do is revoke your docking privileges.
Sorry to cut and run but there's something that needs my attention.
I look forward to seeing how you do.
You also said it would be prevented.
That's not going to be of much comfort to their families, is it?
I think we need to get the Argon police involved.
Blake tailed her target straight back to the port. Looks like you were right.
I see you had some trouble with the Argon police.
Don't worry about it. We're not exactly saints here.
Things went smoothly, I take it.
This is Dal Busta. He's been helping us in our efforts to expand our business.
As you may have heard, a Hatikvah freighter was destroyed earlier today.
It seems that the Scale Plate Pact don't like the idea of us 'going clean'.
That's something we're looking to improve on.
If you're willing, I'd like you to help us.
Our goal is to break all ties with Scale Plate, while making sure they don't continue harassing us.
Fair enough. The offer stands if you change your mind.
I've known Dal for several years now. He's a very cunning and skilled analyst.
When I was tasked to expand our trade operations, get closer to the Argon, I knew I needed him on board.
Unfortunately, the Scale Plate Pact have proven to be rather erratic.
Hatikvah have not had it easy in the years gone by. We traded with whoever was willing.
They were chaotic times and Scale Plate gave us an opportunity to grow.
The Argon simply offer better trade and security prospects than Scale Plate ever could.
I'll let Dal know. Just follow his instructions and you'll be fine.
Why don't you go chase Dal down?
I'm sure he'd want to show off his ship.
We've had another freighter targeted by Scale Plate. No casualties this time, but they're limping home.
I hope you've found something we can use to make them think twice.
I'm sick of us being toyed with. I leave it up to you, Dal. Just don't go overboard.
Good to have you back in one piece.
(slightly annoyed)That's not much more to go on.
(slightly relieved)That's at least something to go on.
(sigh)What do you suggest we do now?
I have a feeling this is going to cost me.
Aren't these demands a bit much? We're supposed to be breaking ties with them, not working closer.
It looks like I've got some favours to call in.
As you've helped us out so much, I'll wire you some additional credits.
It seems we're finally getting to the end of this mess.
There are still some loose ends to tie up.
Acting on the information you gathered with Dal, we sent out a number of automated drones to attack caches of Scale Plate supplies.
In hindsight, maybe not the best idea.
They're not responding to the deactivation signal.
We need pilots to go out and destroy them before they scupper any chance of a deal.
Good job dealing with those drones.
I certainly won't shed a tear for those destroyed Scale Plate caches but I doubt it will help our cause.
As part of the settlement with Scale Plate, we're constructing a new production complex.
This is a huge project and we need to ensure it's safe until we hand it over.
Dal suggested that we should deploy some static defences around it.
Do you have a moment to come and see me?
We're getting close to finishing this.
Captain, good to see you back.
Ah, captain. I have Dal on the line.
I'll send you the station's location.
We're doing our best with the instructions that Dal left us, but to be honest, a lot of my staff are not happy.
Given the losses we've suffered, many of them would rather go to war than appease Scale Plate.
Dal suggested that I go to meet the Scale Plate lieutenant and hand off the settlement package.
That is not going to happen as I'd likely shove that Teladi down the nearest docking shaft.
I'd greatly appreciate it if you go and hand him this.
Just smile, make the exchange and get out of there.
Then we can get on with our lives.
Give me a moment to prepare another one.
Pilot, what is going on? We have Scale Plate making moves against our assets.
We need help defending the station.
We don't have the forces to deal with this, especially in the outer reaches.
Even the local law enforcement isn't keeping up.
I'm going to contact the Argon. This has gone far enough.
Until they step in, please help anywhere you can.
I'll send you data on where we need a hand.
Captain, I suggest you get out of there.
The Argon are rounding up Hatikvah and Scale Plate alike.
Before they bring me in, I'll send you whatever payment you're owed.
This really did end up a mess.
If you see that Teladi bastu on your travels, fire a few missiles from me.
As for Dal, he's probably laying low for a reason. I'll send his last known co-ordinates.
Take good care of her. We don't have much in the budget for repairs.
If you don't want to use the ship we've provided, that's fine, as long as you get the job done.
Alright. Prepare the freighter for departure.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 1 / Diplomat Intro - Argon Manager
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 1
page.t: (station manager)Please standby while we run some checks.
Hey, we did ask you to stay put. Anyway, the delivered goods were fine. Carry on, pilot.
We're happy to see Hatikvah move away from those sketchy dealings of the past.
If it means fewer Scale Plate Pact ships in our space, I'm all for it.
Just watch your back out there, captain.
(station manager)Hello there captain. I understand you're delivering goods on behalf of Hatikvah.
Target gamma-3 is approaching the gate.
I owe that Boron a favour, so don't worry about the cost.
You do know it's illegal without the proper licence, right?
I think our business is done.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 3 / Sol warning announcer 2 / Terraforming contact (ANT)
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 3
page.t: (Sol system restrictions; see also 10153 for male version)
You are approaching a restricted area.
You are entering a restricted area.
You are entering a highly restricted area.
We insist that you change course immediately or face military action.
You are on a course to enter secure space.
We have a vessel in violation of secure space restrictions.

The Antigone Senate has announced this morning that an effort to "terraform" a world near our borders has begun. An unaffiliated third party is reported to be carrying out the process, which has been met with some controversy and debate.
Once again, the Senate has approved the start of terraforming efforts on an as-yet uninhabited world near our borders.

The world to be made habitable is Shiokaze, a blue planet in the Getsu Fune system. It is home to several highly toxic kinds of berries that actually make the air poisonous to humans, which has so far prevented any large-scale settlement. We will update you as this story develops.
Breaking now, we have just received word that Shiokaze's flora is no longer a deadly threat to humans. We have invited the xenobotanist Dr. Leo Corter to talk us through the details and implications.
The first group of settlers has touched down on Shiokaze. Among them are several experts on biology and gastronomy, eager to survey the local fruits.

Shiokaze, once a beautiful but spiteful planet, has been fully tamed. Millions of citizens have made their home on this world, which is quickly becoming a destination for gourmets wanting to sample the emerging speciality cuisine. We have checked in with the locals, and they all agree: the future looks delicious.

The world to be made habitable is Messner, a mountainous planet in the Frontier Edge system. This rather picturesque world would already be mostly habitable, were it not for the constant threat of Xenon invading that system. We will update you as this story develops.

The terraforming of Messner continues. After raising the global temperature, many valleys can now be turned to agricultural use. On the other hand, opponents of this measure argue that this would limit the variety of potential winter sports. More on this debate in our upcoming programming.

Intrepid colonists have begun moving to Messner and sharing images of themselves in front of some breathtaking alpine landscapes. The Xenon do not seem to be overly bothered by us moving in, so this is sure to encourage many more to follow.

Messner, long known as "that cold planet with the mountains", has become the number one holiday destination, attracting visitors from all over known space. And with a wide range of activities and famously cosy hotels, this is looking to be more than a fad. Reservations are going fast, so be sure to make yours soon. I already did!

Incredibly, the world to be made habitable is a volcanic planet in the Atiya's Misfortune system. It's hot enough to instantly set your hair on fire, and the ground shakes pretty much constantly. And as if that were not enough, the surrounding space is a veritable hotbed of Xenon activity, if you'll excuse my wordplay. We will certainly follow the efforts with great interest and update you as this story develops.

Thanks to an ingenious piece of engineering, the volcanoes on Atiya's Misfortune have been successfully tamed. While this is just a step on the long road to habitability, our experts tell us that this measure will actually make all future projects much, much easier, as it also dampens the earthquakes that would have been sure to ruin many a building.

Unbelievably, Atiya's Misfortune now has large habitable areas on its surface. Our experts tell us that the basis for native life is the next step, and possibly the last big item before actual settlement can begin.

Today we are experiencing history. Here I am on the freshly named world of Cinder, standing in a field. The weather is warm, but not uncomfortably so. A few clouds pass overhead and a light breeze rustles the grain around me. To think that not too long ago this place was about as inhospitable as they come... it's staggering. One can't help but be hopeful for the future, if things like this can be achieved. Well, this was Tracie Berron, reporting on location for ANC News. Now if you'll excuse me, I have some awe to get back to.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 2 / Pioneer Terraforming - Police official / Gate discovery official / Sol warning announcer 1 / Terraforming contact (SCA)
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 2
page.t: Command, I'm getting odd readings here.
Shouldn't gate patrol have reported Xenon presence?
Negative, no Xenon incursion passed the gate.
Might be a hiccup in that old program. I'll run sanity checks.
Command, picking up signatures... are there Xenon I should know about?
Nothing to report. Must have been a fluke.
Whatever it was, it got lost in the background noise.
A system error, nothing to report.
(angry)Tell the quartermasters that our scanners need a complete overhaul.
(angry)Command, reporting signature readings in violation of penal code 2-0-2-5 AGI Act.(firm professional alarm raising, speak A-G-I separately, speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Must have slipped through in the noise at the gate.
Still looking for the source. It can't be far.
(angry)Can't find a culprit. Lost the signal.
I'll run diagnostics to see if we can salvage the readings.

(angry)Local patrols, we have a possible signal in violation of penal code 2-0-2-5 AGI Act, I repeat, possible violation of 2-0-2-5.(firm professional alarm raising, speak A-G-I separately, speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Adjust your radars and report any suspicious readings immediately.
(angry)Command, reporting readings on our 2-0-2-5.(speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Command, reading our 2-0-2-5 again.(speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Command, reporting 2-0-2-5 signature readings.(speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Located a ship responsible for the signature. Transmitting the ID.
(angry)Local patrols, we have a ship in violation of 2-0-2-5 AGI Act, presenting as a civilian vessel.(speak A-G-I separately, speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(angry)Reporting ID to military command to suspend their sector privileges.
(angry)We don't know what this one is capable of and we don't intend to find out.
(angry)2-0-2-5 in sight.(speak numerals separately, don't speak dash)
(Discovering Gate from Terran side of the universe)
Incoming Xenon detected. Prepare for battle.
Take them down before they invade deeper into the inner core.
(Discovering Gate from X-side of the universe)
OK everyone, listen up!(this and the next few sentences all spoken in US military command style)
We've got reports of increased Xenon activity in Savage Spur II.
As everyone is aware, this is the primary Xenon entry point into the region and it's our duty to handle this situation.
Our mission is to initiate a precision strike, in order to divert their attention from our movements in Getsu Fune.
Our mission is to patrol and engage any Xenon we spot.
(Teladi vs Terran trade-official bickering - Terran Speaker)
(authority, military, calm)Terran Security to Teladi Vessel. You are approaching Terran restricted space, please divert your course!
(authority, military, calm more strict tone)We are not interested. We insist that you divert your course.(emphasise NOT and INSIST)
(authority, military, calm more demanding tone)Negative! We demand that you change course immediately.(emphasise DEMAND and IMMEDIATELY)

(authority, military, calm very demanding tone)We order you to change your course immediately, or we will be obliged to take measures to protect the safety and security of this system!(emphasise ORDER, IMMEDIATELY, WILL)
(Sol system restrictions; see also 10154 for female version)
You are approaching a restricted area.
You are entering a restricted area.
You are entering a highly restricted area.
We insist that you change course immediately or face military action.
You are on a course to enter secure space.
We have a vessel in violation of secure space restrictions.

Wait, you're really doing this? Getting that place back for us? I can't say that everyone really believes it yet, but they'll stop pestering you and yours. You know, just in case you turn out not to be running a racket here.

Well paint me red and call me a scruffin, you're the real deal, aren't you? People are starting to take an interest in what may become our new home, so don't be alarmed if you see a lot of suspicious ships hanging around. Shimatta, I haven't felt this energised in years!

I... I don't know what to say. I'm not very good at speeches, but... thanks. There are a lot of people down here who can now live a quiet life because of your generosity. OK, maybe not all of us are made for living dirtside, but those that remain in space should get by just fine with less... violent activities. I've even heard that some crews considered joining your outfit! Well, if they do, please take good care of them. They're good people.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 3 / Segaris Pioneer Chief Scientist / Terraforming contact 1 (ARG)
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 3
page.t: Najia, it looks like your security clearance has been approved.
Please come and see me in the Neptune sector.
Please come and see me so we can discuss this in person.
Unfortunately, we're still waiting on some of the team to arrive.
In the meantime, perhaps you could do me a favour.
I'm in need of an item not often found on the general market.
Consider it a test of your resourcefulness.
Just so you're not completely lost without my guidance, I've marked a potential location where you can hope to find the item.
Check your map for those details.
These items are often sourced from Xenon, but it would not be very professional of me to encourage you to seek them out.
You're late. Fortunately for you, we're having technical difficulties.
I looked over your file, and I must say it made for interesting reading.
Know this. You will have to impress me personally if you want any chance of getting an assignment worthy of your apparent skill set.
While we wait for departure, perhaps you could showcase your resourcefulness.
Should you find it, you will most certainly have piqued my interest.
We're out of time. Get back here when you can.
You can likely find the dealer in the bar.
Knowing you, you're probably already acquainted.
Remember, this is critical work. Those satellites don't just help with our research, they also serve as a sensor net.
All teams report that their tasks have been completed. Return to the ship and we'll get moving.
Good job. You're just in time. We're about ready to disembark.
We're on our way towards a facility very important to the future of our people.
It recently suffered structural damage due to some unknown spacial distortion. That's why you've been brought in.
Our resources are limited, but our people are exceptional. I welcome you to the team.
Unfortunately, our limited resources force us to make a minor detour.
A number of satellites have been targeted by Xenon.
While we managed to intercept the attackers, several satellites have been left in a state of disrepair.
I will assign a number of satellites for you to return to working order.
I guess those satellites were in worse shape than I thought.
We'll pass on the word to get new ones deployed.
Now that that's out of the way, we can finally get on with our primary task. I can hardly wait.
As you know, this is a high security facility. Just because you have clearance to do your job, it doesn't mean you can go wandering off or touch everything.
It is currently unmanned and in safe-mode until we can repair the damage and ensure no further anomalies occur.
I'm not at liberty to divulge such information, but rest assured, you will be safe to perform your duties.
We begin by repairing the external structure. Get into your spacesuits and prepare to be guided to your assigned positions.
We're picking up strange readings again. You'd better get back to the ship.
Where did you go? What happened to the station?
The whole station moved with you?
Was there any identifiable cause for this spontaneous transportation?
We will prepare an expedition in order to reclaim our station from the Boron.
If you can, keep an eye on that Boron until we arrive.
If you'll excuse me, I need to get working on that.
I am Dr. Rick Feynman, Chief Scientist of the Oberth(Oberth is the ship's name) and in charge of Project Genesis.(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
Wait, Najia Takio? Is it really you?(Player name from Terran Game Start 2)
Wait! I know you, don't I?
Mr. Hariken? Is it really you?(Player name from the Terran Game Start 1)
You worked for us at the station!
We didn't expect biological matter to have survived this transition.
As I was saying, we are looking into how this station got here.
I'm sorry to inform you that you currently lack the required clearance to access this information.
Oh, it's just part of our gravimetric studies.
For now it is just a mass of data from our sensors, but we'll publish our research once it is concluded.
We are currently lacking Antimatter Cells(translate 'Antimatter Cells' same as {20201,201}) to complete our observations.
If you can organise a delivery to this vessel, we'll be able to greatly advance our timetable.
I'm glad to see you fit and well.
How is our Boron nemesis doing?
Our research vessel is currently observing anomalies and gravimetric shears in this region.
We're looking into how this station got here.
But they are still in our part of the Gate network.
Setting course to the new station position. We will meet you there.
Our research team thanks you for your cooperation.
Thank you for your continued assistance.
We're still waiting for Antimatter Cells(translate 'Antimatter Cells' same as {20201,201}) to complete our observations.
It seems the Terrans, or maybe even the station's current occupant, are obstructing any deliveries to block our progress.
If you can organise a delivery, please do so.
It will greatly advance our timetable.
We're still waiting for ships to join us in a synchronised long range scan.
We need your help in putting this Antimatter to good use.('Antimatter' same as in {20201,201})
Please position your ship at the specified location and prepare to initiate a Long Range Scan.('Long Range Scan' as in {10002,433})
We will need ships at the specified locations to initiate a synchronised Long Range Scan.('Long Range Scan' as in {10002,433})
We will be enlisting, but if you have any friends who could join us, now would be a good time to ask them along.
It looks like you're positioning your ship for the synchronised scan.
Please try to be precise. We don't want junk readings cluttering up our database.
It appears you drifted away. Please adjust your ships' positions to the specified locations.(multiple ships case)
Prepare to use your Long Range Scan in the direction of these coordinates.('Long Range Scan' as in {10002,433})
We read that your ship's Long Range Scanner has booted up. Initiating scan.
You missed your cue. What a waste of Antimatter!('Antimatter' same as in {20201,201})
Your alignment seems off. Please aim your scanner towards those coordinates.
Very good. We are receiving the data stream.
We're far from home, short on hands, and have additional tasks which need doing.
If you're interested, please meet me on our ship.
Please meet me on our ship to discuss our next steps.
Once you initiate the scan from your ship, the other captains will follow your lead.
You apparently misunderstood our task here.
We require ships at all specified locations to initiate a long range scan simultaneously.
It appears you drifted away. Please adjust your ship's position to the specified location.(one ship case)
Very good. Everyone appears to be in position and ready to initiate the synchronised scan.
Losing access to our research facility was what prompted this expedition.
You, of course, witnessed this first hand.
Now we have not only located our facility, but also taken precautions.
If it disappears from under our noses again, we won't have such a hard time tracking it down.
We've prepared some software which will help us regain access, but our ship isn't really inconspicuous enough to plant it on our station.
The malware should be subtle enough to go unnoticed by the current occupant.
It will be your job to plant it at this location, identified by our analyst.
According to the annotation on the station plans, there should be a Signal Leak next to what looks like either a valve or a window, but you'll find out when you get there.
You must surely have heard stories about the Boron, once known as a wise and noble people.
The Community of Planets hasn't heard anything from them in quite a while, so we don't know what happened to them after the Gate shutdown, or even if there are any of them left out there.
However, one of them is still among us, and from what we can gather he is a renegade and has turned criminal.
Can't really blame him. If I were trapped in the midst of Argnu societies for decades, I too would be tempted to take advantage, one way or the other.
This one chose to take our station to reside in.
Despite the noble reputation the Boron hold, this particular specimen has clearly signalled his intentions by stealing a station.
Since we can't be sure what else he might be capable of, it's imperative that we don't make him see us as his enemy.
We can't risk making him aware of our intent, otherwise we won't stand a chance against any measures he decides to take.
Proceed with caution and do not allow any intel to be leaked to the Boron.
After Segarian Intelligence identified the Boron as the perpetrator in this incident, we had them dig deeper.
He had connections to Split criminals. They, however, went off-grid and remain somewhat of a mystery.
He also had contacts with a Paranid Duke(Duke same as {30220,113}) who maintains some sort of private army by the name of Duke's Buccaneers.(Duke's Buccaneers same as {20203,2401})
Either way, the Boron is well connected among, and backed by, various shady characters.
His own technical proficiency, paired with the criminal network he built around himself, makes him capable of anything.
We need you to plant the malware on the station.
(angry)I expect this to be completed soon. You can manage priorities, I assume?
He... he gave you our research?(in disbelief)
This means we can continue with Project Genesis. It is our uttermost priority.(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
We'd better not make an enemy of the Boron, so we will leave him in possession of our station for the time being.
We'll have to come back better prepared if we want to recover our station.
But you were supposed to plant software. How did that happen?
I clearly underestimated this Boron and his capabilities.
I didn't think we'd make progress this fast.
Regardless, we could do with a little more of your assistance.
You'll be helping one of our associates in acquiring research that is vital to Project Genesis.(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
The Segaris Pioneers aspire to take a step up in the galactic community.(Segaris Pioneers same as Faction {20203,2901})
Project Genesis will help us build a foundation for our new future.(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
An independent scientist. Let me contact them.(Paranid Gender)
We are sending you the pilot you requested.(Referring to Player)
Yes... No... No, don't worry. This one is at least a two-star pilot.(Referring to Player Gender)
They('They' Referring to Paranid Gender) are experimenting with a phenomenon in The Void('The Void' same as {20005,1007}) and will instruct you on your part once you get there.
This may seem unconnected at first, but rest assured: You are helping mould our future.
It seems that you are missing crucial spacesuit equipment.
Take this Hand Laser. It will be useful later on.('Hand Laser'same as {20113,1061})
Take this with you. It will be useful later on.(Giving Player Hand Laser/Repair Laser/Bomb Launcher/Bombs if missing)
The independent scientist, Kuromanckami, awaits you at the experiment site.
We are at the rendezvous point and ready for transfer.
Brilliant! Of course, the Terrans would never let a ship full of their confidential data escape.
But that won't matter, as we managed to extract the data.
At last we will be able to terraform!
It will take a while to decrypt, examine and integrate this latest treasure into our existing research on terraforming.
It could take years, maybe even decades.
It's all there. We have the results for our research.
With this, we can immediately put Project Genesis(Project Genesis same as {30224,1}) into execution.
Gaian Prophecy will be terraformed!(Gaian Prophecy same as {20005,9019})
I suppose we might require assistance from your station at some point. Would you assist us in this endeavour?
The same data. They are getting a copy.
They're interested in Xenon behaviour and believe that understanding the original terraforming technology will help them understand the Xenon better.('they' Referring to Paranid gender)
With the new technology, we can make a proper attempt to terraform some of the planets and give our people a homeworld.
You've played a big role in this, and for that we are grateful.
We'll leave it with the Boron.
That is the least we can do after he fast-tracked all of our terraforming research to completion.
I don't know what our secret service was thinking, but it seems to me now that his classification as a criminal might have been an exaggeration.
At the very least he did seem eager to get this situation resolved without any hostility.
We now have access to rather advanced terraforming projects.
That will be required to undo some of the terraforming damage inflicted by the Xenon on Segaris.('Segaris', same as {20005,9047})
I still can't believe that we are about to achieve what we first set out to do.
At last, our people will have a homeworld.
I am proud to announce that we are making great progress in our terraforming endeavours.
You will find that our planet Terranova, in the Segaris system, is now a much more liveable place once again.('Terranova', same as {20005,9048}, 'Segaris', same as {20005,9047})
You will find that our planet Sutton, in the Gaian Prophecy system, now harbours a much more hospitable ecosystem.('Sutton', same as {20005,9051}, 'Gaian Prophecy', same as {20005,9019})
Again, great thanks to you for the part you played in this.
You need to place the satellites as precisely as possible.
Major deviations could result in incorrect data, and my experiment depends on them being accurate.
I would do it myself, but I have to monitor the data as it comes in.
First satellite deployed, although it's hardly worth mentioning as we need all three to gather useful data.
I read in your file that your family has roots in Aldrin. That colony certainly developed some interesting technology when they were isolated.
It's unfortunate that they're cut off again. It's almost as though the universe doesn't want us reunited.
I, for one, am glad to be on this side of the Gate and have access to Sol in its full glory. Maybe one day you too will even be granted access to Earth.
I find it interesting that you like spending so much time here. Most people prefer the relative peacefulness of Sol.
I never thought I'd see the day when Brennan's Triumph, the legendary epicentre of anarchy, was routinely patrolled by Terran forces.
Given the history, you can see why the former space command chose to establish a connection here, but there's only so much that polish can accomplish...
How are we looking with that last sat placement? We have things to do here and these readings don't look good. We need that sensor data.
I'm preparing an expedition to closely analyse the source of the anomalous readings.
I've set up a meeting point in Neptune. Meet me there ASAP.
Najia, what are you doing? Are you off daydreaming again?
I have already set up all the instruments and now I'm only waiting for you.
Hurry up! We don't have all cycle!
Have you not read my message? I clearly stated the importance of this task!
We do have a higher margin of error with placing this one, as we can compensate for any deviation with the subsequent satellites.
We need to be more precise with positioning the second satellite.
Exact positioning is of the utmost importance for this one, to get the optimal performance required for this experiment!
Please return to the deployment area.
Exact placement is critical. You are outside the area we need it deployed in.
This is absolutely critical. Slowly approach your area for optimal placement.
No, no, no! This is not deployed at the correct location!
Do I have to do everything myself?
You have deployed the wrong thing! Satellites are what we need!
Please return to the mission area and proceed with satellite deployment!
It's critical that we stay on schedule, so please use your Travel Drive.

Dear Sir slash Madam slash Other strike out if not appropriate. The Federal Industry and Infrastructure Administration has received your request to terraform in Black Hole Sun and are pleased to tell you that the required permits have been granted. We wish you the best of success on your undertaking.("terraform" and "Black Hole Sun" should sound like they came from separate recordings that were badly stitched together by an automated text-to-speech system)

Dear Sir slash Madam slash Other strike out if not appropriate. The Federal Industry and Infrastructure Administration is pleased to see your undertaking going well. We have authorised the release of the associated grant of zero credits immediately and advise you to spend it prudently.("pleased" "well" and "zero" should sound like they came from separate recordings that were badly stitched together by an automated text-to-speech system)

Dear Sir slash Madam slash Other strike out if not appropriate. The Federal Industry and Infrastructure Administration is pleased to see that your undertaking completed on budget. We look forward to working with you again in the future.("pleased" and "on budget" should sound like they came from separate recordings that were badly stitched together by an automated text-to-speech system)

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 4 / Terran Secret Service Contact
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 4
page.t: Now, I would like to talk to you about this so-called 'Project Genesis'. That's the codename of a top-secret operation that the Segaris Pioneers are cooking up.
We certainly know more about it than they would like, but we remain in the dark when it comes to their ultimate goal.
We do know that it involves a facility in their space with an unknown purpose.
Fortunately for us, there seems to have been an incident and the station was evacuated until repairs could be carried out.
This is a short-lived opportunity to gather intel. As such, we've taken action to inject false security documents into a Pioneer database.
Congratulations, operative. You're now a qualified Pioneer engineer, first class.
You're set to join one of their engineering teams to repair that facility. During the operation, gather whatever information you can, but use your discretion.
Just follow along with their instructions and you'll be fine.
The team is gathering in Neptune.
I'm sending you the information on where the team is gathering.
We believe the scientist in charge of Project Genesis is also heading up the repair team. Be sure to stay on his good side.
He's looking to acquire AGI technology? It seems we can add solicitation of illegal materials to his list of charges.
Carry on. We can't afford to make him suspicious now.
If our own intel is correct, you will likely find the dealer in the bar.
I'm quite sure this sensor net is also used to keep tabs on Terran Protectorate activity in their sectors. Go ahead and repair it, but we may take action later.
Join the engineering team so you can potentially gain internal access.
This is a good opportunity to get detailed readings from the outside without arousing too much suspicion.
We're losing the comm link. What's going on?
I'm very glad to see you.
We were under the impression that you went AWOL, and launched an investigation into your disappearance.
I will update your personal dossier before you run into trouble.
I am hereby informing you that you are being recorded.
Reporting Cadet: Raibu Hariken, dispatched to observe Project Genesis.(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
(angry)(In Disbelief)The Segaris Pioneers are capable of moving stations?(Faction name same as {20203,2901})
I see. We will investigate this Boron.
Is there anything else to report? New intel on Project Genesis?(Project Genesis same as {30224,1})
(with pathos, as if recorded for a promo)Welcome, visitor, to pure and radiant Sol, bastion of peace and prosperity.
(with pathos, as if recorded for a promo)If you, too, want to protect this utopia and the stars beyond, then do not hesitate.
(with pathos, as if recorded for a promo)The Solborn Militia welcomes any and all volunteers to join the...
(a bit stilted, sounds as if recorded separately)... foreign auxiliaries \(subject to qualification\)...
(with pathos, as if recorded for a promo)... and contribute their expertise to help maintain the safety of the Gate network.
(with pathos, as if recorded for a promo)Remember: we are the shield wall of civilisation, and together, we shall overcome.
(as if looking up from her work)Ah, another foreign recruit for the defence effort.
(as if briefly deliberating)I'm assigning you as support for cadet Shinamon.
(warningly)From now on, you act under the mandate of Earth.
(as if turning her attention back to her work)Follow orders and High Command will look upon you favourably.
(smiling to herself)I figured you two would jump at this opportunity.
(giving military speech)Militia squadrons and foreign auxiliaries.
(giving military speech)Those of you who were not lucky enough to be born on Terran soil, let me hereby welcome you formally into the ranks of the first and last defenders of the Gate network.
(giving military speech)And to those who are Solborn, or even Earthborn ...
(giving military speech)... to resist the temptation of heroism and put the defence of our sanctuary first is a sign of providence and true courage.
(giving military speech)By coming here, you have already made Earth proud.
(giving military speech)Captain, the ball is in your court.
There appears to be a Nav Beacon suspiciously close to our outpost.('Nav Beacon' same as {20201,20801})
A Nav Beacon with no apparent owner and purpose.('Nav Beacon' same as {20201,20801})
Investigate, but keep quiet about it.
I'm afraid we will have to postpone your secret mission.
Our scanners have picked up an approaching Xenon vessel.
Saddle up and join the defences.
We have an incoming Xenon strike force.
(lecturing)This sector is vital to the defence of Sol, and the entire Gate network.
(reassuringly)Given time, the Antigone Republic will certainly see the benefits of our protection.
(showing cracks in her composure)Chikisho, that bumbling buffoon is about to waltz right into our mine field.
(again with determination)Any squads in the vicinity?
(stress 'without')Quickly, slow down that ship without injuring its crew.
(stress 'cannot')We cannot have another diplomatic meltdown this soon.
(towards someone in her office)And get me the Chief Secretary on the line, pronto!
Let me be absolutely clear, in case that trespasser's speech got to you.
You are not troublemakers, you are problem-solvers.
Our neighbours might not see it that way, but the network depends on people like you ...
... people like us, who won't hesitate to do what's necessary.
Now, I need you two on standby while I sort out this diplomatic mess.
As a reward for your commitment, let me paint you a bigger picture.

High Command may not like it, but if we continue to face the Xenon head-on, scouring the network with imposing fleets, heroically putting out fires wherever they flare up, we are bound to lose this war.
The Intervention Corps is indispensable, both as long arm of the Protectorate and winged saviour alike.
However, this eternal meat-grinder of clashing fleets cannot be a permanent solution.
To truly beat the Xenon in a war of attrition, it is paramount that we instead thwart their infrastructure wherever possible.
Those parasites are lurking at the edges of our sectors, avoiding our defences and siphoning off our resources.
I am putting you on scouting duty.
Report any sightings of Xenon infrastructure units directly to me.
... we can divert their forces, potentially leaving their infrastructure units unprotected.
Apologies, I just happened to be still listening in.
You may go ahead with your plan, but be warned.
The Xenon are not just simple machines. They're erratic, unpredictable, deadly.
(as if interrupted by static)... enemy movement ...
(as if interrupted by static)... all squads, return to base immediately!
Recruit, where on Earth have you been, and where is your squad-mate?
The entire sector is descending on us!
Do what you must. Use the station as cover; draw them into our turrets' lines of fire.
No matter what's coming at us, we will not budge!
(angry; stops herself from using an insult; stress 'doesn't')That pompous...! He can go where the sun doesn't shine!
(angry, with pathos)All squadrons, recruits, defenders of Sol!
(energetic, angry; 'Intervention' is shorthand for 'Intervention Corps')Show Intervention what we're capable of and eliminate those Xenon stragglers!
(a bit more somber)... even though this was considerably more than you initially signed up for.
I'll be contacting you individually to discuss our next steps once the dust has settled.
Until then, you will want to take some time off. Consider this an order.
(getting her bearings)All squadrons, regroup at the Sol Gate!
(intense)I'm adding you to the admission list to my headquarters.
(intense)We have a few things to talk about.
Recruit! It's good to see you're still in one piece.
Apologies for the harsh welcome earlier.
(stress 'cannot')Communications cut off as soon as you engaged those Xenon infrastructure units, and I cannot stand having no vision on my subordinates.
There's no need for a detailed report, recruit.
My staff have already extracted your ship logs the moment you arrived.
It is beyond dispute that what you have witnessed is of the utmost concern to the Protectorate, but that is only half of the reason why I called you here personally.
You have displayed unquestioning obedience and clarity of mind in the most stressful of situations, and distinguished yourself as a defender of Sol in even the darkest hours of our operation.
(gets a bit intense)I hereby raise you to the rank of special operative, and no, refusal is not an option.
(more lenient, reveals that she was tongue-in-cheek)But I might deign to answer some of your questions, if you have any. No classified subjects, though.
A cutting-edge operation to strengthen societal cohesion, or, if you believe Intervention, just another failed experiment.

When I originally pitched the idea, I was mostly concerned with creating a common cause for the disenfranchised of Sol, though drawing in foreign attention-seekers turned out to be a welcome side-effect.
After all, why would you care, stand up and fight for our beautiful system if you felt like a second-class citizen, or worse, an alien?
I suppose there are a few parallels to the Pioneers Initiative; another campaign that defied expectations in its own way.
Call it a hunch, but I'm sure you'll be able to see that for yourself very soon.
(deliberating)I suppose I do owe you an explanation.
('glorious' is meant sarcastically)Yes, I suspected that the glorious Intervention Corps would have their eye on us from the start, and I did recognise the captain of that transport ship immediately.
I do understand his perspective: a ragtag bunch of barely-citizens, would-be heroes and foreigners, defending Sol?
That sounds like a recipe for failure.
Still, I did not expect commander Lee to degrade himself and poke around right under our noses, only to spit on our efforts when he saw us stumble.
My department may not have much power in the grand scheme of things, but this will have consequences, believe me.
My analysts are not entirely sure about the exact order of events; for that, we would have to interrogate Shinamon himself, and he remains MIA.
Judging by your report, it seems he may have been abducted, but I have a suspicion that there's more to it than that.
I really should have read the signs beforehand; after all, predicting the movements of ally and enemy alike is core to my job here.
For some reason, Shinamon must have tried desperately to make a name for himself, to be inquisitive and proactive in every situation.

He also seemed to have eerie intuition regarding the Xenon; I can only guess that something in his childhood, surrounded by stories about the glorious Terran war against the machine scourge, must have sparked his imagination.
(a bit somber)Trying to understand that which cannot be understood might have been his downfall.
(sighs)That was an unfortunate confrontation to say the least.
We came close to a debacle, but I was ultimately able to smooth things over with the Secretary of the Antigone Republic.
When interacting with the rest of the Gate network, we will always attempt to show ourselves from our best angle, but make no mistake.
(intense)Earth will not allow herself to be abused, or threatened, ever again.
Well, I must say that I am hesitant to send you away again so soon, but since you're asking, there might indeed be something to help take your mind off these unfortunate events.
That is, if you think you're ready.
(unusually warm)For now, you leave through that door, and you recover.
(a bit more firmly)Once you feel ready, come and talk to me again.
I'm sure there will be ample opportunity to apply your very particular set of skills.
I see. No time to waste, right?
There are new developments you might be interested in.
Meet me once you can spare a moment.
Ah, yes, indeed. I recognise you might have... personal reasons for your interest, so it seems only prudent to offer you this assignment first.

Ever since you handed in your report, my people have been working tirelessly to find a connection between a number of intriguing events that have occurred in Sol over the course of the last few weeks.
The first incidents were barely out of the ordinary: high-tech traders missing cargo, manipulated delivery schedules, the occasional kidnapping and ransoming...
Then things began to ramp up: Top secret deliveries being raided, fake distress signals targeting our military trainees, sabotage on a grand scale.
And lately, more and more of these incidents involve the Xenon in some fashion.
We can no longer ignore the possibility of a major new threat to the Terran Protectorate.
Based on recent evidence, my people are fairly sure that our opponents are the infamous Yaki.
In a nutshell, they're pirates. Our data suggest that they originated as members of the Argon Federation. Another splinter group they couldn't keep under control.
The Yaki have always dabbled in dangerous technology, and they seem to have only doubled down on that alarming compulsion since we last had the pleasure of making contact.
Expect their ships to be heavily armed and highly manoeuvrable.
The objective is simple: Find out where these pirates are hiding, what their goals are, and whether they can be defeated.
Unfortunately, you will only be able to call upon limited support during your mission.
As an undercover operative, it is paramount that no direct connection can be drawn between you and the Terran Secret Service.
Once you leave Protectorate space, you're on your own.
I can provide some guidance to help you get started, but ultimately you will be the one making decisions under pressure.
(variant 1)Two of our cadets recently encountered an especially malicious distress signal trap that was presumably set by these Yaki.
(variant 2)You and cadet Shinamon recently encountered an especially malicious distress signal trap that was presumably set by these Yaki.
They seem to be targeting specific Terran ships for some reason. And since they're keen on eliminating anyone who follows their trail, that reason remains a mystery to us.
If we catch them in the act, that will tell us more about their objectives.

An Advanced Satellite("Advanced Satellite" same as {20201,20401}) should be able to pick up on all distress signals in the sector. My team will evaluate the data and point you towards potential discrepancies.
With your record, you will do just fine, operative. I will leave you to prepare.
Anywhere within this sector will be fine, operative.
Let's see here... two medical emergencies, and a harmless collision in the docking queue. Nothing out of the ordinary.
Patrols are already moving in to assist. Carry on with your task.
Beautiful, isn't it? Sol at peace, I mean. I hope we can keep it that way.
(smug)And here we are. You just have to know what to watch out for.
A civilian transport logged an unidentified vessel creeping about at the edges of the sector, refusing to answer when being asked for directions.
There's no mention of a patrol encounter, so that ship might still be out there. Judging by the logged trajectory, we may be able to make a strike in the next sector.
Interesting. We're getting dangerously close to Segaris Pioneers territory.
They're spread thin and rely on Terran trade. That makes them especially vulnerable to these pirate raids.
If I were a shadowy nemesis that wanted to strike the Protectorate where it's weakest, Pioneers space is where I'd begin.
No, there's something here. A faint signal my team can't quite pinpoint.
I believe a more in-depth search is in order.
That produced a result at least. If you keep this up, you'll be able to narrow down the signal's origin.
Move towards the new search area and try again.
I'll assign a local patrol to assist you right away. These pirates won't ambush us this time!
Your escort is ready and eager for a fight.
I'd love to take the time to commend you for your bravery, operative, but I'm afraid you'll have to continue on your quest right away.
A local trader just sent out a distress signal, and the pattern matches that of an earlier pirate attack. We're close to apprehending these intruders!
Seems you've arrived just in time. The reports are piling up in Pioneers territory, as we feared.
How odd. The trader reports that she was ordered to drop her cargo, but that nothing of value ended up being stolen, only a small amount of foodstuffs.
However, there's no time to dwell on that right now. This is as far as I can safely communicate with you, operative. From here on out, you're on your own.
One of their criminal spin-off enterprises, the infamous Beryll, was responsible for an AGI drone attack on Earth in recent history.
Welcome back to the Protectorate, operative.
I see you've made a new acquisition. If you dock it at our Headquarters, my team will take it apart and extract all the information relevant to your investigation.
Please step out of this monstrosity, operative. My team will take it from here.
I'm transmitting the decrypted navigational data to your mission interface.
And one more thing: Since you appear to be nearing the final stage of your investigation, I think you should travel in style.
It's time to drop the masquerade and display the full force of the Terran Protectorate.
("her" refers to a ship)You'll find her on the dock.
We've transferred a peculiar program from the Yaki ship to this one. It appears to manipulate the friend/foe identification in some manner.
This might come in handy when you reach your destination, but stay alert nonetheless.
(intrigued)So, what's the status of the investigation?
Take all the time you need. We can't afford to mess this up, or we'll be the laughing stock of the entire Protectorate.
(eager)Excellent! Then tell me, are these Yaki an organised threat to the Protectorate? Do they have a base of operations that we can target?
(excited)Outstanding work, operative! I will relay this intel to Intervention right away.
(smug)Those overblown grunts will finally see the importance of the work we do.("overblown grunts" meaning self-important military people)
If you want to participate, you'd better prepare for action.
Once the Protectorate forces are under way, I'll mark their position for you.
(relieved)I see. That conclusion does match our observations. These pirates behave far too erratically.
In that case, I will attempt to sway Intervention to tone down their war preparations and instead get an anti-pirate task force under way.
(proud)Again, excellent work, operative. You've done Sol a great service.
(somber)My only regret is that we haven't found out what happened to Cadet Shinamon.
(warningly)Don't get ahead of yourself. This matter is far too important to jump to conclusions.

(variant 1; "Intervention is shorthand for the "Intervention Corps")Intervention let me know that the ship that's been anchoring in front of our HQ is not actually an attempt at intimidation, but simply a decommissioned heap of scrap.

(variant 2; "Intervention is shorthand for the "Intervention Corps")Intervention has gracefully provided us with a military asset, should we deign to support their upcoming operation. A decommissioned model by the looks of it.
It may require a few finishing touches to become fully functional again, but I'm sure you can make use of it.
I'll transmit the ship's location to you. Consider it a reward for your efforts.
Operative, the Intervention Corps just signalled that their fleet is approaching the Yaki base.
If you wish to contribute to the war effort and reap the spoils, now is the time to engage.
Excellent work, operative! Commander Lee has personally requested a commendation for your efforts. That smug little rat.
He also insisted that you be the first to... rummage around in the battlefield debris, to put it politely.
Coming from him, that almost sounds like an exclusive honour. You may find a few useful pieces of scrap out there.
I'll mark the location for you.
(serious)It has come to my attention that I may have chosen my subordinates... poorly.
(serious)Consider your contract terminated. And, should you enter Protectorate space again, the same will apply to you.
Operative, this is an emergency! A massive Xenon assault is approaching the Sol Gate!
I need you to reinforce the defences, now! If you still have an ace up your sleeve, this is the time to play it!
(Solemn)Through your work on the Xenon front, you have proven yourself to be a valuable asset to the Terran cause.
We might have another task for you. This one will require a somewhat softer touch, though.
Having someone in our corner who is familiar with diplomacy and back-room deals will be critical to this operation's success.
Our agents have been watching an analyst going by the name of Dal Busta.
He is currently negotiating on behalf of the Hatikvah Free League.
Get in contact with this Busta character and get acquainted with the political situation outside the Sol system.
(CovOps Chapter 1 - Secret Service Contact Voice Lines)
(Solemnly)We approach you with this operation because you have proved yourself to be a loyal and capable ally to the Terran people.
While it would be tempting to focus solely on the Xenon threat, neglecting other dangers would be foolish.
(angry)Yes, we must never forget the Argon betrayal!
The Argon Federation destroyed the Torus, thereby significantly weakening Earth's defences.
(Getting worked up)This craven terrorist act killed Terran citizens, and caused damage to our government costing trillions!
(Even more angry)It was both a blow to Terran citizens' morale, and a humiliation on the grander political stage!
(More calm, matter of fact)Now, more than ever, we need to project strength in the face of a shifting universe.
The majority of our resources are tied up in the ongoing campaign against the Xenon.
