(4/6)I mean, sure, we could set the Vigor Syndicate on you again, throw waves and waves of hired gunmen at you until you are dead - and you would die, eventually!
(5/6)But why should we? It is costly and unpredictable.
(6/6)And by the time you are permanently done for, knowledge of this place might have spread throughout the entire universe, and we cannot risk that.
(1/5)Yes, so how about we offer you an unofficial position in this enterprise?
(2/5)You are here now. That means clearly the Vigor Syndicate leadership is slipping.
(3/5)You could be the change of management we have been looking for.
(4/5)Of course, we would pay you. Handsomely!
(5/5)And who knows, if we get along well, we might even allow you to buy an Astrid-class ship of your own...
(1/7)You know what?(salesman pitch style and tone)
(3/7)Take a look around this ship!(salesman pitch)
(4/7)Make sure to really take in all of the luxurious details!(salesman pitch)
(5/7)The exquisite wood panelling - that is authentic wood, by the way, none of that synthetic rubbish - and the marble flooring!(salesman pitch)
(6/7)Really think about what your next steps will look like. You could rise to the top with us!
(7/7)When you have made up your mind, speak with us again, and we will set everything in motion!
(1/5)This ship sure is something, is it not?(affectionate)
(2/5)Oh, the magnificent opulence of it all!
(3/5)That'll make anyone want to keep their mouth shut, right?(tempting the player)
(4/5)We deserve to be on the top, and with all your good work so far, you clearly deserve to be rewarded, too.
(5/5)What do you say - are you in?
(2/5)So, does that mean you refuse to fall in line?!(still confused)
(3/5)You will not take this from us!(angry)
(4/5)We built this empire fair and square, we deserve this!(petulant)
(5/5)We own Avarice and its people!(angry, stressing "own", "Avarice" same as {20005,9033})
(2/5)It appears the blueprints to our Protectyon storage facility have just been stolen!(upset)
(4/5)We will make sure your life becomes a living hell, no matter the cost!(threatening)
(1/5)Very well.(calm and satisfied by the choice)
(2/5)We can't say it surprises us, given what we have to offer, but we are relieved nonetheless.
(3/5)I will transfer the payment of credits momentarily, as agreed.
(4/5)As I mentioned before, we are looking to replace the Vigor Syndicate as our right hand.
(5/5)We will get in touch again shortly!
Come aboard to speak to us in person!
It is good to have you on our side!
You should have fallen in line when you still had the chance!
(1/4)We have contacted our Vigor Syndicate intermediary, but they do not seem to be receptive to the idea of a change in leadership.
(2/4)In order to facilitate a smooth transition of power between the Syndicate and yourself, you should demonstrate that you, yourself, are not one to be messed with.
(3/4)And what better way is there to do just that, than to kill their leader?
(1/3)Oh, and you also need to clean up your own loose ends.
(2/3)Now, I don't know who you have worked with so far, but if there is anyone out there that could expose the company and its secrets, they need to be dealt with.
(2/5)We have negotiated terms, and they agreed that you are to be instated as our new security force in these parts of the network.
(3/5)In addition, we have arranged for a significant amount of their assets to be transferred to you, to make the transition as seamless as possible.
(4/5)It also seems like you kept true to your word, and nothing damaging has leaked to the outside.
(2/3)We promised you the chance to become part of a very exclusive group of people, if you did your job well.
(3/3)Which you did. So, come and talk to us about buying an Astrid-class ship, if you are interested!
Are you here to buy an Astrid-class ship?
(2a/2)I have just commissioned the closest wharf!(if wharf available)
(2b/2)I will be in touch to facilitate the transfer.(if wharf not available)
(1/2)(When it finished building)You are now the proud owner of an Astrid-class ship.
You double crossed us? After all that power we handed you?
You surprise me; I overestimated you. We will all walk away from this the poorer.
(2/2)No way! This is a highly exclusive item we are talking about here. We won't just mass produce her like that!(agitated)

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 14 / Syndicate Enforcer
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 14
page.t: (reaction to friendly fire)Hey, will you stop firing?
(reaction to friendly fire)You're wrecking my shields!
(reaction to friendly fire)Why are you shooting at me?
(* Gamestart Narration * - Pirate DLC GS 1 / Syndicate Runner)
(line 1 is spoken by a different character)

(squad leader, making conversation with a subordinate, talking to the player at first, start with a chuckle, "runner" means "courier who transports illegal wares" and refers to the player who can be male or female, last word of the sentence that cuts off was supposed to be "said", checks herself with a small harrumph and assumes a commanding attitude before saying "Hey, everyone")Who said transporting this stuff doesn't pay, just because we've legalised it? Isn't that right, runner? A few more of these contracts, and you'll be swimming in credits. Letting us in on the deal was the smartest move you could have made, by the way. Finally, someone who respects the work we do. Obey the rules, and you've got nothing to fear, is what the boss always... oh. Hey, everyone, drop point coming up, get back in formation!
Come on, don't make this difficult, Britson. You're the one who broke the rules.(confident, routinely, talking to male)
Okay, one last time: no illegal wares.(firmly, spelling it out word for word, talking to male)
Oh, quit whining. We're not taking anything that isn't already ours. You weren't supposed to get this far in the first place.(dismissive, talking to male)
Of course I know that, idiot. It's how the business is run. Our lives are all just business, and you've made a miscalculation. Now drop your cargo.(stern, condescending, talking to male)
(1/2)Not part of the plan, not part of the plan!(surprised, panicking slightly, to herself)
(2/2)The boss will be so mad...(frustrated, to herself)
Hey, you! This is Syndicate business! Stay away or else!(commanding, to the player)
Hey, runner! Keep out of this, or I'll personally make sure you lose your licence!(commanding, to the player, "runner" means "courier who transports illegal wares")
(1/2)Libaras, you still there? Gerra? Where is everyone?(strained, a bit breathless, addressing her subordinates, read "Where is everyone?" with urgency, like an exclamation)
(2/2)Lowlifes! I'll tear you to pieces!(to the player and their ally)

(1/2, slightly bored, "runner" means "courier who transports illegal wares"; talking to the player, who is her subordinate, in all 302871XX lines unless stated otherwise)All right, runner, let's get this over with. Head for the station, make your delivery, get paid, blah blah.
(2/2, slightly bored)We'll keep an eye on you... and any suspect traffic, of course. No need to worry while you're with us.
(slightly annoyed, "Aurora station" houses the "Aurora Casino" {20103,2701})You're off course. Aurora station is this way.
(very annoyed)You're testing my patience. Get back in line, and don't make me repeat myself!
(angry, commanding, talking to subordinates about the player)Looks like this one needs to be taught a lesson!
(dismissive, talking to subordinates)Hold your fire, everyone. They got the message.
(1/2a, player got caught, disappointed, dismissive)That was the stupidest attempt I've ever seen. You're out of the game.
(1/2b, player got away, disappointed, dismissive)Big mistake, running away like that.
(2/2, disappointed, dismissive, stretch "aaaaaall")When you come crawling back, you're starting all the way down at the bottom.

(1/3, talking to female manager, switching to broadcast, dismissive, the "runner" is the player, "Aurora station" houses the "Aurora Casino" 20103,2701)Aurora station? Our runner just made a... run for it. Looks like they weren't up to the task.
(2/3, talking to female manager, amused)What's that, compensation? Oh, you haven't lost anything yet, believe me. Unless you want to take this up with the boss?
(3/3, talking to female manager, smug)Yeah, that's what I thought. Sayonara!
(1/2, talking to subordinates, mischievous)Well, well, well, look what we have here.

(2/2, talking to subordinates, mischievous, "Aurora" is shortened for "Aurora Casino" {20103,2701}, "Syndicate" is shortened for "Vigor Syndicate" {20203,3301})Another trader en route to Aurora, and they're not flying Syndicate colours. Such a shame... for them.
(1/4, creepy, menacing, talking to other ship called "Unsinkable")Why hello there, "Unsinkable". What are you doing out here, in the dark, all alone?

(2/4, creepy, musing, talking to other ship, "Windfall" is a place, same as {20005,9057})Haven't you heard? Nothing but scum and villainy in Windfall these days. Personally, I wouldn't take a single step outside without protection.
(3/4, creepy, musing, talking to other ship)Wouldn't it be terribly inconvenient, if, say, one of your engines suddenly caught a couple of stray, high-velocity rounds...
(4/4, creepy, musing, talking to other ship)Imagine getting stranded like that. And the distress call operators are all so very, very busy right now...
(1/2, cheering, gleefully, to a male subordinate)Ha! They dropped a bunch of crates! Hey, Gerra, go and pick them up!
(2/2, warning, to the player again)Not you, runner. Keep staying on course. And be happy you're on our side.
(1/3, snide, talking to other ship pilot who just received docking permission)Permission denied! Out of the way, lowlife!
(2/3, smug, talking to the player again)See? That's how it's done. That trash has nothing on us.
(3/3)Now, go and get those wares delivered. You have priority docking permission.
(encouraging, patient)Smooth landing. Now, open your trade interface and deliver the highlighted wares.
(still patient, but slightly annoyed, emphasise "entire")Yes, that's part of it, but you need to deliver the entire amount. Come on.
(1/3, satisfied)All goods delivered. Nice work, runner.

(2/3, tongue-in-cheek, well-meaning, "Syndicate" is shortened for "Vigor Syndicate" {20203,3301})Now, you're not formally with the Syndicate just yet, but maybe you've picked up on the proper manners by now. Act the part, and nobody will bother you.
(3/3, tongue-in-cheek, well-meaning)See you out there! And stay on the same team... for your own sake.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 15 / VIG Leader
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 15
page.t: (1/3)(angry)I don't know who you guys are, or where you got wind of this beacon, but you had better forget about it before I get to you.
(3/3)(angry)This is the moment where you should engage your travel drive and start running for your lives.
(1/3)(angry)You there, approaching the Wreck!(calling out to the player)
(2/3)(angry)The Vigor Syndicate confiscated the Erlking fair and square, and we do not allow passers-by to approach.
(3/3)Get away from our property, right now, or suffer the consequences!
(1/2)(angry)By deciding to ignore our directions, you have chosen death!
This is VIG base to approaching ship.
Let me give you some free advice: turn back while you still can.
(1/5)What do you...?(monotone, then interrupts herself when she recognises the player character)
(2/5)Oh... it's you! I would not have thought you were brave enough to return to our territory.(intrigued)
(3/5)Or perhaps it is not bravery... stupidity?
(4/5)No, clearly you did not get to this point by being stupid.
(5/5)I don't much care what you did to the Northriver Company suits, but it must have been good.(chuckling)
(1/2)Ah, so you want to pay us to back off?
(2/2)Very well, I will relay the message, and your credits.(pleased)
(1/4)The Vigor Syndicate recognises that you mean business.
(2/4)The new management feels that it is not worth pursuing this matter any further.
(3/4)Your monetary contribution has gone a long way, as well.
(4/4)Be assured, that as far as we are concerned, this conflict is resolved!

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 16 / Mad Scientist
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 16
page.t: (introduction, talking only to the player in all 3XX lines, passionate researcher voice with *occasional* hints of German accent mixed in (th->z, w->v, c->z) when she gets excited, for example "do you have ze items?", "it vill be magnifizent")Hey there, how can I help you?

(introduction, emphasize sentient, life, technology)I'm Corin King, researcher of sentient life technology. Self-employed, for the time being. Those naysayers at Jinko-Tekina will eat their words when they realise what I've achieved!

(ask about research)I'm researching a sentient on-board computer. One that predicts, learns and loves; imagine that! Safe travels, deadly precision, and a sophisticated companion to boot! My invention will revolutionise our lives - with your help, of course.
(ask about progress - between missions)With the parts you have delivered, I think I'm ready for the next great breakthrough! Once I've finished putting them all into place, that is.
(ask about progress - mission active)I'm still waiting for those parts. When do you think you'll have them ready?
(ask about progress - no mission offer available)I'm still working out the details, contemplating the implications, that sort of thing. When I need assistance, I'll ask.
(ask about progress - first mission offer available)Perfect timing! I've just about finalised the set-up for my first experiment, and it seems like I'm short of a few crucial items.
(ask about progress - mission offer available variant 1)No, no, no, this has all gone horribly wrong! We'll have to try a different approach.
(ask about progress - mission offer available variant 2)The last attempt was a major setback, a real disaster, but we can't give up now!
(mission accepted variant 1)Hurry, hurry, I'm itching to get started on my next experiment!
(mission accepted variant 2)Sweet progress! I can't wait to get started!
(mission failed variant 1)How disappointing. I was really counting on this delivery.
(mission failed variant 2)What a disaster! This is going to delay my work significantly.
(mission complete variant 1)Excellent! I will have this tech up and running in no time.
(mission complete variant 2)Magnificent! That's just what I need for the next stage.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 17 / Kriss Mellerd
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 17
page.t: Greetings, Yololios Sanduras Rusiris XI.(speak XI as "the eleventh")
Welcome to Woodworm Scrubs!(same as {20102,2301}, prison station name)
Or should I say, welcome back!
(1/8)I imagine that you are wondering if our little arrangement falls into line with official Ministry business.
(2/8)You should know that I used to fly with a pirate crew.
(3/8)I still have contacts there, which makes me quite an asset for the Ministry.
(4/8)They rewarded me with a job bossing around Ministry employees, who look at me as if I have no clue about what I'm even doing here.
(5/8)It is an uphill battle on both fronts, but we are fighting the good fight.
(6/8)You know? Ending unregulated illicit trade and all that.
(7/8)All I'm saying is, there is merit in disclosing any illegal activities that you might know about.
(8/8)The Ministry is still extremely interested and pays generously.
(1/2)I don't imagine that you requested our meeting to receive personal gratitude, so let's talk business.
(2/2)What can I do you for?(Pun as she runs a prison)
(3/6)Yes, I believe we can come to an arrangement.
(4/6)I'll make sure you disappear from our systems.
(5a/6)The Ministry will lose all criminal records it might have, ridding you of any negative reputation you have built up.
(5b/6)The Ministry will lose some criminal records it might have, ridding you of part of the negative reputation you may have built up.
(2/9)(On a call)Yes, I need to call in a favour.
(3a/9)(On a call)A former customer needs to disappear from our systems.
(4a/9)(On a call)I've sent you the file.
(3b/9)(On a call)I have a shady character looking for employment.
(4b/9)(On a call)Eager to work, maybe, but not much of a profile yet.
(8/9)(On a call)I'll call you later about that other case.
(1/3)You'd rather have a long-term income over a quick buck?
(2/3)I'll try to arrange something, but don't get your hopes up.
(3/3)I am not hiring, but let me talk to a third party who might be interested in you.
(1/4)I'm sorry, there is no interest in the market.
(2/4)The groups work on a trust basis and prefer to employ people they have a history with, or select for themselves.
(3/4)The fact that you are actively looking to be employed raises some red flags.
(4/4)Let's get you a proper reward for a job well done and have you on the way.
(2/4)I would have thought he'd send someone more trustworthy.
(2/3)So he sent you to gain access for your future heist?
(3/3)I suppose you want a moment with that terminal. Go ahead.
(3/3)I suppose you want a moment with that terminal. Go ahead.(animation variation)
(1/10)Are you expecting me to prevent you from stealing classified Ministry property?('Ministry' same as {20203,704})
(2/10)Let me clear up your confusion; I don't care.
(3/10)Just go back to your buddies and tell them the gates are wide open.
(4/10)Maybe leave out the fact that I'm expecting them.
(5/10)Do what you need to do to bring the old man right here.
(6/10)It all needs to go according to his little plans.
(7/10)He will be rattled enough by what we've already accomplished.
(8/10)He might even have a hard time keeping up that calm attitude of his.
(9/10)You can escape with the Ministry ship and we can talk about your rewards once I get hold of him.
(10/10)Now pull that switch and be done with it.
I expect you'll find your way out.
If you'll excuse me, I have another guest to attend to.
(1/6)Thank you for leading the old man, and his crew of clowns, right to my doorstep.
(2/6)Crossing them off the Ministry's list will do wonders for my career advancement.
(3/6)You just stumbled into this whole affair, so I will offer you a one-time chance to get out of this.(if not betrayed plan to Mellerd)
(4/6)All you have to do is dock at my ship and hand over the pirates you are currently harbouring.
(5/6)You won't be able to keep the ship, but I promise I will make it up to you!
(6/6)This is what we agreed on. Dock, and our deal will be complete!(if betrayed plan to Mellerd)
(1/3)So, you have chosen to go down with the sinking ship?(not surprised)
(2/3)Ah well, it's all the same to me!(indifferent)
(3/3)One less loose end for me to tie up later!
(1/2)No, I cannot let you get away!(frustrated)
No, please! I don't want to die!(when Mellerd's capital ship is blowing up)
(1/4)Step away from the ship now.(matter of fact)
(3/4)Allow me to take the prisoners away.
(4/4)As we agreed, a brand-new Ministry ship for you.
(2/4)The Ministry wants the pirates alive, to make an example of them.
(3/4)So, I would preferably like to get my hands on the old fool alive.
(1/4)Thank you. The Ministry will take it from here.
(2/4)I will make sure your record is updated to reflect your change of heart.
(3/4)Rest assured that the prisoners will be subject to a fair trial before being transferred to an on-world prison.
(4/4)Be proud of a job well done.
(1/3)I would have preferred to have taken him alive.(if pirate ship destroyed)
(2/3)But then again, it doesn't really matter that much.(if pirate ship destroyed)
(3/3)I still have the others to show for our efforts.(if pirate ship destroyed)
(1/3)You have done the Ministry a great service.(praising player)
(2/3)Best keep your nose reasonably clean from now on.
(3/3)Unfortunately, I do not have enough sway in the Ministry to offer complete impunity to associates. But I'm sure I'll get there...(slightly apologetic)
(4/4)You even get to keep the ship as an advance, how about that?
I need you to do one more thing before I pay you.
What? Are you trying to fool me? The deal is off if you don't bring me the right ship!(if player delivers wrong ship)
No, I don't want to die!(scared, when character dies)
(1/4)Hah, that is a very unconventional way of solving this particular conundrum.(slightly amused, when player ship destroyed)
(2/4)But I guess I can make this work, and still sell this as a victory to the Ministry.(more thinking out loud than talking to player)
(3/4)Two down, two more to go.(Matter of fact)
(4/4)Take out the Arcadian Endeavour's engines, and I will forget the role you played in all this!

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 18 / Nomad Researcher
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 18
page.t: (1/16)Log. #412. This is Dr. Doran Viv reporting from research station Hadad.(matter of fact, #412 as in "number four one two")
(2/16)It has been seven years since the cataclysmic initial event reshaped the Avarice system.("Avarice" same as {20005,9033})
(3/16)Although I previously reported that progress on the matter of the Tide phenomenon has been so slow as to be essentially imperceptible, I now believe that we have achieved a breakthrough.
(4/16)As established in preceding logs, we suspect that whatever instigated the Tide phenomenon also weakened the surrounding fabric of space-time.
(5/16)Whether that cataclysmic event, and the appearance of these anomalies, is in some way linked to the ongoing Jump Gate shutdown, has not yet become clear.
(6/16)What is evident, though, is that not all of the anomalies have the same properties.
(7/16)At first glance they all appear to be unstable, and their destinations seem completely unpredictable when an anomaly is traversed.

(8/16)Our big breakthrough was realising that the energy released by the Tide can interact with a specific anomaly to temporarily stabilise it, which fixes the destination to reliably travel between the same two systems.

(9/16)This in itself is already an invaluable insight, as it suggests that, provided you apply enough energy, the properties of an anomaly can change. Unfortunately, our technology is nowhere near capable enough yet.(barely contained excitement)
(10/16)What we found on the other side of the anomaly is so much more immediately significant: a completely unconnected system, devoid of life!
(11/16)In a fit of unexpected whimsy, I could not help but name said system "Leap of Faith".
(12/16)Astonishingly, this solitary system houses an abandoned artificial structure. We were able to extract a condensate from it which reacts violently when exposed to the Tide's advancing energy.
(13/16)We believe that with some further research we could utilise this material to create some shielding which would protect against the most destructive effects of the Tide.
(14/16)While we don't yet know the nature of said alien structure, or how the stable anomaly works exactly, these findings undoubtedly have the potential to change life in this system for the better.
(15/16)The impact of the last Tide must have destroyed some communication equipment on the station. I am having trouble establishing contact, but repairs are currently underway.
(16/16)I cannot wait to share this discovery with the wider scientific community.

page.title: Argon Tutor - Flight School
page.descr: Lines for Argon Tutor for Flight School
page.t: I'll need to set everything up. Please give me a minute.
Ah, you knew how to do that already.
You're not in actual danger, by the way. We're only simulating damage to your ship.
You can close this menu now.
Close the map when you're done.
Close this menu to move on.
And that's it for this lesson.
Now.(as in "do it now", comes some time after an instruction)
Hi. I'm Jace Winger, your flight instructor for today. We'll be running through the full lesson plan, but if you're already familiar with some of the basics you can talk to me about skipping ahead.
Before we begin I need to perform a few routine physical tests. Regulations, you know.(say the last sentence slightly apologetically)
Please move your head as far up or down as you can.
OK, now please walk a few steps.
And now do a few jumping jacks, please.
Great! You seem to be in good physical shape, so we can move on to your flying lessons.
We'll start by using the transporter room outside to go to the docking bay.
From here you need to embark and take the controls.
Let me know how you want to proceed.
You are cleared for undocking. Proceed.
Use the steering controls to turn your ship.
Now use the strafing controls to move sideways or vertically.
OK. Before we continue, make sure that there's no obstacle right in front of you. I can't check from here so I have to trust you on this one...
When you're clear, gently accelerate forwards.
There's usually a speed limit inside docking areas, but you don't have to worry about exceeding it; the ship's computer will limit the speed for you.
You can also fly backwards. Try this now.
I see you found the strafe controls! That's great, but I do need you to use the steering controls now.
Now I need you to make sure that there really is nothing in front of you.
When you're ready, strap in and hit your ship's boost.
Your ship's sensors are all well and good, but sometimes it can be useful to get a more direct look at things.
First, look around your cockpit. There are many different kinds, but ship cockpits often provide a wide field of view outside the ship.
You can also look at your ship from the outside, with the magic of camera drones. Try it.
Fly around a bit to get a feel for how it behaves.
You can also cycle into a different external camera mode.
This also works on targets within range. For now, return to the normal cockpit view to move on.
You can even tell a camera drone to stay in a fixed location. Try this now.
The controls here behave a little differently. Play around with them now. Return to cockpit view to move on.

If you'd like to see what's in front of you with fewer obstructions you can turn off the HUD. You can even make the cockpit practically invisible to you. Is there anything camera drones can't do? Try both now.(emphasis on "can't")

If you'd like to see what's in front of you with fewer obstructions, you can even make the cockpit practically invisible to you. Is there anything camera drones can't do? Try it now.(emphasis on "can't")
You can look at your ship from the outside, with the magic of camera drones. Try it.
This also works on targets within range.
The camera controls work just like in the other external view.
Return to cockpit view to move on.
You can even get a live stream of various places around the galaxy.
This mode automatically cycles between objects you have access to.
It starts out with your personal channel, which cycles through the objects you own.
Since you only own this one ship at the moment it's not very exciting yet.
I've unlocked another faction's channel as well.
You'll get access to these as you increase your rank with that faction.
You can either wait for the channel to automatically switch, or use the controls in the top right of the screen to do so yourself.
With these controls you can also lock a channel or object to keep the mode from switching.
Use the controls to cycle to the Wharf, then lock it in.
Feel free to stay in this mode for as long as you'd like.
Return to cockpit view to end this lesson.
Please fly out of the docking area now.
So, let's practice what you've learned so far.
I've prepared a little course for you.
Please fly close to each of the navigation beacons in turn.
Your next target will always be marked in orange.
Don't worry, you're not being timed.
Your ship also has a boost function.
Boosting drains your shields, so use it wisely.
You may also notice that it has set your speed to maximum. This is normal and will only persist until you change speed again. Some pilots even find it a convenient way to set their speed to maximum.
Your remaining shield energy is shown in the blue bar right below your crosshair.
You have a limited pool of boost energy; use it wisely.
Your remaining boost energy is shown on the speed bar, right below your crosshair.
This next thing is something you are going to be using a lot.
I've marked a remote location for you to fly to. Don't worry; I don't expect you to crawl there at your base speed.
First, please align your ship so that it points roughly towards the target.
Depending on your engine type, it may take a little time to get started.
Look at your speed bar, just below the crosshair.
You will keep accelerating for a while until you reach your ship's top travel speed.
Now that you've gathered some speed you'll notice that steering has become much harder.
This is why it's best to point your ship towards your destination before engaging Travel Mode.
Now turn off the mode, the same way you turned it on.
You are now coasting, which means a few things.
First, your ship is decelerating much more slowly than it normally would.
Second, steering is easy again. Give it a try now.
Third, you've probably noticed that your ship keeps flying in the same direction!
You can come to a stop much more quickly by actively decelerating. This automatically re-engages the safety limits on steering.
As for the travel direction, any strafe movement will revert that to the behaviour you're used to.
You can also drop out of Travel Mode more quickly, skipping the coasting phase.
Now wait until you've built up some speed.
Whenever you're ready, quickly drop out of Travel Mode. You can look at the distance marker on your objective to get a feeling for your ship's braking behaviour.
You've probably noticed other modes in the list when you activated this one.
Each mode has its special use, and only one mode can be active at a time.
Whenever you're ready, quickly drop out of Travel Mode.
Great. The next part will take place some distance from here, so let's take a break and let the autopilot do the hard work for now.
The autopilot automatically navigates to the current objective. It engages Travel Mode when appropriate, and makes use of gates, accelerators and highways.
It even avoids obstacles in the way. Well, mostly, which is why you still need to be at the controls.
If you're getting bored, you can disable the autopilot at any time and fly the rest of the way yourself.
You may notice that it sometimes turns Travel Mode off when everything seems wide open to you. The safeties are on a bit of a hair trigger, probably to keep insurance rates from skyrocketing...
There's a ship next to you. Its colour on your HUD indicates that it's not hostile.
Please select it as your target.
By the way, matching speed is even possible when both you and your target are in Travel Mode.
I've now activated your primary weapon.
The small dots that have just appeared indicate where the weapons are currently aiming. They will automatically track your current target, as long as it's close enough.
There are a handful of targets in front of you. Their HUD colour indicates that they are enemies.
Note that the HUD markers of some targets are smaller. These targets are currently outside your weapon range.
A new HUD element has appeared, right in the centre of the target. This is the aim-ahead indicator; it shows you where you need to aim, which is especially useful if the target is moving.
Slowly cycle through all the targets.
When a target outside your weapon range has been selected, you can see the weapon indicators becoming darkened. The aim-ahead indicator also changes its appearance.
Select the closest enemy target again and shoot at it until it's destroyed.
Keep destroying targets. You'll need to move closer in order to hit some of them.
If you look to the right of your crosshair, you will see bars next to your weapons that gradually fill up when you are firing. This is heat. It automatically dissipates when you stop firing.
Your weapons just overheated. You will not be able to fire until they've cooled to a safe temperature.

This target is much sturdier than the others. Look at the blue bar above the target. This is its shield strength. After a few seconds without damage it will begin to recharge. All shields work like this, including your own.
I've now activated your secondary weapon, a missile launcher. It's loaded with a type of guided missile that requires a target lock. Please select the target in front of you.
You can now see a lock being acquired. You may fire when ready.
The target has dropped something! Fly right at it to pick it up.
It's another type of missile. It has been automatically added to your ammunition storage.
Missile launchers have limited ammunition. You can see the number of remaining missiles to the left of your crosshair.
Let's go into more detail about your weapons.
We'll focus on the highlighted weapon configuration section.
Each installed weapon has its own row.
The squares in each row show you which weapon groups that weapon is a part of.
You can assign any weapon to any weapon group.
You can also change the ammunition that's loaded into your missile launchers.
Try it if you like. Close the menu to move on.
You can quickly cycle through your configured weapon groups.
Please activate each primary group at least once.
You can also cycle through the available ammunition for any active missile launcher here. Try this now.
It takes a little time for the new missile type to be loaded into the launcher.
This happens more slowly if there are multiple weapons cooling down at the same time.
You can also use the container magnet, that way it'll come to you!
The line you see is your on-board computer's estimate of the heat you'll gain from firing that weapon.
It'll turn red if firing another shot will make your weapon overheat.
Time to learn how to defend yourself.
Some are darker than the others.
Those are behind something, and can't be hit with your weapons right now.
Look at the curved blue bar below your crosshairs.
I'm going to demonstrate damage to your shields.
Use the highlighted buttons to assign each weapon to its own group.
The target in front of you has strong shields.
Your ion weapon is especially effective against shields.
Switch to it and fire until the target's shields are down.
Now switch to your plasma weapon and finish it off.
This target here is small and agile, quite tricky to hit with a plasma weapon.
Switch to your beam and shoot it down.
You probably noticed that this ship also has turrets.
You have a plasma turret and a beam turret.
You can arm and disarm them using the buttons on the right.
They're set to Defend, which means they will fire at whoever attacks you.
Let's go through the other modes.
"Attack all Enemies" means that the turret will independently choose a suitable target in range.
"Attack only capital ships", "Attack only fighters" and "Shoot only missiles" work similarly, but only allow a subset of targets.
"Attack capital ships first", "Attack fighters first" and "Shoot missiles first" prioritise a subset of targets, but other targets are allowed.
Set the beam turret to only shoot missiles, and the plasma turret to attack capital ships first.
Just sit still, and watch your turrets defend you.
"Attack my current enemy" makes the turret fire at whatever you have selected, as long as it's hostile.
"Mining" may be obvious... it makes the turret fire at asteroids within range.
There's a capital ship nearby. Please approach it.
Get as close as possible to its surface.
You can get much closer than that.
Don't be nervous! Get even closer.
(laugh a little before speaking)Okay, that was a bit too close. But as you can see, small collisions are no big deal.
You are now flying relative to the ship, thanks to special flight assistance software. This works for most things that are bigger than medium-sized ships.
No matter what the capital ship does, you will move along with it.
This is especially useful for combat, as well as for docking or undocking.
I've set up some targets on the ship's surface. Please destroy them.
Try to use the ship's surface as cover wherever possible. Your strafe thrusters are useful here.
Now fly away from the ship's surface until it leaves you behind.
All right, now come to a stop.
Fly to the next objective. You may use Travel Mode or the autopilot if you like.
This wreck has something inside it. Your ship will not fit so you're going to have to get out of your ship and do a space walk.
Move a little closer to the indicated position and park your ship there.
Please get up and leave the ship in your space suit.
You've probably noticed that you keep moving in the same direction. That's because space suits don't have flight assistance and are limited to Newtonian flight.
Any directional input, whether it's strafing, accelerating or decelerating, will push you in that direction. I'll let you try it out for a little while.
Try to come to a stop using these inputs.
Tricky, isn't it? Luckily there's an easier way. Try it now.
Much better. I think you're ready for some manoeuvring. Please fly inside the wreck using the indicated entry point.
There's a lockbox here! What a lucky find. Please activate your weapon and carefully shoot off all the locks.
Congratulations, you did it! You may keep the item for yourself after you've finished here.
You also have a repair tool. This tool works on most damaged objects, as long as they're not actually wrecked. This thing is beyond repair, though.
Please leave the wreck and return to your ship now.
You may have noticed the oxygen indicator, which is slowly going down. There's no need to worry about it; you will be back in your ship with plenty of time to spare.
The space suit is also equipped with a booster. You can use it now to reach your ship more quickly. Be careful, though. It's easy to overshoot or crash into your target that way.
To get back in, you need to make a docking request. Please do so now.
Now follow the green lights to the dock and fly inside.
Your space suit is equipped with a small hand laser. Please don't try to use it in fights with actual ships. You'd be pulverised immediately!
There's an access hatch, but it's malfunctioning. Look for a broken control panel and use your repair tool to fix it.
There's another broken control panel. Repair this one as well.
Ship weapons also work, but you have to be much more careful with those.
Lockboxes are fragile, and some even explode!
While the feeling of flying your space suit is fresh in your mind, let's try the same with your ship.
Please turn off flight assistance now.

You have access to two modules right now: a Pier for capital ships, and a Dock Module for smaller ships.
There are many more options, but you need to acquire their blueprints first.
You'll notice its colour sometimes changing between green and red.
If it's red then it's not in a valid location.
It may be outside of the plot, intersect with another module, or be in an exclusion zone.
We will learn about those in a moment.
Place this module anywhere inside the plot.
You can still change its position.
You can grab and drag any of the arrows to move the module along that axis.
Doing the same to one of the circles will rotate the module.
You can reset a module's rotation by interacting with it.
Ok, now select the other Dock Module.
As you move it around, you will notice that it can snap to the already-placed Pier.
You may also notice that you can't place it in the marked area in front of the Pier.
That is the so-called exclusion zone.
It needs to be free of other modules so that ships can dock.
Let's place a few more modules to make this a fully operational station.
First take a look at the Other Modules section.
There are a number of cheap connection modules that you can use to make your station look nice.
You don't have to use them, but feel free to do so during this lesson.
Now select a production module and place it.
All production modules turn certain resources into a product.
Except for this one, which stores solar power in Energy Cells.
Its output depends on the sector, your encyclopedia has the info you need.
There are also build modules, which work very similarly, but their products are ships and equipment.
Next we'll absolutely need a storage module.
There are modules for the different types of storage.
We only need container storage here, so place one of these.
Without it you won't have room for a workforce.
While productions can run automatically, actual workers increase their efficiency a lot.
You do need to keep them supplied with food and medicine, though.
By the way, if you're struggling to attract people to your station, a welfare module can go a long way to help.
It doesn't automatically come with any turrets, so let's add some now.
Interact with the defence module and select Edit Loadout.
This works exactly like loadouts for ships.
Add at least one turret and confirm the changes.
When you're satisfied, you can confirm your changes with the highlighted button.
Now we need to hire a builder ship.
The map is now in a special mode that focuses on these builder ships.
The one next to the other station is currently busy, but you can select the other one by interacting with it.
Next you need to make sure that the required resources will be delivered to this station's Build Storage.
If you expand this item you can see exactly what is needed.
And if you expand this one you can allocate funds for trade offers.
These will be seen by traders, who will then sell them to your station.
Of course, you can also deliver everything yourself.
But for now, simply accept the estimate and close this menu.
The builder ship will now move to your station and use the delivered resources, and its welder drones, to construct it according to your plan.
You can move or remove fully-built modules as well.
The builder ship will then deconstruct the module, placing the recovered resources back in the Build Storage.
So you've successfully built a station, now let's make it operate properly.
First off, you need a manager.
Dock at the nearby station and hire someone.
Now interact with your new station and select the Manager role.
Your new hire will now travel to the station and start working.
Almost every production module turns one or more resources into a product.
Your one requires Silicon and Energy Cells, and produces Silicon Wafers.
Select the mining ship and assign it to mine for the station.
It'll also want to buy certain resources, like Energy Cells, as well as sell its products.
So assign the two transport ships to trade for the station.
The station manager is now taking care of orders for these ships.
How well they do depends on the skill of the manager or the ship's pilot, whichever is better.
The miner will start to work straight away, but the traders can't.
Your station has no budget to buy resources.
Now put some money into the station account by moving the slider.
You can also simply accept the manager's estimate.
The manager is now going to use that budget to buy resources.
Profits from selling products also go into this account.
As soon as the manager exceeds the limit by a certain margin, any excess funds will automatically be transferred to your account.
While you're looking at the info menu we can also quickly cover Trade Rules.
You can set them up in the Global Orders menu, which you can also open with these handy buttons.
They let you control exactly who is allowed to trade with your station.
Now interact with the station and open the Logical Overview.
Here you can see a diagram of the station's production line, among other things.
To the left you can see the various resource wares in the station's storage.
Next to that are the productions.
This station only has one, but you can add many different ones.
The rightmost column shows the end products currently in storage.
There are many things that you can control from this menu.
You can override several automatic settings, or assign a Trade Rule specific to this ware.
It shows you a lot of detailed info, and you can pause the production from here.
You can also use this menu to set some wares to be traded without having a production module that needs or produces them.
Try to add Helium as a trade ware.
If you open the details you can see what it's about.
In this case, the problem is that your station doesn't have the right kind of storage for this ware.
You can remove it by deselecting it in the Select Trade Wares menu.
You've probably been wondering about the workforce "production", so let's open that now.
Each production module works better when it has people working in it.
The optimal amount depends on the type of production.
Workers require food and medicine, even when they're not working.
Keep them consistently supplied with these, or they're going to leave.
At the bottom you can see how the workforce is expected to change over time.
Growth mainly depends on the sector population, but plenty of living space and a well-maintained station help as well.
You can also build certain welfare modules to attract workers more quickly.
Here you can set target amounts for certain types of drones.
The manager will then create buy offers for drone components, and manufacture them once these arrive.
While most traders carry cargo drones of their own, giving the station a few as well can speed up trades with capital ships.
And I don't need to tell you why defence and repair drones might be useful, right?
And those are the foundations of station management.
Simply close the map to complete this tutorial.
Now we're getting into something for real enthusiasts!
You can find these in the Ship Dealership at any wharf or shipyard.
You can't mod small ships at shipyards, though, or capital ships at wharfs.
I've given you access to my personal database for this lesson.
To use them yourself later, though, you'll need to do some research of your own.
Expand any one of the entries to see details about what it does.
Each of these modifications requires certain rare materials.
It also costs a flat fee to install one, as listed in the top right.
Install a modification of your choice now, using the highlighted button.
You can now see its actual properties at the top.
If you dismantle it, you will get the rarest part back - the Nanoweave in this case.
The other materials, as well as your money, are spent, though.
If you've got the other materials to spare, you can keep re-trying until you get the mod exactly how you like it.
And that's how you modify ships!
You may play around here as long as you like, we'll move on when you close the menus.
Modding your ship is far from an exact science.
With these kinds of non-standard parts you never know exactly what you're going to get.
But you can see the range of what to expect.
This type of chassis modification requires something called a Nanoweave, as well as some Nividium Crystallite.
Today we'll cover another important topic: missions.
As a reminder, the current objective of the active mission is always shown in the message ticker.
Right now the objective does not have a specific target.
I've now set one of the ships in front of you as the mission target.
The yellow markings let you know which one it is.
I've now changed the mission target to a different ship.
A yellow arrow near your crosshair points in its direction.
It should be to the right of it.
Turn your ship until you see the mission target in front of you.
Mission targets are highlighted in the same yellow on the map.
And as you can see, there can be more than one at a time.
Targets don't always need to be objects, either.
Some missions give you a position or area in space, like this.
What the radius means really depends on the mission.
Maybe you need to find something somewhere in there, or are required to cover the entire area with satellites.
For now I just need you to fly to anywhere in that area.
This menu shows you any mission offers that you are aware of.
Some are broadcast widely, most are more local.
Select one of the mission offers.
You can now see its title, description, and objectives.
The map also temporarily shows you guidance for the mission you've selected.
You may have noticed that the mission area is no longer marked.
That's because you can only see guidance for one mission at a time, and accepting a mission automatically activates it.
This doesn't mean that inactive missions are paused.
You can still progress, and even complete them, while they're inactive.
And of course you can choose which mission should be active at any given time.
Here you can see all of your accepted missions.
The active mission is shown in yellow.
Select the inactive training mission and activate it.
This is because one mission ending does not automatically activate another mission.
Activate the remaining mission yourself, please.
Now please zoom out, find the station in the other sector, and interact with it.
This isn't really a mission, but guidance is now temporarily switched to lead you to this station.
Or rather, it would do that if you knew the way!
Your computer doesn't have the necessary Jump Gate in its database, so it's showing you that you need to find it in order to proceed.
I'm marking the gate's location on the map.
Close the map and fly to it.
Now that the gate is in range, the computer has automatically added it to the database and updated guidance to lead you through it.
Follow guidance until you're at the destination.
Unlike real missions, this one has automatically switched back to giving you guidance for the previously active mission.
You can also get this kind of guidance by asking people for directions to certain locations or people.
Today we'll learn how to use the various means of travelling between systems and sectors.
In front of you is a Jump Gate.
Sometimes you'll find one that's inactive.
This one's working, though, which you can tell from the swirly bits in the middle.
To use it, simply fly through.
That's all there is to it.
Now, I've been told that the technology is totally different, but in practice these Accelerators function pretty much exactly like Jump Gates.
While Jump Gates connect different star systems, Accelerators take you to different places within the same one.
They also take you to sectors within a star system.
The main difference is that they are directional, so you need to use the entry gate, not the exit.
As you see, it's a tiny bit slower than the other methods.
I like it, though, it lets me enjoy the view.
The entry of one is right in front of you.
It has a much lower speed than the superhighway we just came out of, but it's still a whole lot faster than most ships can travel on their own.
It's not wide enough for capital ships, though.
Medium-sized ships are the largest that can use them.
Local highways can be entered and exited at any point along the way.
Fly into the one right in front of you.
This highway is special, in that it leads you right into a Jump Gate.
You don't have to do anything, the transition will just work on its own.
Please pay attention to the objective in the corner of your HUD.
It's counting down to when you should exit the highway.
Wait until it's done, then exit the highway.
Before we start, please note the yellow icon below your crosshair.
The manuals call it the "check engine light" but I've never seen an engine that looks like that...
It means that you can't make use of your Travel Mode right now.
That's because this lesson takes place in a region that prevents it from working.
Being hit by a weapon disables your travel drive for a short time as well, so don't rely on it to get out of trouble.
I've also heard of weapons that target this system specifically, to make you an easy target for pirates.
Now on to the actual lesson at hand.
At some point you may find yourself with a bunch of fighter ships under your command.
Let's learn how to use them effectively.
Under Subordinate Control you can see several groups of ships.
At the moment they all have the Follow role, which means that they will follow you and only fight back if directly attacked.
We'll use most of these roles today.
But Fleet Supply and Mimic will be covered in another lesson.
Let's begin with the Interception role.
This group will now attack any hostile ships it detects on its Gravidar, up to medium-size.
To attack capital ships you need to use the Bombardment role.
The group is now attacking the hostile capital ship.
If you want them to be a bit less aggressive you can use the Defence role.
These ships will now fight back if you or one of your subordinates are attacked.
These ships will now attack any hostile that you target.
I've activated a weapon on your ship.
Shoot at the target in front of you.
The group will now attack this target until it's destroyed, or until you attack another hostile target.
It's also possible to directly give an overriding attack order.
Do this on the marked target.
This has given all of your direct subordinates an attack order, regardless of their current role.
They will carry it out until the target is destroyed, unless you directly tell them to resume their previous role.
Either way, they will resume their assigned role.

(Spoken like a radio ad, can sound a little stilted or awkward on purpose. Everything after the first "guaranteed" should be spoken as quickly as possible.)Tired of waiting for shuttles? Want to fly wherever you want, whenever you want? Then what you need is a pilot's licence! And what's the best place to get one? That's right: Jace Winger's flight school! I do theory. I do practice. And I'm licenced for weapons training. With my tried and tested training course you'll be an ace pilot in no time, guaranteed! Success not guaranteed. No liability in case of explosion, blunt trauma, exsanguination, asphyxiation or rapid decompression.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 19 / Mission Specialist
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 19
page.t: (reaction to friendly fire)Hey, will you stop firing?
(reaction to friendly fire)You're wrecking my shields!
(reaction to friendly fire)Why are you shooting me?
Approaching the Jump Gate.(Matter of fact)
(2/2)Sir, we are picking up an unusually high energy signature!
(2/4)Our team confirms that the Heretic's End gate does indeed contain the coordinates to the Kingdom End system.
(3/4)The timing cannot be coincidental, can it? Just after we received word from the Boron?(uncertain)
(4/4)Is it possible that their experiments were somehow related to the gate reinitialisation?
(1/2)The Split didn't exactly give you a choice over your research focus.
(2/2)Could this be the Boron? Could they really have unlocked Jump Gate technology?(excited)
(1/3)This is clearly a mining ship, but that's strange. As far as I can detect there's really very little here to mine.
(2/3)All I can imagine is that the vessel came under an attack of some kind.
(3/3)We should be wary of potential assailants nearby.
(2/2)Oh yes! The change in energy signature is immediately detectable!
(1/2)I can confirm that we can interface with the Jump Gate.
(2/2)It appears that we can input basic commands.
It's too late for that now.
The Jump Gate is almost powered up!(excited)
Everything... all scans seem to indicate regular Jump Gate function.
My readings indicate that they expended an enormous amount of energy to bring about the Gate's activation.
If they hadn't, then the whole experiment would have been a dud.
(2/2)We have to make sure that everything is in order.
(1/2)I am anxious to finally get there!
(2/2)I have worked with many gates before, but none were ever in quite such a delicate state as this...

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 21 / Fleet Admiral
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 21
page.t: (1/5)The Terran Secret Service has been alerted to potential gate activity.(If Terran DLC)
(2/5)The Intervention Corps has been ordered to undertake a threat assessment, with regard to the potential impact on Sol territories.(If Terran DLC)("Corps" is pronounced "Core")

(3/5)We can only guarantee everyone's safety as long as the expedition remains close to the Intervention Fleet. However, we advise everyone to stay clear of our firing arcs.(If Terran DLC, slightly condescending)
(4/5)The Alliance of the Word has long been a valued ally of the Argon Federation.(If Argon)
(5/5)We are happy to offer your expedition protection while we investigate the potential for harm to the Federation and its allies.(If Argon, reassuring)
(3/4)Intervention Corps, prepare for traversal.(If Terran)("Corps" is pronounced "Core", giving orders)
(3/4)Everyone, get ready to pass through!(If Argon)
(2/4)According to our files, you have not yet finished your current assignment.
(3/4)Take care of your duties to Sol before you go running off with this rabble.
(1a/3)The Protectorate has determined that this system poses no threat to the citizens of Sol, or the wider network.(If Terran, reassuring)
(1b/3)Investigations conclude that this system poses no threat to us, or our allies in the network.(If Argon)
(2/3)Our orders are to deploy to a position of more strategic importance.
(3/3)Still... stay alert! None of us know what might be lurking out there.(energetic)
As High Representative of the Terran Protectorate, may I formally welcome you aboard.
(2/3)We hope to craft a habitat worthy of the representatives of Queen Polypheides of the Boron. This will help no end.
(3/3)Thank you Herald. May your time in Terran space pass without incident.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Female 20 / Bar Witness
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Female 20
page.t: (1/3)Gates opening, gates closing, a world beyond our grasp, playthings of invisible forces, unable to resist, unable to even perceive.(intoxicated)
(2/3)What else remains for one to do in this fading excuse of an existence, but squander yours before someone or something does it for you?(intoxicated)
(3/3)We've looked into the void, and everyone with a spark of understanding will be in an establishment like this, trying their best to forget.(intoxicated)
(1/4)Yes, yes, I've seen everything, I now live here after all.(intoxicated)
(2/4)The Boron was at the table right over there and told me something about water. Until he got very upset.(intoxicated)
(3/4)He might not have been accustomed to the gloom and misery around here.(intoxicated)
(4a/4)He even left a box with some belongings at his table when he rushed off. The waiters haven't even found it yet.(intoxicated)
(4b/4)He even left a box with some belongings at his table when he rushed off. The waiters haven't even found it yet.(intoxicated)
Did you find his belongings at the table over there?(intoxicated)
Did you find his belongings at the table over there?(intoxicated)

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 22 / Mysterious Boso Fan
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 22
page.t: Oh, wow! I am such a big fan.
(proud)I am known by many names, and I have many tools at my disposal. Together, we can defeat the scourge!
Perhaps I was too hasty. Fear not, for I am the renowned Slayer of Xenon!
I will return once I have proven myself!

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 23
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 23 - Civilian captain / Non-gruff military in high stakes situation
page.t: Hey! I said, do you hear me?
You need to make your way to the docking bay so we can leave!
Get a move on! We can't wait much longer!
Sorry my friend, but we're out of time. Good luck!
There you are! Get on board, quick!
What are you doing? Those things are still out there!
Ok, we have no choice but to undock and leave.
There are abandoned ships among the wrecks. See if this one still flies.
You are one lucky son-of-a-gunne!(pronounced gun) Catch up with us. We're checking for survivors before getting out of dodge.
Alright, we're getting the heck out of here!
Not seeing any survivors, but there is a fighter which looks slightly dinged-up.
We need all the help we can get.
Get into a spacesuit and see if you can bring it back online.
How's the ship? I'm reading that the weapons should still be operational. We may need them.
Nice of you to join us. We could use the cover.
We've collected some data transmitted from ships before they were lost.
Whatever those things are, they tore right through us.
The last warning said that ships fleeing by gate were being picked off one by one. Those things can come out of nowhere.
Let's keep a low profile and stay away from the gates for now. Maybe we can grab some survivors on our way to the trading station.
I'm transmitting the last known positions of ships that ran into trouble.
I'd really appreciate you sticking close, just in case those things show up again.
Don't venture off too far. We'll have a better chance together.
Alright buddy. Stay safe out there, and head back to us soon. We'll take a look in this direction.
Contacts! Right on top of us!
All we've found are wrecks. Did anyone else survive this?
Just wreckage. We'll gather data here and move on.
The gates are a no-go. Let's head to the trading station and look for survivors along the way.
Head back to us when you can.
It's no good. There's nothing left...
More of those things keep showing up, so we don't have much time.
I hate to sound morbid but unless an Argon fleet pushes through the gate blockade, I don't fancy our chances.
Let's pool all the data we've gathered. I'm sure the Argon Navy and next of kin would appreciate it.
We'll make a run for a gate, transmitting the data as we go.
Sounds good. Let's get a move on.
Simulations show that we need to get closer to the gate for our transmission to cut through the interference.
Let's clear the area and plan our next move.
Look at the size of that ship!
Alright, get us out of here.
What the heck are these things? They came out of nowhere.
We're lucky this many of us managed to get out.
Last I saw of the captain, she was manning the gunnery station herself.
I know it looks bad, but keep it together people. We'll get through this.
Steady on this heading. Hopefully we'll keep a low profile.
There, up ahead. Looks like wreckage from a fight. Let's hope lightning doesn't strike twice. Bring us in close.
Well done everyone. We've certainly done our duty.
We've done all we can. Let's at least give them a fight!
Damn it all. We gave it a good shot!
A pirate attack stranded our ship in a dense fog with limited visibility. We can't see anything out here!
We've suffered major system damage due to an EMP or some kind of weapon, we can't even receive messages!
Our Gravidar is impaired. We don't know if anyone's looking for us, but we desperately need help!
We've managed to fend off the pirates for now, but we fear more are on their way. We're sitting ducks here!
If you're out there searching for us, please hurry! Time is of the essence!
We're in dire need of assistance! Our ship's systems are barely holding together.
Is anyone out there? We're running low on supplies and can't hold out much longer!
We're hoping for a miracle, a beacon of light in this endless fog...
We've sent out a distress signal, but we don't even know if it's getting through this fog...
Our engineers are doing their best to repair the ship, but we could really use some help...
Our medical bay is running low on supplies; we have injured crew members who need immediate attention!
If you can hear us, please respond! We don't know how much longer we can hold out...
We've been adrift in this fog for what feels like an eternity... please, help us!
The morale of our remaining crew is deteriorating. We need to get out of this fog as soon as possible!
If you find any of our escape pods, please ensure the safety of our crew members!
We're trying to conserve energy, but our life support systems won't last forever...
We've been sending out SOS signals non-stop, but we have no way of knowing if they're being received...
Our scanners are useless in this fog. We're completely blind out here...
The uncertainty of our situation is taking its toll on the crew. We need help now more than ever!
We can't even tell if it's day or night any more; we're losing all sense of time...
We are down to our last laser tower...
We're detecting a faint signal, is that you? We're in desperate need of help!
It seems like someone's approaching! We're hoping it's a friendly ship...
We can't see you yet, but we sense that you're getting closer. Please, hurry!
Our sensors are picking up something... could it be our rescue?
Hold on, crew! We might have a chance; there's a ship approaching!
You made it! We're incredibly grateful, but there's no time to waste. We need your help, now!
Is that you, our saviour? We're so relieved to see you. We're in dire straits!
Thank you for finding us! Let's work quickly to assess the situation, and get out of here!
Finally, some hope in this fog! Let's get our systems back online and defend ourselves!
You're a sight for sore eyes! Let's secure the area and prepare for possible pirate attacks!
If you have laser towers, mines, anything, drop them quickly!
We're detecting hostile signals nearby, but we're defenceless! We need assistance!
The pirates might have found us again! We can't fight them off without your help!
Our sensors are picking up pirate ships nearby! We're sitting ducks here!
We don't know how much longer we can hold them off! Please, we need you!
These pirates are relentless! They're closing in, and we're out of options!
We're barely holding on! The pirates are circling us like vultures...
If you're out there, please help! The pirates are getting closer, and we're vulnerable!
We fear the worst... the pirates might have found us! We need your help, now!
Our time is running out! The pirates are closing in, and we can't defend ourselves!
We're desperate for help! The pirates are nearly upon us, and we're defenceless!
They're attacking us! We're sustaining heavy damage! Help us, please!
The pirates have opened fire! Our hull is taking a beating! We need backup!
We're under fire! Our shields are failing! Where are you?
The pirates are ruthless! They're targeting our life support systems!
Our weapons are offline! We can't fight back! Please, hurry!
They're boarding us! We're trying to repel them, but we're overwhelmed!
Our crew are fighting for their lives! We can't hold out much longer!
We're losing power! The pirates have targeted our critical systems! We're in serious trouble!
The pirates are relentless! We're taking heavy fire and losing hope!
Our defences are crumbling! We need immediate assistance to fend off the pirates!
They're trying to breach our hull! We're doing everything we can, but we need your help!
The situation is getting critical! Our ship won't survive much more of this onslaught!
We're taking casualties! The pirates are showing no mercy!
The pirates have disabled our engines! We're completely immobilised!
Our life support systems are failing! We don't have much time left!
The ship is falling apart! We're running out of options and time!
Our ship is on the brink of destruction! If you're out there, please help us!
We can't hold out much longer! This might be our last transmission...
Our hull is critically damaged! The next hit could be our last!
We're evacuating the remaining crew! The ship is about to go down!
This is our last stand! If you can hear this, know that we fought to the bitter end!
We need to prioritise repairs. What should we focus on; shields, engines, or weapons?
We can't repair everything at once. Please tell us which system to concentrate on; shields, engines, or weapons.
Our resources are limited. Please direct us whether to prioritise repairs on shields, engines, or weapons.
We need to make a decision. Which system should we restore first; shields, engines, or weapons?
They are launching ships that carry missiles!
Those ships coming in are equipped with missiles!
The pirates have targeted our shields! We're losing power and protection!
Our engines have been hit! We're losing mobility and need immediate repairs!
Captain, our weapon systems were just hit! We're sitting ducks without them!
We're en route to the Jump Gate, but we need to remain vigilant for any pirate activity!
Making our way to the Jump Gate, Captain! Let's hope we don't run into more trouble...
We're travelling to the Jump Gate, but we must stay on guard for any surprise attacks!
Our journey to the Jump Gate continues. We're keeping a close eye on our surroundings!
As we head to the Jump Gate, we need to be prepared for any potential threats!
Moving towards the Jump Gate, but we're not out of danger yet. Stay sharp, Captain!
We're making progress towards the Jump Gate, but we can't let our guard down!
Captain, we're on our way to the Jump Gate. Let's hope for a safe passage!
We're closing in on the Jump Gate, but we must be cautious of any pirate activity!
Navigating towards the Jump Gate, but we can't afford any more setbacks. Stay alert!
We've reached the Jump Gate! Preparing to jump and leave this treacherous area behind!
Captain, we've arrived at the Jump Gate! Initiating jump sequence for our escape!
The Jump Gate is in sight! We're almost out of this dangerous region!
We've made it to the Jump Gate! Let's jump out of here and regroup!
At last, we've arrived at the Jump Gate! We can finally escape this nightmare!
We couldn't make it in time, Captain. We gave it our best shot, but the pirates were too much for us.
I'm sorry, Captain. We tried our best, but we just couldn't save the ship.
Our efforts weren't enough, Captain. The pirates overwhelmed us, and we lost the ship.
We did everything we could, Captain. Unfortunately, it wasn't enough to save the ship and crew.
Despite our best efforts, we couldn't turn the tide, Captain. The pirates were too powerful.
Captain, we can't thank you enough for your help! Your assistance saved our ship and crew!
Your support was invaluable, Captain. We wouldn't have made it without you!
We owe you our lives, Captain! Your timely intervention saved us from certain doom!
We're forever grateful for your help, Captain! You truly saved the day!
You have our deepest gratitude, Captain! Your assistance was crucial to our survival!
This is Argon Station Security calling all allies in the vicinity of True Sight.
There is a Paranid fleet on an attack vector heading for this station.
Defences are not online, repeat, station is undefended. Request immediate assistance.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 24
page.descr: Lines for Mission Argon NPC Male 24 - Pirate
page.t: We've entered the system, guys! Let's search for that crippled ship and claim our booty!
We're in the right place, boys! Keep your eyes peeled for that stranded vessel. Riches await us!
This be the system where that damaged ship be hiding. Let's find it and plunder its cargo!(spoken using your best pirate impression)

(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, I thank you for your efforts.

page.title: Mission Argon/Terran NPC Male 26 / Terran diplomat
page.descr: Lines for Terran Faction Diplomat
page.t: (Accepting invitation)The Terran Protectorate has deemed you important enough to accept your invitation. Prepare for my arrival!
(Diplomat Arrival Confirmation)Your embassy has welcomed me.
(Player deteriorates relations, diplomat leaves)Sol will only deal with those who treat us fairly. You have made an enemy of the Protectorate today.
(Player requests military support)Our friends can always count on the might of the Protectorate to keep them safe.
(Faction military support has ended)Our duties require that we divert our military attention elsewhere - for the time being.
(Promotion ceremony - intro)I am glad to see you in person.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, friendly)Your continued service to the Terran people has not escaped our notice, and we want to award you a new rank.
(Promotion ceremony - cntd, allied)As a true ally to the Terran Protectorate, please allow me to present you with this rank.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', friendly)Since your deeds have proven you to be worthy of our trust, your new status will allow you greater access to the Terran Protectorate.
(Promotion ceremony - handing over 'medal', allied)In recognition of your loyalty, you are rewarded with unfettered access to the Sol system.
(Promotion ceremony)Of course, this rank comes with benefits beyond that as well.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 1)Should you prove to be unworthy of the trust placed in you, these privileges will be revoked.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 2)Although, should it come to that, a revoked licence would be the least of your worries.
(Promotion ceremony - fluff line to spread notifications out 3)I am confident that you will find these rewards to be adequate compensation for your efforts.
(Promotion ceremony - subgroup licence hint)You can also expect certain Terran organisations to approach you for your help in the future.
(Promotion ceremony - outro)Once again, the Terran people thank you for your service.
(Promotion ceremony - outro cntd)We look forward to your continued assistance.

Ah yes, the adventures of Selaia Tarren, my most brilliant and distinguished sub... I mean assistant. From a young age, I dare presume, she yearned to explore the unknown and uncover the mysteries of our universe. Indeed, it may appear as if we had a lot in common back then. We surveyed anomalies in time and space, brought about the materialisation of a unique and special station, almost intentionally, and escaped from the vicious machinations of one pair of particularly unpleasant Split fellows. And that was only the start of the excitement!(sub...' is meant to be 'subject', but cut off mid-speech)

Assistant! We have already accomplished much, but there remains a lot to be done before I can... I mean before we can achieve our lives' work! Fascinatingly obscure sectors require charting, groundbreaking research needs to be groundbreakingly researched, and there appears to be a smudge on my habitation unit. I suggest you get to work immediately.

My pursuit of knowledge has led me on many adventures; from the daring escape from Split imprisonment, to that time I lost several tons of BoFu in a wager with a vociferous spacefly herder. While my life is seldom dull, I currently find myself in a somewhat comfortable position with an impressive laboratory, as well as a capable assistant. I foresee that we will accomplish much in our time together.

I pride myself on seeing a task through to completion. Scientific progress cannot halt at the first obstacle, nor should it be stifled by petty bureaucratic concerns. I am free; free to expand my knowledge, my understanding of the universe. All from within the confines of this humble tank.
