The Kha'ak Forager is a lightning fast and highly manoeuvrable scout ship, with little accompanying weaponry. While notionally fragile, Commonwealth pilots report that the Forager is notoriously hard to catch and target.

The appearance of the Kha'ak can trigger a sinking feeling in the stomach or stomachs of any pilot, however accomplished. These "space bugs", as they are often described, attack in mystifyingly geometric vessels, and have, thus far, rebuffed all attempts at communication.\n\nThis fighter has been dubbed the Protector and, like all Kha'ak ships, it is well-armed and trigger-happy.
The diabolical pyramids of the Kha'ak are a perpetual threat. The Hive Guard is a heavy fighter and one of the more disturbing Kha'ak ships that may appear on a pilot's scanner.

Armed with the frighteningly accurate Kyon Emitter, the Kha'ak Queen's Guard most commonly attacks in swarm formation to devastating effect.\n\nThe pseudo-insectile nature of the Kha'ak gave rise to the theory that they are directly or indirectly controlled by a Queen. This, in turn, inspired the name given to this vessel. However, the theory is as yet unverified.

While once little more than a rumour, sightings of Ravagers are becoming increasingly more frequent. Little is known about this ship class. However, thanks to its deadly primary weapon, it is able to deal massive amounts of damage to any that come across it. As the command hierarchy of the Kha'ak is pretty much impossible to discern, it is unknown precisely how the Ravager functions within the overall Kha'ak structure, but it is generally agreed that it appears to be acting as a capital ship.

This monstrosity has only been spotted a few times throughout history, before disappearing never to reappear again. It is unknown whether there is just a single Obliterator, or whether there are many more of them, lurking outside of currently explored space. The Obliterator is a hulking behemoth that is best compared to a battleship, although these comparisons break down when discussing the organic constructions of the Kha'ak. Very little is known about the Obliterator, as it is rare that anything survives an encounter with this ship. The fear that it causes is understandable, since on several occasions it has turned its devastating power on a planet, using its weapons to obliterate that planet entirely.
The Cargo Drone is a Teladi invention that expedites freight transfers and is ubiquitously popular among merchants across the known galaxy.
The Repair Drone is an autonomous, self-propelled micro-vessel that is used for the repair of ship and station hulls.

Affectionately named "termites", building drones are an essential component of station construction.\n\nAll races have moved to drone-based construction due to the scale of injury and loss of sentient life incurred through manual methods.

Advanced battlefield tactical command has been transformed by the evolution of Defence Drones. Once little more than cannon fodder, a drone swarm is now a formidable defensive capability.\n\nThe very best commanders are able to coordinate drone and non-drone strategies, adapting them to make best use of the strengths of each. Defence drone mastery is not an easy task, however; it is the mark of a top-flight tactician.

The humble Mining Drone is an essential asset at the heart of any primary resource-based business empire. Inexpensive, but highly vulnerable, the "termite" as it is colloquially referred to, is highly effective, particularly when deployed in large numbers.
The Gas Collector Drone is an advanced drone system that greatly increases the efficiency of gaseous harvesting operations, particularly when used in large quantities.
While romantic histories describe captains going down with their ships honourably, the advancement of escape pod technology has proven to be a popular alternative to flaming death.

For most, though not all, known species, the Space Suit is an essential item of Personal Protection Equipment for survival in a vacuum.\n\nMany suit enhancements are available to facilitate manual chores required during extravehicular activity.

The Boarding Pod enables the transfer of marines for the purposes of capturing target ships. Although vulnerable in transit, their use in numbers with a well-trained marine contingent, can enable commanders to grow a fleet quickly, without the trouble of building or paying for ships.\n\n"I felt the engine thrust through my bones. The five of us avoided eye contact, knowing this short trip could be our last; that we might never make it to our target. In the boarding pod, our life or death was dependent on the skills of our cruiser's Commander and gunners. I resisted the temptation to hold my breath until the breach. Once we were in, my survival would be back in my own hands and I'd need to be fully oxygenated. Breathe. Focus..." Excerpt from "Marine Life" by Menika Loma.

The Autonomous Distress Drone is an interesting vessel subsystem. It alerts local authorities if you are under attack and otherwise out of range of the police. Unfortunately, this only deters assailants who seek to maintain good relations with those authorities or, indeed, are not assaulting you on their behalf.
The Drop Drone is an essential system in terraforming operations, transporting the required surface-bound wares.
{20101,101511}\n\nThe Medium-sized model is an upgraded drone with additional capacity.
The economic benefits of a successful planetary reformat can be immense.\n\nThe Small Terraforming Drone is a highly complex, state-of-the-art innovation, essential for enabling this work.
{20101,101711} The Medium Terraforming Drone is an enhanced model, offering a greater operational efficiency.

Argon Station Security Vessels police the vicinity of Argon installations, seeking out felons and those carrying contraband. While they are lightly armed, crossing them may compromise a captain's good standing with the authorities.
This is a short-range civilian vessel, unsuited to trans-sector flight.
The Short Range Transporter is used to ferry cargo and passengers within sectors.
This leisure vehicle allows denizens to see the sights and enjoy the delights that this system has to offer.
This Mass Transporter is a short-range vehicle, carrying passengers and cargo, and is limited to in-sector flight.

The Paranid authorities are notoriously strict, particularly if a captain is not of their species. It is advisable to remain polite and compliant with regard to the Station Security Vessels policing Paranid space.

While the Teladi are tolerant of the trading of many wares that are illegal elsewhere in the Commonwealth, access to those markets requires the good maintenance of a trader's reputation. It is wise to remain respectful of the Teladi Police and their Station Security Vessels.

This is a short-range Xenon drone with an undetermined array of capabilities. Captured examples and debris confirm the use of advanced technology and encryption that, to-date, has evaded a comprehensive scientific understanding.\n\nWhile these drones are likely to be undertaking predictable tasks, the range of wares and items they transport is a matter of supposition, as is the extent to which they are considered truly intelligent or merely autonomous.
The Split police and their Station Security Vessels are known to be impatient, abrupt and trigger happy. "Innocent until proven guilty" is not a concept that translates well into Split culture.

Terran police forces generally recruit martial-minded people who failed the tough military entrance exams. This results in a Station Security Corps, whose vessels intercept honest traders as often as criminals.

When the Yaki clans were found to have instituted a police force and resourced it with a fleet of Station Security Vessels, outside observers where somewhat surprised. Debate is ongoing as to whether this presages a Yaki intent to normalise its relations as a part of the Commonwealth of Planets.
This Maintenance Vessel is limited to a local range, and is suitable for conducting minor repairs and other works.

(Astrid)The Astrid yacht is the Northriver Company's spirit personified: sleek and luxurious to the point of excess. The designers on board Aurora station had to make the ostentatious ship fulfil a large number of extravagant and often conflicting requirements set by their client. As such, both the assembly of the pompous final product and the manufacturing of many of its core components had to happen by hand, and the Astrid therefore remains a prized unicum. A wide array of highly specialised workshops and laboratories had to be commissioned to provide the garish synthetic materials and dazzling, custom-made metalwork used in its lavish interior and uniquely refracting, streamlined hull. This entire process proved to be incredibly expensive, and the Astrid is therefore deemed utterly unsuitable for mass production, much to the delight of the affluent collector. While working on its engine, the Aurora engineers heavily leaned on their previous experience with designing high speed ships like the Lux. The dazzlingly flamboyant ship also carries a thickly shielded storage compartment capable of containing volatile Bose-Einstein Condensates, rumoured to somehow improve its resistance to cosmic particles and improve its flight characteristics. Though this claim may sound like pseudo-scientific marketing lingo, one has to agree that even for a grandiosely cutting-edge yacht, the Astrid turns out to be surprisingly fast, which has given CEO of the Northriver Company the reputation to be in multiple places at once if he so pleases.

Perhaps the most interesting thing about the Nodan fighter is the lack of information available regarding its existence. It is only known to be available from the Alliance of the Word, and the organisation has remained tight-lipped as to the vessel's inception and design.\n\nThe design is somewhat quirky, with no clear antecedence related to other faction architecture. However, the Nodan has earned itself plaudits from committed dogfighters, based on its impressive speed, agility and deceleration.
{20101,120311}\n\nFor those seeking additional speed, the Nodan Vanguard model is available.
{20101,120311}\n\nThe Sentinel model provides the ship with a hardened superstructure.

{20101,80001}(Avarice Ship Building)

(Erlking Shielded against Tide)Shortly after the first Tides in 800 \(NT\) devastated the Avarice system, nomad engineers on Tidebreak, under their lead engineer Sihi Do, began the Erlking project. This project was an attempt at building a capital ship, sturdy enough to withstand the Tide and be used as a mobile base in Avarice. No sooner had they succeeded in providing the ship with sufficient shielding, than they abandoned all work on the barely operational Erlking. They refocused their attention on another, undisclosed, major project, before ultimately disappearing. Despite being unfinished, the Erlking continued to be deployed, while Tidebreak engineers repeatedly attempted, and failed, to improve on, or even reproduce, the design's unique power core.

With the connection of Avarice to the more militarised Syndicate system in 821 \(NT\), Tidebreak engineers attempted to weaponise the Erlking, and reclassified it as Battleship. They added turret and weapon hard-points, but failed to develop compatible turrets and weapons. The Syndicate later confiscated the ship to remove this potential military threat, and attempted to develop the weapon systems themselves. Among the engineers of Windfall, those of the Solid Ice Union had the most experience with capital ships, but the political situation, and fear of a power grab, meant that they were not allowed to work on the Erlking. Instead, the Scrapyard engineers were tasked with completing the weapon systems. Having previously failed to stabilise the energy supply on the Shih fighter, to increase the number of supported weapons, the Erlking presented them with the opposite problem: all efforts to connect conventional weaponry to its unique power grid resulted in them being blown off the hull. Attempts to modify either the power grid or the weapon systems were also in vain, but their work had started only recently and Syndicate expectations remained high.(Battleship same as {20221,5031}, Sihi Do is female)
Promethean Spark(Twin Story Ch1 rebellious Trader Ship)
Bestowed in Perpetuity(Twin Story Ch2 Fan Trader Ship)
J.P. Morgan's Knife(Twin Story New Fan Ship)
Eleius' Vigilance(Queen's ship named after Eleius, a deceased Boron queen; Eleius from Greek mythology)
Menelaus' Reminiscence(Boron carrier ship named after Menelaus, a deceased Boron queen; Menelaus from Greek mythology)

Developed as a near-perfect replica of Kyle Brennan's original ship, the Xperimental Shuttle is the definition of attention to detail, with every part - down to the smallest rivet - reproduced precisely. The project to recreate this iconic ship was undertaken by Kaori after using it in a simulation, which brought on intense feelings of nostalgia for Earth. Initially, this ship was fitted with an advanced teleportation device, derived from Sohnen technology, allowing the Xperimental Shuttle to traverse the universe with ease. After this drive was rendered unusable following an unfortunate accident, it was replaced with a standard-issue travel drive.

Commissioned in the wake of escalating tensions between Family Tharka and Family Rhonkar, this colossal vessel represents a fusion of Split resourcefulness and determination in the face of adversity. Utilising their expertise in manufacturing and engineering, Family Tharka pooled what little resources they had remaining to construct this Colony Ship, a marvel of modular construction composed of repurposed space station components.\n\nUpon completion, Family Tharka embarked on a journey to find a new territory in which to settle in. Many different hardships befell them before their odyssey was concluded, leading to the legacy of Tharka being found all across the known universe.

The Dart was initially released as a mail-in kit project, to which an aspiring racer could subscribe and have parts shipped to them periodically. Due to its popularity, the Dart was quickly offered as a ready-to-fly ship, and the project took no new kit customers.

It is easy to identify a kit-built Dart from a production one, as the tooling for the rear titanium fins was recreated due to complaints about the fins' shape not fitting that of the rest of the ship.

Despite being discontinued, the kits remain remarkably popular, and incomplete kits regularly sell for beyond the price of a production ship.
Saiien II(pron. sy-yen 2, see pronunciation sample)
Saiien III(pron. sy-yen 3, see pronunciation sample)

A joint development by the Argon Federation and the Teladi Ministry of Finance, the Envoy integrates each faction's latest technologies. The Envoy class is equipped with exclusive high-performance engines and shield generators, unavailable to other vessels.

The joint technology program also included the development of a set of heavy weapons specific to the Envoy. Due to market demand, turret variants of those weapons were also introduced. These variants are compatible with a wide variety of ships, but some ships are excluded due to technical constraints. The ship also includes two forward-facing hardpoints, supporting a range of conventional weaponry for tactical flexibility.

A dedicated low-signature stance is available, in which most weapon systems are concealed and inoperable. While in this configuration, the vessel exhibits reduced detectability and increased manoeuvrability, at the expense of speed.

Ship operators may also activate faction camouflage protocols, allowing the vessel to appear to belong to another faction when observed externally. These advanced protocols are licensed on a strictly individual basis, and are not available to employed personnel.

First observed shortly after the introduction of the Envoy, the Cypher's origins remain unclear. Though not officially linked to any known faction, it is frequently flown by pirates or other independent operators.

With some structural similarities to the Envoy, and capable of using the same exclusive engines, shields and primary weapons, the Cypher's main systems are typically supplemented with equipment acquired from Teladi or other manufacturers.

Although the vessel lacks configurable stances, it retains the ability to engage identity-masking protocols, allowing it to mimic the transponder signature of other factions.

The sweeping, yet pragmatic, design of this s-class fighter is immediately apparent. Engineers mounted two extensions alongside the cockpit in an attempt to stabilise the ship for prolonged travel between branes. With its front-facing weapons, it is a fierce but practical ship, allowing a well-trained combat pilot to deal with any encounter, no matter what situation they find themselves in. It is unsurprising, therefore, that the design has been adapted by several factions vying for power and influence across the Multiverse.

The hyper-aggressive, technologically advanced Yasur-class brane ship was built to withstand all crossbrane-travel induced turbulence. This extraordinary stability was achieved with the help of hull plating reinforced with Brane-Bismuth. Notably, it took a lot of effort on the part of the Coalition Engineers to assemble these ships at scale at the Coalition Headquarters. The four front-mounted guns, and its agile nature, make this ship a fearsome dogfighter, and its sleek design makes it hard to hit by any enemies who dare to engage.

page.title: Stations
page.descr: Names and descriptions of stations
page.t: This centrally situated Teladi Trading Station(Teladi Trading Station same as {20102,1311}) serves as a hub for interstellar trade. Although the Teladi Company does not usually care much for unnecessary luxury, this station boasts a striking habitable orbital ring. The effort to maintain the ring's pleasant, planet-like biome is significant, but well worth it. Visitors are drawn from all over, and they tend to spend a lot of time on the station. The more time they spend on the ring, the more credits they spend on frivolous purchases, to the glee of the Teladi Company.
This facility was constructed by the Segaris Pioneers as a home for their most advanced, possibly illegal, and certainly top secret, research projects.

This abandoned Xenon asteroid base has developed something of a local mythology. Nearby stations hum with stories of ghosts, disappearances, and hallucinations. However, empirical investigators have discovered no such phenomena.\n\nWhile investigators concede the station does indeed have a somewhat "creepy" aesthetic, the famed Segaris anthropologist Sasha Bhattarcharji put it most succinctly: "don't all abandoned stations look creepy?"(I have used Sasha Bhattarcharji as it's a feasible Earth name and Sasha is gender flexible. It doesn't refer to anyone in particular.)

A Xenon structure with evidence of pirate faction modifications. The entire facility appears to be built on a highly crystalline rock formation.\n\nThe precise function of the facility is not entirely clear. However, the visible modules seem to have some form of energy amplification capability.

Possibly the least intentionally designed station in the known universe, Spacelab is the headquarters of the Segaris Pioneers.

Spacelab has grown organically from a once-modest research outpost, to become what is now a sprawling, connected network of laboratories, workshops and storage modules.

Questions are raised periodically as to whether all the material stored at Spacelab is, in fact, any longer useful or whether some sort of psychosocial hoarding phenomenon is in evidence.
Rusiris Sunrise is a Sunrise Flower Factory with a dubious commercial record. It is believed to have been founded by the least talented scion of an otherwise glittering Teladi dynasty.

With the relatively limited amount of natural resources available to the Quettanauts, the construction of the Renewable Energy Production Array \(REPA\) marked a turning point in their history. Given their economy, the distribution of energy has been an oft-debated issue. There are some who argue that it should be a basic right for all Quettanauts, and that it should be distributed freely to all Quettanaut stations and ships based on their requirements. But others point out the need to maintain and run the REPA long-term, and that energy distribution should be traded like any other ware. In reality the Quettanauts treat this problem somewhere in between - the REPA maintenance is seen as a form of civic service, and as such the availability of energy within Quettanaut space is more evenly distributed than it might otherwise have been.

The labyrinthine network of pipelines, distillation towers and storage tanks give this station the ability to process a vast number of gases essential for industrial production and resource management. Whether this is synthesising fuels for spacecraft propulsion, or refining exotic gases for use in manufacturing processes, the Hydro Processing Plant plays a central role in sustaining the Quettanauts' industry.

Arguably one of the key nodes of the Quettanauts' supply chain, this station creates the majority of the components required for the construction of almost every part of Quettanaut life. The design and construction of this factory is such that any one of its many production lines is scalable and reconfigurable, allowing the station to adapt its output in response to fluctuations in demand for any of the building blocks of a myriad of finished products.

The Organic Produce Facility stands as a testament to unity, diversity, and culinary range. This station produces the majority of the foodstuffs consumed within Quettanaut society, drawing from the backgrounds and cuisines of the races that make up Quettanaut culture.\n\nUtilising advanced cultivation methods, the Quettanauts have been able to produce many of the ingredients alongside one another, resulting in a pungent aroma noticeable to all travellers when they first step onto the station. Defying fears that there may be conflict between some of the crops and other foods, a dedicated scientific team on the station provide constant observation to ensure the reliability and resilience of the crops, and the quality of the produce.

This Ministry of Finance station serves as both an outpost facing the lawless frontier, and as a jail. It was erected after Windfall reconnected to the network, with the explicit intent to squash the criminal activity spilling out of the system. Apprehended Criminals are kept in the prison complex while they are prepared to be shipped deeper into Teladi space for their trial and sentencing. While the station's presence seems to have some effect on the local crime rate, the station's leadership seems less than capable when it comes to combating piracy in the long term.

The Grand Ice Refinery is the headquarters of the Solid Ice Union, an important group within the Vigor pirate syndicate.\n\nThe SIU conglomerate was founded by ice miners in Windfall during The Dark. This bond, forged in adversity, resulted in a group that is notably suspicious of outsiders.

Keepsafe is the headquarters of the Scrapyard sub-faction of the Vigor Syndicate.\n\nAs a scrapyard, it reverse engineers ship designs for the syndicate. However, the partly stripped hulks have stories of their own to tell and are well worth exploring.
Holy Order of the Pontifex Headquarters

After the gate realignment, the remaining Duke's Buccaneers were split by a schism not unlike that between the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex. A small group retained their faith in the nebulous machinations of their Pirate Duke, who was attempting to use the disorder of the Paranid Civil War to his advantage through diplomatic means, but the great majority showed no such inclination. Driven by the urge to restore their pre-Dark identity, these orthodox Buccaneers continued to pillage and plunder, hoarding the spoils in hidden-away stations, the locations of which remained a well-guarded secret. Surely, the Errant Duke, as they began to call him, would one day break free of his stupor, realise his misguided ways, and return to lead them on the path to greatness that they had once trodden together. To this day, these splinter groups do not see eye to eye, and it would require a significant upheaval to reconcile their ideologies under a unified banner once again.

These enigmatic installations are well-protected Kha'ak bases of operation. Often found close to busy mining regions, not much is known about them. The Kha'ak tend to construct them away from a system's centre, and they are built seemingly instantaneously. This leads some defence experts to believe that the Kha'ak might be in possession of warp technology powerful enough to move entire structures around the universe.

Positioned at the heart of Mitsuno's Revelation, the Lighthouse stands as a beacon of trade and commerce, serving as a vital nexus for the Quettanauts and their interactions with other factions. This station fills a multitude of essential functions, aimed at facilitating commerce, diplomacy, and cultural exchange. Its trade halls are filled with the bartering expected from a Quettanaut station and bustle with activity.

Boasting state-of-the-art manufacturing capabilities, and equipped with advanced fabrication machinery utilising automated assembly lines, the Light Vessel Assembly Plant complex provides not only the facilities for construction and trade of spaceships, but also a centre for engineers and craftsmen to share and improve the technology.\n\nThe Light Vessel Assembly Plant is also an important part of the Quettanauts' economy, trading with both internal and external markets. Higher value trades may seem impractical, but this station is well placed to provide the necessary storage and logistics to facilitate these types of transactions, often working as a form of escrow.

Pillars of Elysium stands as an enigmatic bastion amidst the celestial expanse of Mitsuno's Sacrifice, serving as the primary hub and sanctuary for the Quettanauts.\n\nSituated at the heart of Quettanaut territory, it provides a safe base of operations. Though many questions remain unanswered about this station, it is nevertheless an important location for anyone visiting the Quettanauts.

page.title: Landmarks
page.descr: Names and descriptions of landmarks
page.t: Originally installed by the Plutarch Mining Corporation, the so called Badlands Colony, not actually a colony but a mining operation, was however repurposed after the Albion gate powered down and as since served as an actual colony and stronghold to PMC senior staff. The fragment of the Broken Moon the station was built into had supposedly been chosen due to a large tunnel leading all the way from one side of the rock to the other allowing easy access to its interior through many shafts driven into its walls. One part of the installation still serves as a mining facility and is commonly referred to as The Mines.

Probably a candidate for the title of Profiteroid 2.0 the Lonely Giant brims with a strange concentration of 99% pure Hydrogen-3 in crystalline form. The visible crystals on the surface only amount for a tiny fraction of what deep scans have revealed to be immense chasms on the inside filled up with frozen Hydrogen-3. However, both the reason why the Lonely giant did not yet melt under the heat of Albion's central star nor willingly spread its wealth is the immensely hard silicate a majority of the rock is made up from, giving the PMC a hard time twisting its innards. For the meantime the two massive rocks orbiting one another are held in a containment field trapping the subliming Hydrogen-3 gas emanating from the surface crystals with the pretty side-effect of illuminating the whole scene in a soothing picturesque turquoise as the gas touches the particle barrier.

The Core Dig was the most prominent source for the Iridium isotope Ir-209, also known as the famous 'Unobtainium'. This is a stable and highly heat-resistant anti-ferromagnetic complex agent perfectly suited for fusion reaction containment. Such containment suffered from the previous lack of a material that was not also radio-activated under constant neutron radiation. Iridium-209, formerly considered non-existent in nature and ineffective through cost to synthesise, seemed to fit the bill. Unfortunately, as Matter/Antimatter technology emerged and increased its hold on the reactor market, Unobtainium faced a severe decline in demand and resale value compared to the cost of extraction and processing. The Core Dig now operates with a reduced crew and has redirected its operations to extract and store the trace Nividium also present in the minerals available.

The crude technology this large installation is based on still bears a glimpse of genius. Its core consists of a series of tunnel connections between some junction structures of different sizes upon which the surrounding gases were made to condense and crystallize under the influence of a chemical catalyst. Today the station has a crystalline coating of varying thickness between 100 and 500 Metres and will most likely form a solid asteroid-like mega-crystal a couple hundred years from now. The Lost Colony already has pioneers dig into the thicker areas of the coating expanding the station into it with some success now which makes it clear that this colony may very well grow into something far more befitting of such name.

As the M/AM drives gained popularity this behemoth among freshwater supply stations was quickly abandoned in favour of more readily accessible water sources. Before that however the Aqueduct was the Maelstrom system's largest freshwater supply installation and probably one of the largest facilities of its kind in the known universe. Today it is being swarmed by Xenon who lurk within the dense clouds of frozen H2O that span the space between the many asteroids around the Sable Vortex.

Named for the countless natural and artificial tunnels that snake through it, the Maze is the huge broken asteroid in which the Jump Gate in Fields of Opportunity is situated. The nature of the tunnels, which run from one end of the asteroid to the other, lead the Teladi to believe that the Maze was broken up for mining by one of the system's previous occupants, though there is no evidence to suggest who these settlers may have been.

Though Overwatch still receives a supply of Teladianium from the foundries in Fields of Opportunity, after a Jump Gate realignment the Habitat-class "superstation" was cut off from most of the technology it requires to manufacture ships from its dedicated shipyard. Even though it now depends on Albion for these technologies, Overwatch still has much to offer the system, since it provides food and energy to all the stations still scattered across Serpentine Haze and Fatal Path. More importantly, however, it is home to thousands of Teladi civilians and the headquarters of the Teladi Union, making it the first port of call for any traveller coming to Fields of Opportunity.

The Teladi of Fields of Opportunity have always struggled against the Xenon that exist on the outskirts of the system, but mass incursions into the system by the Xenon are rare. When they have occurred, however, they have always ended in bloodshed. The so-called "War Memorial" is perhaps the largest of the battle scars, and was left in the far north of Serpentine Haze in commemoration of the Teladi who sacrificed themselves to make sure their comrades would escape unharmed.\n\nRealising that they did not have the firepower to push the Xenon back, three Teladi captains ordered their crews to abandon ship before ramming the Branch 9 Xenon K leading the attack and causing it to crash into the side of an asteroid. The subsequent explosion destroyed everything in the vicinity, but ended what had been one of the Teladi's most vicious and bloody conflicts.
(Stronghold description)This Split station has been taken over by an Argon slave insurrection.

This vast and ornate cathedral constitutes a centrepiece of Paranid tradition, a blazing symbol of its architects' imperishable past and future. Whatever its elaborate architecture may conceal, no truly devout Paranid would dare spill another's blood in its consecrated aura of sanctity.

(Funeral Accelerator description after generic accelerator text){20001,1002}\n\nThis particular accelerator has been built by the Free Families for the funerals of their Patriarchs. Only dead Patriarchs are allowed to the other side, where they may float through the eternal void, forever undisturbed.

This imposing structure serves as headquarters and stronghold to the Duke's Buccaneers, a ruthless security outfit which turned to piracy and zealotry. Amid a labyrinth of defence platforms and production facilities resides their elusive leader, the Pirate Duke Reborn, ceaselessly scheming to contrive his next grand conquest.

(Hall of Judgement description)This station was built to control the colonial territories. It is used as a hub for police operations, a high court for prosecutions, and a prison for enemies of the colonial rule.

The once-elegant arcs and towering spires of this station wreckage betray it as the site of a pre-shutdown faction headquarters, which over decades seems to have succumbed to the erratic discharges of ill-maintained experimental weapons technology and the relentless efforts of the local scavenger fleet.

To an outsider, the palace of the Trinity of Pontifices might be emblematic of the triumph of grim reality over adamant dogma. To the Paranid, however, the Conclave of the Three represents a logical conclusion to an excruciating mathematical impossibility, at long last facilitating the glorious consolidation of the realm and the unification of its people.
Torus Aeternal Segment #34(speak Torus Aeternal as provided in sound sample, speak # as "number", speak 34 as "thirty-four")

The Torus Aeternal was an orbital ring station encircling and guarding planet Earth until the advent of the Second Terraformer War. The structure's scale and capabilities were unprecedented within the Jump Gate network. Tethers kept the station in a stable orbit and allowed for the transportation of people and wares between the station and the planet. While the outward-facing sections were completed, many of the sections facing Earth were still under construction. This limited the number of people present on the Torus Aeternal to an estimated 1 million.\n\nThe Torus Aeternal was ultimately destroyed during the Second Terraformer War. Two Argon infiltrators, Saya Kho and Sherman Hiatu, initiated an emergency procedure known as segment-separation, during which the station separated into its 420 constituent segments and drifted into higher orbit, irrevocably destroying the Torus. This destruction of the Torus triggered all out war with the Argon Federation(same as {20203,201}).

Centuries old, this Gate wreckage is a sombre memorial to the First Terraformer War. It reminds the Terrans of the Xenon roots in Terran technology, the Xenon threat to the survival of Earth, and the sacrifices the Terrans had to make. Had it not been for the heroic actions of the Dragonfyre(same as {30602,101}), drawing the Terraformers through this Gate before its destruction, Earth and all humans in Sol would have succumbed to the machines. The resulting 500 years of isolation, knowing what lies beyond and yet confined to this small corner of the galaxy, were considered a small price to pay for the survival of Earth.

After the rediscovery of the lost colony of Aldrin, the former United Space Command decided to establish a lasting Jump Gate connection. The commissioned Jump Gate would be the third Gate created by Terran engineering. Neptune was chosen as the location for the new Jump Gate, its distance to Earth being a compromise; close enough for trade, but far enough not to become a major safety risk. The connection served people from both sides, allowing for economic, scientific and cultural exchange after centuries of separation. Like the rest of the gate network, this connection was lost during the Jump Gate shutdown.\n\nEven with the Second Terraformer War on hold and the Jump Gate shutdown in progress, Terran relations with the Community of Planets were still poor at best. This led the Terran High Command to set up a covert operation to re-establish a connection using the Neptune Gate. The Terrans chose to connect the Gate to an old Gate in the Brennan's Triumph system, originally destroyed during the First Terraformer War. After moving the alien Jump Gate to the far outskirts of Brennan's Triumph and repairing it, the Terrans managed to establish a connection and keep it secret for several years. After the Jump Gate in the Asteroid Belt shut down, the Neptune Gate prevented Sol from being fully disconnected from the Gate network once again. With the help of an independent entrepreneur, the Terrans connected the outskirts of Brennan's Triumph with its core, establishing their hegemony over the system.
Torus Aeternal Wreckage(speak Torus Aeternal as provided in sound sample)

The Aurora Casino is the largest gambling establishment in the network, known for drawing in hopeful gamblers from all over the galaxy. In this bustling venue, tourists mix with thugs and gangsters, as the station also serves as an unofficial gathering place for the Vigor Syndicate(Vigor Syndicate same as {20203,3301}) and other shady organisations.

(Eye of the Beholder)This sleek, almost featureless, structure of arcane origin hovers at a safe observation distance from a black hole. At times, well-adjusted scanners can pick up a strange frequency, seemingly humming in tune with the system's background radiation, and bearing remarkable similarities to the Tide phenomenon in Avarice. The alien artefact's surface shows signs of a concerted, but only partially successful, effort to penetrate its hull and unearth its secrets. A tangle of tubes attaches to what appears to be a dispenser mechanism, pried open and held in place by crude scaffolding.

(Tidebreak)Shortly after the first Tides devastated the Avarice system in 800 \(NT\), one abandoned mining facility built into an asteroid was found to be sturdy enough to withstand the Tide. The Avarice Company Ore Extraction Plant #001 soon became a shelter. It was renamed to Tidebreak and gradually developed into the station it is today. This safe haven would soon be the only remaining station in Avarice, until the Northriver Company introduced Protectyon in 818 \(NT\). This allowed Avarice to recycle the station wrecks and resettle the system, by building new stations protected by Protectyon Shield Generators. Now, Tidebreak is used as a trading hub from which Northriver sells the Protectyon that is required to power the Shield Generators.(Protectyon Shield Generator same as {20104,92501})

A derelict ship, broken apart and floating far from inhabited space. The design suggests that it is of Boron origin. It appears that the ship came under a major attack of some kind. It is too ravaged to salvage any more useful data from its systems.
Inactive Gate(Gate buried inside a huge asteroid but still visible)

Antigone stands as a beacon of unity, cooperation and interstellar commerce among the diverse races of the Commonwealth. Its cosmopolitan design, bustling thoroughfares teeming with life and activity, labyrinthine corridors, and crowded marketplaces all become apparent to the traveller when they first reach the station. At one point Antigone tried to run with the slogan "If you can't find it on Antigone, then you haven't asked the right trader". This was plastered on banners, and on merchandise and souvenirs available to travellers. It was generally considered as unsuccessful, but the graphic design has launched a niche community of fans.

Funanori Station(Funanori Station same as {20103,3901}) is an innovative endeavour to consolidate multiple local stations' functionality into one large station, with the aim of protecting against the rapidly increasing hostility in the sector. While this has led to significant criticism regarding centralised dependencies and having a single point of failure for the sector, it is undeniable that, to this date, it has provided a significant increase in efficiency, which given the diminishing local resources, is enough to silence most of its critics.\n\nAs the population of Getsu Fune longs to be free of what is fast becoming a terrible place for them to live, many rumours and speculations have begun circulating. Among these, the prevalent theory is that the station is built around experimental technology that is designed to allow the station to move. So far none of these have been substantiated and are generally considered mere wishful thinking.

Nestled within the shadows of asteroid clusters, Anarchy Port stands as a notorious bastion of lawlessness within the chaotic expanse of Loomanckstrat's Legacy. At the heart of its operations lies its stringent security measures designed to ensure that only those deemed worthy gain entry. Automated scanning systems meticulously inspect approaching vessels, searching for any signs of hidden law enforcement presence. This precautionary measure has earned Anarchy Port a reputation for being a safe harbour for pirates seeking respite from the constant threat of retribution. Of the pirate captains drawn here, the most prolific command the utmost respect and influence on the station, their prowess in combat and cunning in strategy earning them the admiration of their peers. Beneath them, a diverse array of rogues, mercenaries, and outcasts eke out a living through various illicit activities, from smuggling contraband to teaming up to raid unsuspecting trade convoys.

The disputed seat of power of the Second Duchy, this grand station stands as the pinnacle of Paranid technology, boasting the famed towering spires adorned with the sparkling crystalline maja-lattice coating.\n\nIn the wake of the shutdown, the Paranid of Cardinal's Domain were left without their Cardinal. In desperation, the sector was run by a council, acting as the sector's stewards, until the Cardinal's eventual return. Upon reconnection to the gate network, they have happily stepped down and accepted a new Cardinal, appointed by the Godrealm.

Memento Mori stands as a solemn sentinel, its silhouette a stark reminder of President's End's turbulent past and the Kha'ak battle that once ravaged the sector. At its heart lies the shattered remains of a colossal Kha'ak capital ship, its fractured hull now ensconced within the steel embrace of the station. Amid the echoes of the past, and a quiet solitude that comes from the hulking remains, there is also a sense of hope, a constant reminder of the resilience of its people.

As a centre for propulsion research and development, this research station plays a pivotal role in pushing the boundaries of space exploration and technology. Scientists and engineers stationed at the outpost work tirelessly to develop and test new propulsion systems, and theoretical models, aimed at unlocking enhanced potential for travel among the stars.\n\nThis outpost has also become a tourist destination and retreat, with some people visiting purely for the peace that can be found in a place of science in a quiet corner of the universe, while others are more interested in the advancement of science, and want to see first hand the future of space travel.

The Free Argon Trading Station, initially conceived as a nexus solely for trade and commerce, has inadvertently spawned an entire economic ecosystem around its bustling core. What began as a hub for business transactions has blossomed into a vibrant marketplace teeming with ancillary services and attractions. From holographic cinemas and casinos, to bustling eateries and bars, the station now offers a wide range of amenities catering to the diverse needs and interests of its visitors. Consequently, it has transcended its original purpose, evolving into a sought-after tourist destination frequented by travellers from across the galaxy.

This type of communication station was once widely deployed throughout the known Gate Network by the Paranid Empire. While their purpose was officially described as scientific, intelligence gathered over decades suggests they may have served as covert military monitoring stations.\n\nThis particular installation, however, appears to have been abandoned for an indeterminate period, likely as a result of the increasing frequency of Jump Gate disconnections that heralded the era now known as The Dark.

page.title: Station Modules
page.descr: Names and descriptions of station modules
page.t:
Let's face it, owning a spaceship is a necessity in almost all civilised regions of space, no matter how densely populated the official census data makes them appear. Owning two spaceships differentiates the entrepreneur from the middle class, private owner. However, owning three, six, twelve - or however many - spaceships elevates the distinguished gentle-being to the upper class, the one-percenters that can. And if we're honest, what multi-millio-, billio-, quadrillionaire would place their shiny valuable spacecrafts into a parking orbit around some inconsequential moon in a godforsaken star system, never to be appreciated by anyone? That is right, none!

The rule of wealth goes like this: if you own it, show it. Place it into a lustrous hall, have its hull polished by an army of exquisite robot hands, bathed in blinding lights by a laser beam from above. And then, if you have your romantic interest over for dinner, or your prospective business partner - or your grand elder-being, for that matter - parade them past your luxury vehicles.

You earned it!

The Protectyon Shield Generator(same as {20104,92501}) was designed by the Northriver Company's Research and Development team. It is constructed in such a way that, when supplied with Protectyon condensate, it generates shielding that protects the entire station from the devastating effects of the Tide. As part of this process the Protectyon is depleted. Due to the high potency of Protectyon, and the incredible volatility inherent in such a substance, the module's design only allows for a small storage capacity.
This module extends the Habitat-class superstation so that it can support additional modules behind its primary ring. These attach to the extension module in a spoke-like fashion.
Used primarily for structural support between a Habitat-class superstation's centre and its primary ring, this spoke-like column also holds quarters for the station's workers and inhabitants.
Forming the heart of the Habitat-class superstation, the HCC houses most of its administrative sectors, as well as about a third of its living space.

Placed in the inner-side of the Habitat-class superstation's primary ring, the city is home to thousands of citizens and station workers. When designing the station, the Teladi Company attempted to make the city suitable not just for Teladi, but for as many species as possible, and so it is not unusual to find cities with many different biomes.

Forming the central structural support to the Habitat-class superstation's primary ring, this small ring also extends from the Habitat Centre Complex to act as an entrance to the station for any ships that wish to dock.
These components of the Habitat-class superstation house huge trading floors where official and civilian traders can go to trade wares and produce.

As well as acting as secondary support for the Habitat-class superstation's primary ring, the bridge also provides high-speed transport from the ring to the complex centre and ring extension, allowing citizens and station workers to travel around the station.
Penthouse Observation Deck(on top/bottom of station)
Conservatory Observation Deck(on side of station, horizontal)
Pavilion Observation Deck(on side of station, vertical)

(*Gambling Welfare Effect Text*)A station offering a wide range of recreational activities can help set it apart from its competition, and will improve conditions for its workforce. Gambling establishments increase the rate at which a station's workforce grows.

{20104,110001}(Gambling Welfare Effect Text)\n\nThe Casino(same as {20104,110101}) is a monument to excess, which will draw visitors from all parts of the Jump Gate network. With its luxurious interior, well stocked bar, and wide range of games, it is guaranteed to keep its patrons enthralled and entertained for hours on end.

{20104,110001}(Gambling Welfare Effect Text)\n\nThe Gambling Den(same as {20104,110201}) is a modest, but cosy, space where workers can gather to gamble away their savings after a long shift. The establishment offers tables with a wide variety of games, and a bar for people to take occasional breaks and have some refreshments.
Pheromone Art Gallery(translation should be similar to that of {20227,1780})

{20104,110001}(Gambling Welfare Effect Text)\n\nThe Pheromone Art Gallery(Pheromone Art Gallery same as {20104,110301}) exhibits the most fragrant and fin-tingling pieces of art created in the Royal Academy. This is sure to attract many a Boron, but even olfactorily underequipped friends will find this well worth a visit as audiovisual supplements are provided for every piece.

The Jump Gate shutdown left many sectors with very limited access to resources, prompting stranded Argon engineers to begin development of advanced recycling facilities. One of these was the Scrap Processor; a module designed to process S and M-sized ship wrecks into scrap, which in turn can be recycled into other useable resources. The first Tug ships were also introduced at this time, to transport the wrecks to the Scrap Processor. Scrap Cubes were a later introduction, designed to allow larger wrecks to be compacted into blocks suitable for towing and processing.

The arrival of the first interstellar messenger drones after the Fall of the Gates encouraged the administrations of many sectors to share survival-critical information with now inaccessible neighbouring systems, including blueprints for the new recycling technology. The aim was to help resource-disadvantaged populations, in the hope of receiving important information in return.

This system of mutual information exchange worked so well that many sectors maintained it locally even after Jump Gate connections were restored.(Raw Scrap same as {20201,6801}, Scrap Metal same as {20201,6601}, Tug same as {20221,5051}, Scrap Cube same as {20109,10801})

The Jump Gate shutdown left many sectors with very limited access to resources, prompting stranded engineers to design advanced recycling facilities. One of these was the Allographyne Scrap Processor; a module designed to process Kha'ak ship wrecks into Allographyne Fragments, which in turn can be recycled into other useable resources.

The arrival of the first interstellar messenger drones after the Fall of the Gates encouraged the administrations of many sectors to share survival-critical information with now inaccessible neighbouring systems, including blueprints for the new recycling technology. The aim was to support resource-disadvantaged populations, in the hope of receiving important information in return.

This system of mutual information exchange worked so well that many sectors maintained it locally even after Jump Gate connections were restored.(Allographyne Fragments same as {20201,7401})

The Jump Gate shutdown left many sectors with very limited access to resources, prompting stranded Argon engineers to begin development of advanced recycling facilities. One of these was the Scrap Recycler; a module designed to process scrap into usable resources, converting them into Hull Parts and Claytronics in alternating production cycles.

The arrival of the first interstellar messenger drones after the Fall of the Gates encouraged the administrations of many sectors to share survival-critical information with now inaccessible neighbouring systems, including blueprints for the new recycling technology. The aim was to help resource-disadvantaged populations, in the hope of receiving important information in return.

This system of mutual information exchange worked so well that many sectors maintained it locally even after Jump Gate connections were restored.(Scrap Metal same as {20201,6601}, Hull Parts same as {20201,1201}, Claytronics same as {20201,501})

The Jump Gate shutdown left many sectors with very limited access to resources, prompting stranded engineers to design advanced recycling facilities. One of these was the Allographyne Scrap Recycler; a module designed to recycle Allographyne Fragments into usable resources by converting them into Allographyne.

The arrival of the first interstellar messenger drones after the Fall of the Gates encouraged the administrations of many sectors to share survival-critical information with now inaccessible neighbouring systems, including blueprints for the new recycling technology. The aim was to support resource-disadvantaged populations, in the hope of receiving important information in return.

This system of mutual information exchange worked so well that many sectors maintained it locally even after Jump Gate connections were restored.(Allographyne Fragments same as {20201,7401}, Allographyne same as {20201, 7601})

{20104,130102}\n\nUpon receiving blueprints for the Scrap Recycler, the Segaris Pioneers modified them to be compatible with their Terran economy. Instead of converting Scrap Metal to Hull Parts and Claytronics, their variant produced Silicon Carbide and Computronic Substrate in the same alternating fashion.(Silicon Carbide same as {20201,6301}, Computronic Substrate same as {20201,6001})

page.title: Weapons and Turrets
page.descr: Names and descriptions of weapons and turrets
page.t:
Many experienced pilots fondly remember the affordable and reliable Pulse Laser as their first weapon. Its pin-point accuracy and high projectile speed make it an excellent choice for fighting small and fast targets, handling fragile lockboxes, and for dealing with deployables like mines and laser towers. Often initially scoffed at for its comparatively low damage output, its slow heat generation and sublime cooling result in a steady stream of disruptive fire, which in turn rewards pilots who can stay on target for an extended period. Faced with larger enemies, the Pulse Laser does not become obsolete as quickly as one might expect. Used in greater numbers, it can still be a formidable choice against frigates and corvettes, though an upgrade to a larger weapon mount may be advisable to maintain a level playing field. The Pulse Laser remains the preferred choice of commanders who favour versatility over optimisation against specific opponents, or who have little trust in the aim of their subordinates.

The technology behind the Pulse Laser is advanced and efficient. Within a shielded chamber, microscopic fragments of matter are superheated and accelerated by a pulsed neodymium laser. The weapon was originally designed by the Ministry of Finance to provide a robust loadout for their escort fleets, without having to invest time and resources into the maintenance of a well-rounded combined arms setup. Over time, and thanks to the Teladi Company's aggressive marketing, it has been adopted as the number one weapon of convenience by all other former members of the Community of Planets.

The Mk2 variant sports a slightly longer burst. This lowers the efficiency of the heat dissipation between bursts and thereby exponentially drives up the cost of the internal shielding, but results in an overall higher damage output.

The Bolt Repeater offers balanced damage output and thermal performance, making it a common selection for general-purpose use. It is typically positioned as a progression from the Pulse Laser, retaining sustained firing capability while employing larger, slower-moving projectiles. This allows prolonged bursts capable of effectively engaging targets of comparable size, though effective use depends on disciplined burst control and heat management.

The reduced projectile velocity allows smaller, highly agile vessels to evade fire under favourable conditions. Against capital ships, the Bolt Repeater is suitable for disabling exposed surface elements such as turrets and shield generators, though its effectiveness against hull structures is limited.

The current Bolt Repeater design originates from Argon military development programmes based on earlier Mass Driver technology dating back to the Kha'ak conflict era. By removing shield-penetration capability and focusing instead on sustained projectile output, the resulting system achieved a reliable general-purpose profile that saw widespread adoption among Federation-aligned forces.

The Shard Battery is a short-range kinetic weapon system characterised by the simultaneous discharge of multiple projectiles. This configuration compensates for limited accuracy and effective range by delivering high damage against both shields and hulls. Functionally, the system is derived from the Bolt Repeater, though the requirement for a wider barrel aperture and increased projectile spacing results in higher energy consumption.\n\nIn terms of raw damage output, the Shard Battery is often compared to the Plasma Cannon, though it serves a different tactical role. It performs most effectively against larger, slower targets such as M-sized vessels, which are less able to evade its projectile spread. The weapon is also well suited to engaging capital ship surface elements from inside their defensive turrets' dead angle.

The Plasma Cannon is a long-range heavy weapon system delivering high damage per projectile. Its effectiveness is offset by slow projectile velocity, a low rate of fire, and substantial heat generation, making accurate shot placement critical. These characteristics favour its use against capital-class targets, where target size and predictability mitigate its handling limitations, particularly in concerted combat formations.

While short-range systems such as the Shard Battery and Split Tau Accelerator can exceed its damage output under optimal conditions, the Plasma Cannon's principal advantage lies in its extended engagement range. Although capable of engaging smaller vessels, effectiveness in such roles depends on favourable positioning and timing rather than sustained fire.

The Plasma Cannon was developed by the Holy Order of the Pontifex shortly after the onset of the Paranid Schism, building on earlier High Energy Plasma Thrower technology. As with its predecessor, high radiation build-up necessitates periodic purging between firing cycles to prevent damage to the weapon system. The design blueprint was later acquired by the Argon Secret Service and disseminated throughout the Commonwealth following the Argon Federation's entry into the conflict.

The Beam Emitter is a long-range energy weapon characterised by high accuracy and near-instantaneous impact. It projects a focused energy beam optimised for shield depletion rather than hull damage, leading to widespread use by both security forces and criminal organisations.\n\nAs with any energy weapon that generates thermal load during operation, sustained firing is more efficient than repeated short bursts.
For primary resource collectors, the Mk 1 Small Mining Drill is an entry-level tool used for asteroid mining. It is available in an upgraded Mk 2 format.

Developed by the Argon Navy in collaboration with Jinko-Tekina Technologies, this anti-shield weapon is an approximation of Boron ion technology, access to which was lost following the Jump Gate shutdown. While early prototypes underperformed, incremental enhancements to electrical field strength have significantly improved performance, narrowing the gap with the original design.\n\nIn addition to severe shield degradation, the weapon's electrical discharge can momentarily disable the travel drive, boost engine, and targeting systems on small to medium-class vessels.

The Muon Disintegrator deploys a short-range projectile that adheres to its target and disrupts electromagnetic bonds in both shielding and baryonic matter. While the muon particles remain active, affected shields and travel drives are unable to recharge, reducing the target's ability to disengage or recover under fire.\n\nDeveloped by the Ministry of Finance Science Division in response to advances in shield efficiency and travel drive regeneration, the system was intended as a countermeasure rather than a raw damage solution. Although early adoption was limited in favour of the more immediate output of plasma-based weapons, the increased presence of Terran and Boron propulsion technology has renewed operational interest in the Muon Disintegrator.

The Mass Driver launches a single high-energy kinetic projectile capable of retaining accuracy and effectiveness over extended ranges. Thermal charging commences upon weapon activation, allowing the operator to either discharge immediately or delay firing for improved targeting.

The Burst Ray is a short-range weapon system optimised for disabling capital ship surface elements. It delivers damage through rapid, sequenced emissions that apply concentrated radiation beams to exposed subsystems, causing the target's surface to lose molecular cohesion. This makes it particularly effective against engines, shield generators, and turret installations.

This specialised role comes with clear limitations. The Burst Ray exhibits limited effectiveness against primary shield arrays and hull structures, and its short engagement range restricts its utility in general-purpose combat, particularly against small and medium-sized vessels. The instantaneous application of its individual beams can nevertheless offer situational effectiveness against small and evasive targets.

The weapon's development is attributed to initiatives within the Paranid theocracy, reportedly commissioned in response to an increasing reliance on heavy fleets and long-range armaments during internal doctrinal shifts.

The Blast Mortar fires a compact high-explosive charge encapsulated by superheated chondritic material. A proximity fuse triggers detonation near the target, with a wide blast radius compensating for the system's limited accuracy. The affected area is sufficient to neutralise multiple surface elements on capital ships with a single discharge.

It is often compared favourably to the Plasma Cannon due to its higher projectile velocity, enabling limited engagement of smaller targets when required. However, it is not a flak weapon and is most effectively employed against medium or larger vessels that cannot readily evade fire.

Developed before the formal proclamation of the Holy Order of the Pontifex, the Blast Mortar reflects early Paranid efforts to maximise combat effectiveness under constrained industrial capacity. The result is a weapon that combines high destructive output with relative manufacturing simplicity.

The Split Boson Lance delivers a single, high-velocity projectile over an extended range, with negligible thermal output. Its primary limitation is its costly energy recuperation system, which requires extended recharge intervals and restricts the use of wider gimbal envelopes.

As a result, the Boson Lance is most commonly employed as a secondary weapon. Split fighter wings nevertheless frequently assign a single vessel equipped exclusively with this weapon for specialised interception and initial engagement.

The Boson Lance is a comparatively recent development originating from advanced Split weapons research. Following the reconnection of the Zyarth Patriarchy with the Commonwealth, the Patriarchy obtained the original schematics and adapted the design for large-scale manufacturing.

The Tau Accelerator is a short-range kinetic weapon optimised for high-impact engagements. Owing to its Split design, the Tau Accelerator delivers destructive force similar to the Shard Battery while its rapid rate of fire produces a demoralising effect on enemy combatants.

Compared to the Shard Battery, the Tau Accelerator delivers higher per-shot energy output and a tighter projectile spread. These gains are offset by reduced heat dissipation efficiency, shorter effective range, and a lower projectile count with diminished velocity. As a result, the weapon is most effective at close proximity, where its high rate of fire can rapidly overwhelm exposed targets before thermal limits are reached.

The Tau Accelerator remains in common use among Split bounty hunters, for whom close-range engagement is standard practice. In this operational context, its thermal constraints and limited reach are considered acceptable trade-offs for concentrated firepower and rapid target neutralisation.

The Split Neutron Gatling is a short-range, rapid-fire projectile weapon comparable to the Bolt Repeater. Like its Commonwealth counterpart, it produces a continuous stream of relatively slow-moving projectiles, requiring lead when engaging manoeuvring targets. The system delivers high collateral damage through projectile spread, at the cost of limited accuracy and reduced effectiveness against smaller targets, favouring close-range combat.\n\nThe weapon's design emphasises sustained fire and aggressive engagement profiles, reflecting Split combat doctrine. Its volume and persistence of fire can exert significant pressure during close-range encounters, despite limited targeting precision. While primarily a functional combat system, the Neutron Gatling is frequently associated with engagement patterns that prioritise psychological dominance.

The Split Thermal Disintegrator is a short-range weapon designed to bypass shielding. On impact, its projectiles adhere to the target's hull, inflicting sustained thermal damage over time. This persistent effect can interfere with shield and travel drive regeneration.\n\nDeveloped through Split research into shield-penetration technologies, the system did not achieve full shield negation. However, its reliable partial bypass and operational versatility proved sufficient for broad deployment.

The Meson Stream is a high-output beam weapon designed for extreme-range engagements. It emits a single transient beam that reaches the target at relativistic velocities. As is the case with other high-precision systems, its limited gimbal envelope restricts its effectiveness against nearby or fast-moving targets. This limitation is largely mitigated by the weapon's optical configuration, which is optimised for long-range focus. At distances below its effective range, beam coherence degrades rapidly, resulting in a steep reduction in destructive output.

Due to its exceptionally high energy demand and thermal load, the Meson Stream can only be installed on high-energy weapon mounts.

The system borrows its concept from large-scale directed-energy weapons first explored by the now defunct Terran AGI Task Force. Although it required the development of an entirely novel platform and operates with a notably inefficient energy profile, its value as a long-range deterrent was considered sufficient to justify these constraints. The Meson Stream represents the first operational result of this programme, marking an initial but deliberate step by the Terran Protectorate toward fielding super-heavy directed-energy armaments.

The Terran Proton Barrage is a short-range weapon system compatible exclusively with high-energy weapon mounts. It represents the Terran high-energy counterpart to the Commonwealth Bolt Repeater. Compared to its Commonwealth equivalent, the Proton Barrage offers increased damage output and projectile velocity at the expense of effective range. While delivering greater overall damage, it operates at a lower rate of fire, favouring more powerful individual projectiles during extended bursts.

The system is restricted to Terran ship designs due to its mount requirements and it carries a significantly higher acquisition cost than the standard Bolt Repeater. Despite these limitations, the Proton Barrage fulfils a general-purpose role and performs effectively across a broad range of target profiles.

The origins of the Terran Proton Barrage began after the reconnection with the Commonwealth, when the Terran Secret Service obtained Bolt Repeater design blueprints, enabling Terran engineers to refine its design and develop adjustments for high-energy mount capability. These modifications resulted in increased power output while producing a weapon system distinct from its Commonwealth predecessor.

The Kha'ak Kyon Emitter offers limited individual output when compared with contemporary beam weapons. Its effectiveness relies on massed deployment: when employed in coordinated swarm formations, multiple emitters can be brought to bear simultaneously, resulting in a cumulative damage profile capable of overwhelming targets despite the weapon's modest standalone performance.

The Xenon Impulse Projector is a high-rate, low-velocity projectile weapon, which in the wrong circumstances, can be a particular threat to smaller vessels. It seems that novel converter topologies enable a greater range than would be expected under current understanding of the technology.

The Terran Pulse Laser is a variant of the standard pulse-based weapon widely deployed throughout the Jump Gate network, and incorporates superior Terran optics. While its effective range is shorter than most Commonwealth implementations, higher projectile velocity, and the resulting reduction of in-flight time, improve overall hit consistency. As with comparable pulse weapons, it favours sustained fire and continuous target tracking over short, high-damage engagements.\n\nFollowing the Gate Realignment, the Terran Protectorate evaluated contemporary armaments and adapted the existing Pulse Laser design to Terran manufacturing standards. The resulting system preserves the weapon's core operating principles while incorporating structural and optical changes intended to restrict unauthorised replication. Although initially considered unsuitable for use by foreign arms providers, the design has since been integrated into a diverse range of vessels with only minor compromises.

Boron Phase weaponry is an iteration of particle accelerator weapons first developed by the Paranid and Argon. The fired energy pulses, consisting of highly accelerated and polarised particles, prove effective against hull, while less so against shielded targets. This puts Phase weaponry in a unique position among the Boron arsenal, which otherwise tends towards primarily impairing shields and mobility. As a necessary last resort against undeterrable hostiles, Phase armaments are widely available as either weapons or turrets in various sizes, and form the backbone of Boron weaponry and fleet compositions.

Boron Arc weaponry is a utility-class armament designed not only to inflict damage but to impair a target's targeting capabilities. It fires ionised particles that trigger electrical discharges on impact. Unlike conventional ion weapons, the resulting energy fields are calibrated to disrupt sensitive sensor circuits rather than deplete shields.\n\nThe turret-mounted variant is particularly valued on civilian vessels, which prioritise evasion over direct engagement. Originally developed and authorised for field use by the Royal Boron Military Defence, Arc weaponry remains classified as experimental.(Royal Boron Military Defence same as {20233,1021})

The Ion Gatling was developed by Faded Dreams Defences to improve the chances of Boron dogfighters. Its electrically charged particles are not only effective against shields, but also impair the target's mobility and allow the attacker to pin down hostile fighters. This proved effective against regular Split incursions, but the weapon's specialisation requires it to be combined with other weapons or fleets to supplement its shortcomings in hull penetration. To counter the Ion Gatling's proficiency against inept Split shields, Split raiders started deploying fighters without shields.(Faded Dreams Defences same as {20233,1051})
For primary resource collectors, the Mk1 Small Mining Drill is an entry-level tool used for asteroid mining.

The Gamma HEPT(Gamma HEPT same as {20105,1551}) was developed as a cutting-edge weapon and represents a pioneering advancement in plasma weaponry. This weapon epitomises the fusion of innovation and practicality, designed to provide unparalleled firepower in the unforgiving depths of space. Drawing upon the fundamental principles of plasma manipulation, the Gamma HEPT projects a torrent of searing energy spheres with devastating force.\n\nWhile future iterations on this same design improve and refine the concept, this early version is perhaps the most important. It marks the point at which the balance of power and reliability was such that it became a truly formidable weapon as opposed to a purely experimental one.

The Electromagnetic Gun is an Earth Fleet weapon system belonging to the family of e/m armaments. These systems operate by generating high-energy electromagnetic fields to compact and accelerate small plasma spheres, resulting in projectiles capable of partially bypassing shield defences.\n\nAs the smallest implementation within this family, the Electromagnetic Gun maintains an exceptional rate of fire, making it suitable for vessels expected to engage in close-range combat.

Originally used as a construction tool, the Needler Gun remains at its core what it has always been, a huge nail gun designed for heavy duty construction projects. Over time the Xenon have adapted it from firing mundane nails and rivets, to having ammunition chambers housing armour-piercing projectiles, allowing it to deliver devastating blows to enemy ships.(note: similar to {20105,7022}, just de-emphasising the size a little)\n\nThe Needler Gun's high rate of fire transforms what would otherwise be a minor annoyance into a significant stopping power. It is able to cover its target with hits at a rate that can produce significant structural damage in a short amount of time.
{20105,1102}\n\nMore established miners generally opt for the Medium Mining Drill, which is also available in Mk 1 and Mk 2 configurations.
{20105,1402}\n\nThe Kyon Emitter has also been seen, and in some cases salvaged, in a format comparable to Medium Class conventional weapons. As expected, this larger format is more damaging.
{20105,1412}\n\nThe Impulse Projector has been observed in an apparent Medium Class format, which takes this Xenon technology to a higher level of lethality.

This ship module is apparently a Xenon Mining Drill, however, it is unclear what performance it delivers and whether it is optimised for the collection of specific minerals. There is continued debate over whether this module has other applicable uses.

The Ion Atomiser is a weapon system based on Paranid and Teladi Phased Shockwave Generator technology. Its compressed energy projectiles expand on impact, creating a series of phased energy shockwaves, which greatly deplete shields and disrupt ship systems. During launch, each projectile is primed to detonate after covering the distance between the barrel and the target at the time of launch, effectively limiting the projectiles lifespan. This timed detonation catches targets in the resulting explosion, even if those targets narrowly avoid a direct impact, turning near misses into hits. Some Boron pilots have reported, with relief, that this time fuse has also prevented some cases of friendly fire. While the Ion Atomiser is said to be difficult to use against small, fast targets, some creative and experienced pilots manage to do so.

Ion Pulse armaments use magnetic acceleration to launch ionised shards of super-heated plasma. As with most Boron armaments, such projectiles are more effective in depleting shields than damaging hulls of unshielded targets. Nevertheless, this weapon system, developed by Eleius Astrosecurity, excels at its intended purpose of intercepting fighters. As such Ion Pulse Turrets and Railguns are widely used on Boron military ships, and are known to clear a safe passage through enemy formations.(Eleius Astrosecurity same as {20233,1041})

{20105,1512}\n\n\More established miners generally opt for the Medium Mining Drill, designed, field-tested and distributed by Deepwater Drilling Industries.(Deepwater Drilling Industries same as {20233,1071})

The Electromagnetic Cannon is an Earth Fleet weapon system based on electromagnetic acceleration technology, designed to deliver high-energy, discrete plasma projectiles. It employs electromagnetic field generators to compact and accelerate plasma spheres to high velocity, resulting in substantial impact force on target.\n\nCompared to turret-mounted variants, the system prioritises concentrated, high-impact fire over sustained pressure. This makes it particularly suitable for defensive engagements against medium-sized vessels, where controlled, decisive strikes can be applied to neutralise individual threats.

Though originally designed for salvage operations to disassemble wrecks, the Plasma Cutter Beam(Plasma Cutter Beam same as {20105,2571}) has been repurposed into a deadly weapon of war.\n\nOperating on a principle of short-lived bursts of devastating energy, the Plasma Cutter Beam boasts a formidable initial onslaught capable of inflicting heavy damage upon unsuspecting adversaries. Though its reload time is protracted and its lifespan brief, when used effectively, the coordinated fire of multiple beams can unleash a torrent of destruction upon any target within range.

Manufactured by Theonray Defence Corporation under Argon Federation contract, the Heavy Scalar Aperture Emitter (HSAE) is a high-energy weapon system that bypasses conventional shielding by exploiting Planck-time discontinuities in shield emitter cycles. These micro-apertures allow the beam to inflict direct damage to hull and structural elements, making it effective for disabling capital ships or other targets. Enhanced tracking algorithms maximise dwell time on moving targets, placing the HSAE in direct competition with conventional energy weapons. The HSAE can be fitted to Envoy and Cypher class ships.

The Heavy Distortion Pulsor was developed by the Joint Teladi Defence Consortium for use in the Ministry of Finance's Envoy-class fleet. It fires a coherent matter wave at relativistic speed which discharges on impact, temporarily disabling and immobilising smaller targets. The weapon's high accuracy stems from its underlying quantum emission principle. The Heavy Distortion Pulsor can only be fitted to Envoy- and Cypher-class ships.

The Argon Behemoth main battery is a powerful and reliable capital ship weapon, albeit lacking in showiness. Designed in a rare period of Argon peacetime, it smacks of something of an afterthought.

Legend has it that the first Behemoth was in service for three standard months before the Captain and crew realised that the Argon Prime shipyard had, in fact, neglected to install the main battery.

All requests to the Argon military for confirmation of this rumour are generally met with dark silence and furrowed brows.

Weaponsmith Ebmancketvahs considered the Odysseus main battery to be his career crowning achievement.
