(bad grammar intended)ArgFed fleet attack Split space. Puny attempt; Split laugh. You destroy fleet!

page.title: Terran vs Xenon War
page.descr: Texts for the 'Terran vs Xenon war' mission-group and sub-mission variants
page.t: The Community of Planets' irresponsible inaction in containing the Xenon has once again demonstrated that Sol can only be safe if the Terran Protectorate takes a proactive stance. We request that any able citizen of the Sol system reports to their designated representative. Furthermore, we also welcome any individual from outside Sol, as long as they prove to be capable.
These machines threaten everything we hold dear. It is crucial that we never budge, no matter the cost! Be vigilant! Destroy the enemy!
Despite our best efforts, the Xenon have been steadily approaching our borders and their numbers are rapidly growing.
Reconnaissance has picked up a significant number of Xenon ships heading right for the Sol system.

Our recent engagements with Xenon forces have resulted in massive losses on their side. However, this does not change the fact that there is still a significant Xenon presence right outside our borders.
Terran scouts have registered a large Xenon presence not too far from here. While their proximity is alarming, we now know where they are, which means we can engage them on our terms.

Our military has suffered heavy losses, and the Xenon are encroaching on Protectorate territory. We have to turn the tide while we still can. It is of vital importance that we re-establish a secure perimeter and set up our defences, or the Sol system will be overrun.
These machines just won't stop coming. Their sheer numbers are overwhelming. The consequences of Xenon ships slipping through our defences this close to Earth would be disastrous.
We simply cannot afford any holes in our line of defence. It needs to be air-tight.
This war has reached the point where any negligence could result in untold civilian lives lost. A solid defence has to be our immediate priority.
If we ever want to win this war, we have to make sure we have a stable base of operations. There cannot be any doubt about whether our defences will hold the Xenon at bay.

The Xenon fleet regularly attempts to intrude into our space, but our defence system is maintaining the battle line and decimating their numbers. Even so, we have to make sure that our defences are adequately prepared for any possible attack.

Our forces are continuing to clash with the Xenon. Right now, we have the advantage that we are fighting close to home, and we can use all of the defensive measures we have put in place to provide our pilots with backup.
It is our first priority to ensure that all protocols are in place, and all of our defensive systems are in working order.
You can help us with this immense task. Our work here, if done with diligence, will save many lives.
So far we have not been able to stop the Xenon advance. Unfortunately, we can no longer dismiss the possibility of having to engage them, here, in the Sol system.
So far, all attempts at defending against the Xenon have resulted in heavy losses. It has become painfully obvious that our defences are not adequate for the threat we are facing.
These recent developments have underlined the need for stronger security to be in place.
We ask anyone with the necessary capabilities to help by building defence stations and expanding our fleet, to aid us in our endeavour of creating a more secure Sol system.
Since the enemy is so close by, time is of the essence. It is crucial that anyone capable of helping us significantly increase our security, does so.

The Xenon fleets trying to gain entry into our territory are suffering from heavy attrition thanks to our valiant troops. We have to ensure that we support the troops by supplying replacements and fortifying their defences.
The Protectorate is renowned for its military supremacy. What people might not realise, though, is that it takes a lot of effort to maintain our fleets and defence stations.
Now, with the enemy at our gates, it is key that we act swiftly, and decisively.
It is for this reason that we must turn to outside help. If you can help deliver fleets or build defence stations, you are duty-bound to do so.
We are asking anyone experienced in ship or station construction to aid us in our task. Lives depend on it.
With the Xenon so close at hand, we had little option but to focus all of our attention on keeping them back. Now, that narrow focus has resulted in our supply lines coming under threat.
Unfortunately, the Xenon fleet's movement has caused some areas, specifically ones that the Protectorate usually relies on for resources, to become unavailable. This is unacceptable.
A resource shortage in this critical situation could lose the war and seal all our fates.

While we increase pressure on the Xenon fleet in an attempt to push it back from our borders, we need the help of someone who can identify new ways of procuring the required resources that fuel this war effort.

Resource availability has to become our second-largest focus, next to protecting our system from being overrun. Things are not looking good, and we need help with maintaining a reliable resource supply.

While our recent war efforts have been going well, Command is worried about potential supply shortages. Some of our usual ways of obtaining resources have become unavailable due to the shifting war front.

Thanks to the tremendous efforts of our troops, the Xenon are losing ground. We are steadily pushing them away from our borders. However, we are also worried that our current resource supplies might not be sufficent, should the Xenon launch a prolonged counter-offensive.
These resources are of critical importance in maintaining our fleet.

As such, it is important to ensure the supply of raw materials and resources. Outsourcing these urgent tasks would take a lot of pressure off of our own military. If you have the facilities, please consider taking up this responsibility.
The Xenon attacks are unrelenting. Our fleet is able to hold them off, but just barely. Anything that tips the scales in their favour might become a watershed moment, and our system could be overrun.

The fighting outside our borders has not let up. We are taking heavy casualties, and so are they. The battle lines have become very entrenched, and High Command does not like them to be drawn this close to home.
We need more room to manoeuvre. If we could ease the pressure, we could focus on rebuilding our defences, stocking up our supplies and starting to push back.
We need more fighters on our side. You would not have to beat back their entire fleet. It would suffice if you hit them enough to tip the scales back in our favour.
Right now, we need all the help we can get. Any combat pilot who is capable of inflicting casualties on the Xenon is welcome to join our efforts.
The results of our ongoing military campaign have far exceeded our expectations. We have a real opportunity to push the Xenon fleet away from our borders for good.
While it is worrying that the Xenon were ever able to establish a presence so close to our system in the first place, our fleet has done a tremendous job of keeping them in check.
If we can press our advantage, and do not let up, we will be able to regain ground currently occupied by the Xenon, and re-establish a safety zone between them and Sol.
If you are an experienced Pilot, we invite you to take part in this initiative. Destroy as many of these machines as you can. It will help turn the tides of war.

The Terran Secret Service is preoccupied with a number of operations outside Sol, so they have reached out and asked to outsource all intelligence work pertaining to the Xenon threat outside our borders.
Despite the worrying fact that the Xenon have established a presence close to our system, we do not have much actionable intelligence on their numbers, or their movements.

Accurate information is critical to waging a war. Especially if you are up against an enemy that, while fundamentally unpredictable, has at times displayed recognisable patterns. We can leverage that fact to our advantage.

With the Xenon having managed to gain a foothold so close to our home, we need any advantage we can get. Even in the face of superior technology, or a much larger fleet, almost any battle can be turned around through actionable intel.

There are tasks which will help improve the data we have gathered on the Xenon. Some of them might bring you into close contact with them, while others are less direct. They are all equally important to securing Terran space.
To be able to defend our system, we are dependent on capable pilots to map out the enemy territory, and gather as much intelligence as possible without them putting themselves at risk.

The military has been making good progress in pushing the Xenon away from our gates. However, we frequently lose ships due to a lack of information on enemy movement and fleet strength. This issue is quite unfortunate, but it can be addressed.

After much back and forth, the Protectorate has finally gained the upper hand, and can purge the Xenon outside their gates. However, in order to ensure all machines are located and properly dealt with, we need to gather more intelligence.
An increase in the quality and quantity of the information we gather could save Terran lives and help eradicate the Xenon presence going forward.
We have assembled a list of tasks that need to be fulfilled to improve our intel. You can help us establish the new network that will deliver this crucial information to our headquarters.

The Xenon have gained significant ground on us. It is simply unacceptable to cede control of our territory to them. For this reason, High Command has decreed the reclamation of lost ground to be our highest priority.
In fighting the enemy, our military has suffered heavy losses. For that reason, we ask that everyone, no matter what their specialisation, gets involved in our takeover efforts.
You do not have to be a brave combat pilot to leave a mark. You can transport officers to the front, or set up a defensive perimeter in the sector. All are duty-bound to do their part.
Through the united efforts of our valiant military branches, we have gained a position of strength over the Xenon. We have to press the advantage, and move forward into Xenon space.

Taking Xenon territory is a crucial objective on the path to winning this war. It will significantly weaken their forces, and each system we free from this scourge means one more layer of protection between us and them.
To ensure that this advance is a success, everyone who is capable of helping is urged to do their part. You can ferry officers, secure objectives or deliver supplies; it does make a difference!

We have suffered significant losses, and morale is waning. High Command is putting pressure on us to produce a victory to show to the Terran people. To that end we have identified a Xenon station of note.

We have identified a station, not far from our system, that supplies the Xenon fleet. If we were to tear it down, we would be able to slow the Xenon attacks, and potentially open up that system for a counter-offensive.
It has now become our top priority to take it down, not only to weaken the Xenon foothold in the system, but also to lift the spirits of our military cadets, and the civilian population.
Tearing down a hostile station is no small feat. This is why we only approach the most trusted and powerful of our allies to execute this operation.
Right now the situation is critical. If we do not take that station down, we might lose the war. Only our most powerful allies will be capable of helping us with this undertaking.

We have fought long and hard to secure our borders from the Xenon. It seems their attacks have grown less intense. Now, we have to seize the moment, first to significantly reduce their presence here, and then to push them away from our system.

We are able to defend ourselves quite well from the Xenon. A certain routine has set in, where our fighters know exactly how to engage them. The problem is, this status quo will not be broken if we do not change tack.
We must be coordinated, and strike the enemy with determination. We have to come together with the single purpose of destroying their Xenon station.
This task is only suitable for the most trusted, powerful allies of the Protectorate. However, should you succeed in tearing down the station, you will have significantly improved our situation.

The Xenon may have set up their base somewhere far from Sol, but that does not mean that we can turn a blind eye to the infestation. They continue to wreak havoc in the universe and, if left unchecked, they will only grow in numbers.
We need to hunt down the Xenon, no matter how far away from Earth they are holed up. We will not be safe until they no longer have any corner of the universe to call their own.
Our military is fighting them, no matter how far they have to travel to meet the Xenon in combat. Unfortunately, though, waging war so far from your stations represents a logistical challenge.

It is imperative that these fleets are supported out there. We cannot let them venture out into the unknown without adequate protection and supplies. We ask anyone who can, to make the journey and help our troops.
Since we cannot afford to divert our Sol-based fleets to support the war effort on the far end of the universe, we have to rely on recruiting a third party.
The Protectorate must carry the shining beacon of humanity into the deepest, darkest corners of the Gate network. Only then can we truly protect humanity.

When we were reconnected with the network, it soon became apparent that we had to take the fight to the Xenon systems, and that we had to disregard the Community of Planets' sovereignty to do so efficiently.
Since we cannot rely on any other organisations, it is challenging to supply and maintain a fleet that far out from home.
It is for this reason that we approach powerful allies such as yourself for help. We would pay well if you could help establish our first line of defence out there.

The Xenon are still overrunning systems and growing in strength. The fact that these systems are far outside our usual reach cannot matter. These machines will eventually find their way here, and they will leave a swathe of destruction in their path.

It is the nature of self-replicating machines that they will grow exponentially in both strength and number. It would be tempting to ignore those Xenon strongholds far away from Sol, but we cannot afford to ease off and rely on the Community of Planets to handle the threat appropriately.
Our fleets are currently tied up in border skirmishes with Xenon strays and pirate elements.
It is a challenge to establish a meaningful presence halfway across the universe, and should you help us in these endeavours, you would be handsomely rewarded for doing so.
Should you elect to aid us with this military operation in far-off space, the Protectorate would be eternally grateful.
The Terran Protectorate aims to carry the light of human ascendancy into the farmost reaches of space. To seek the Xenon menace and exterminate it is our most founding principle.
We have decisively beaten back the Xenon forces from our borders. As a result, we now have the resources to focus on more remote systems that have been overrun by the Xenon.
We are looking to establish a presence and to push out into hostile Xenon space. If we do not take this fight to them, we are dealing with the symptoms, but we are not treating the disease.
Due to the challenges of coordinating an operation this remote, we are looking for suitable partners to help us in our efforts.
We have compiled a list of tasks for you, should you wish to help the Protectorate cut through the remote Xenon haunts.
Our reports indicate that the Xenon are amassing in large numbers in a distant system. It is only a matter of time before they make their way to Sol.

When the Gates reconnected, our leaders proclaimed that the Protectorate was going to become the absolute authority on protecting and policing the Gate network. We intend to fulfil our pledge. Our next target is going to be a distant Xenon system, far from Earth.

These Xenon fleets may be far away, but they are not outside the Protectorate's grasp. It is our intention to whittle down their numbers long before they find their way to the Sol system and become a threat to the Terran people.
While the Protectorate does not need help, it is a good opportunity for you to prove your mettle by assisting our fleet in this offensive operation.
Since this operation will take place in a remote location, without the ability to quickly respond and send backup, we offer experienced Pilots such as yourself the opportunity to aid us.
We are currently preparing an offensive into faraway Xenon territory. Too long has the Community of Planets turned a blind eye to the forces of destruction growing in its midst.
The Xenon have been growing stronger in far-off systems, undisturbed by the other inhabitants of the Jump Gate network.
If we want the Xenon menace dealt with, we have to be proactive and do it ourselves. Unfortunately, there is no other way.

If you are an experienced Pilot, we invite you to join this operation. Disrupting the enemy on their home turf is our primary objective. Whittle down the Xenon numbers, and show the other factions how it is done.

It takes a tremendous amount of effort and coordination to supply a Terran fleet out there. We have to ensure that our valiant troops are well equipped. Help us to supply them with provisions so that they can keep the universe safe.

A well-stocked armoury is the key to beating back these soulless machines. Supplies also help to assemble and maintain our vast fleets. The Protectorate hopes that you can help transport resources to the areas in which they are needed.

Maintaining a secure perimeter takes a lot of effort. Laser Towers are often the very first things that get damaged or destroyed during a Xenon invasion, yet they are critical in slowing down the enemy and holding them off. Please see to it that our perimeter is well defended.

Since the Xenon are machines at their core, they will always exhibit a certain amount of predictable behaviour. Our military can capitalise on that fact by laying minefields to deny them easy access to strategic positions. We could really use a hand in deploying these mines.

We have had notable success in cutting down enemy attacks through strategically placed minefields. If they do not destroy a fleet outright, they will usually slow them down enough for us to initiate a counterattack. As such, it is important to continuously expand our network of minefields.

The Xenon have repeatedly attempted to access resource fields located within our jurisdiction; resource fields which we are relying on to keep our economy running, and our fleets stocked. We need to shore up our defences and ensure they cannot access these fields. Deploying Laser Towers should be an efficient deterrence.

Far too often have Xenon attacks caught us off-guard. While none of their attacks so far have been able to penetrate all of our defences and find their way to Earth, we cannot risk them taking us by surprise. Help us to improve the quality of our intel by enhancing our satellite system.

When our fleets invade Xenon space, we want to make sure that they are secured along their flanks. One straightforward way of offering protection is to install Laser Towers in the Xenon system. You, too, can help the Terran Protectorate to prepare for our next offensive by deploying these front-line Laser Towers.

Our combat analysts have reviewed multiple data sources, and concluded that the presence of Laser Towers in combat areas has a positive effect on the outcome of the battle. Based on this, the Protectorate has developed an initiative which aims at deploying Laser Towers in any potential theatre of war.

Creating minefields in Xenon territory may not be the one thing that will end this war, but deploying them still reliably slows down Xenon supply ships, and disrupts their routines. Attrition is a considerable factor in any war, and therefore tasks like these, even if they seem menial, are vitally important.

The Community of Planets has shown themselves to be very reluctant to deploy minefields in order to protect themselves from Xenon attacks. The Protectorate does not hesitate to employ mines in order to inflict damage on Xenon fleets. Any Xenon ship taken out by mines is a ship we do not have to engage in combat.

Ideally, the Terran Protectorate would be aware of the enemy's movements before they even finish mobilising their fleets. In order to achieve that, though, we need Satellites in their territory. Deploying Satellites this close to the enemy can be dangerous, so stay watchful.

While the Protectorate's attention is always focused on the Terran border, along with any systems that have been overrun by the Xenon, it is important not to lose sight of our own back yard. Having an already established satellite network would prove very useful in the case of the Xenon actually pushing into this system. Please make sure that we are adequately covered by the Satellites.\n$REQUIREMENTS$

Our Satellites do not last long in Xenon territory. The enemy will actively seek them out, and destroy them. Despite their fragility, the Satellites' intel is invaluable to the war effort. Your task, therefore, is to enter enemy space and replace those that have been lost.\n$REQUIREMENTS$

Clashes with Xenon forces routinely leave ships in our fleet damaged. Our military fleets have grown to such a size that maintaining them and repairing them after battle has become a genuine challenge. That is why we have asked our allies to help out with the repairs.

We have received a distress call requesting the repair of a ship which has been stranded far outside our sphere of influence. They have been ambushed by the Xenon and, while they were able to escape, they are now sitting out in the open without adequate defences. Since the ship is some distance from our nearest available support units, we have delegated this urgent matter to you.
Help Assemble our Best and Brightest

The Sol system has always been renowned for its citizens' fighting spirit. It comes as no surprise, therefore, that the military is rarely short of motivated, skilled young cadets, itching to get in on the action. So many, in fact, that it can be hard to coordinate their transport. So, we need your help in bringing them all together.
As you may be aware, the Protectorate is fighting the Xenon on remote fronts. We have recently suffered casualties and need to bolster our numbers. Aid us in shuttling our marines to the war front.

Our primary line of defence will always be strategically placed Defence Stations. They are instrumental in keeping the enemy fleets at bay. We need to increase the number of Defence Stations in our system, and we want you to help build a station that fits our specifications.

The Protectorate is not the only power waging war against the Xenon. These machines are a blight on all races of the network. Since our military superiority affords us a unique position, we have to aggressively expand our bases into distant systems to help keep the Xenon in check. Build a station that fits our specifications.

We are looking to establish a presence in a hostile Xenon system. Before we engage the enemy, however, we need more information about that system, especially with regard to its resource fields. With a working knowledge of the area, we can quickly establish supply lines that will keep our fleet well stocked. We need you to find high-yield regions containing the following resource: $WARENAMES$

(male)$NPCName$ has repeatedly come to our attention for his pro-AGI stance. He seems to be an influential voice in the debate. We cannot afford for the faction's stance on AGI to soften, so we have to silence him before his dangerous opinions change too many minds.

(female)$NPCName$ has repeatedly come to our attention for her pro-AGI stance. She seems to be an influential voice in the debate. We cannot afford for the faction's stance on AGI to soften, so we have to silence her before her dangerous opinions change too many minds.
(ma target)\nHe was last seen flying a ship with ID: $SHIPID$. Silence him.
(fe target)\nShe was last seen flying a ship with ID: $SHIPID$. Silence her.

(Xenon Boarding Mission Description)ATF High Command has authorised technological evaluation of current Terraformer capabilities. Your directive: capture and secure designated Terraformer vessel for detailed engineering analysis at ATF facilities.
The Terran Protectorate is conducting an offensive operation into Xenon territory. We demand that our allies support this operation in any way possible.

The Protectorate is always in need of capable pilots, willing to lay down their lives for Sol. There are plenty of skilled pilots out there, but capable pilots with this kind of fervent dedication are harder to come by. So, should you know of any such pilots, we ask you to deliver them to us for cadet school.
We are looking for $NPCCOUNT$ pilot\(s\)
$DESTINATION$
$SKILLS$

We have to ensure that the military installations facing the Xenon are functional at all times. The Protectorate is looking for $NPCCOUNT$ engineer\(s\) to be brought to our station. Experience in maintaining weapons systems is mandatory.\n$DESTINATION$\n$SKILLS$

In order to aid the other factions' fight against the Xenon, the Protectorate has offered to provide specialist military training in return for foreign policy concessions. The Protectorate is especially looking for skilled pilots who can teach our friends how to fight the Xenon. Bring any applicable candidates to the allied station.
We are looking for $NPCCOUNT$ pilot\(s\) to train their forces.
$DESTINATION$
$SKILLS$

It is not always possible for us to maintain our fleets that are fighting the Xenon in systems that are far remote from Sol. For this reason that we have arranged for Terran Protectorate Engineers to be assigned on allied stations, so that they can help maintain far-off ships.\n$DESTINATION$\n$SKILLS$

The Protectorate is preparing a fleet to meet the Xenon forces head-on. The fleet has to be sizeable enough to protect Sol's borders from this, and any future, threat. You can help our war effort by bringing the following ships to $SECTOR$ :\n$FLEET$

We are planning to invade Xenon territory some considerable distance from Sol. For that, we need to gather a fleet. Aid us in assembling this fleet by bringing the following ships to $SECTOR$ :\n$FLEET$

In order to adequately fight off Xenon forces, our stations need to be well stocked. Without medical equipment, ammunition and miscellaneous other supplies, our fighters cannot inflict the damage they ought to.\n\nThe station concerned requests that their resource levels are raised above: $STORAGEPERCENT$%

Our intelligence officers have observed a Xenon fleet of impressive size that seems to be gearing up for an invasion. We need you to preemptively weaken their fleet by reducing their numbers. Our specialists have identified one type of ship type specifically, whose absence would weaken the approaching fleet.\nHunt down Xenon ships with the following specification:\n$SHIP$

We believe we may have identified a structural flaw in the Xenon ships' hulls. If we could gather more data to confirm our findings, we could adapt our combat protocols accordingly. Scan a Xenon ship to gather the crucial data.\n\nTarget reveal percentage: $PERCENT$

The Protectorate is preparing an offensive into Xenon territory. Before we commit to the assault, we need to know exactly what it is that we are facing, however. Scan a Xenon station so that we can analyse what we will be up against.\n\nTarget reveal percentage: $PERCENT$

Recently, the Xenon fleet's behaviour seems to have changed, and our specialists are puzzled as to why. We suspect that it might be connected to the nearby station's layout. If we can find any aberrations, perhaps we could use any newfound insights to our advantage.\n\nYou need to scan the following module: $MODULE$

Based on our observations, we are expecting Xenon ship production to rise in the near future. Since they are not rational beings, the best indicator of their battle plans is what wares they convey, and which stations they supply. Help us determine their plans.\n\n Find a Xenon ship containing: $WARE$

For reasons we cannot divulge due to your lack of security clearance, the Terran Secret Service is interested in tracking one specific Xenon ship. We need to know its whereabouts at all times. Please, locate that Xenon ship for us. The ship in question has ID code $IDCODE$

We want to identify and trace the Xenon supply line so that we can efficiently sabotage it by strategically placing minefields and having Terran fleets patrol the route. Anything that disrupts their fleet production will help us in the long run. You can aid us in this endeavour by scanning a ship transporting Hull Parts.

We have to know where exactly the Xenon obtain their raw resources from. If we can trace their supply routes, we can ambush their ships and slow down their growth. To achieve that, all you have to do is scan ships transporting Ore.

The Protectorate is always in need of water supplies. Since we intend to push the Xenon out of their system, and then hold it, we need to know where in that system the Xenon obtain their water supply. You can help us identify the source by scanning ships transporting Water.

In preparation for the upcoming military campaign, we need to make sure that we have easy access to Xenon systems. They are known to impede access by placing mines. You are ordered to seek out the minefield and destroy the mines which would slow us down.

We have lost too many pilots to carelessness. It is a challenge to be aware of your surroundings at all times when engaging in dogfights with the enemy. Often, solitary mines are overlooked. To reduce the risk of unnecessary casualties, we ask you to remove these mines swiftly, before we engage the Xenon again.

In order to secure the fleet's next foray, we have to send a team of ships solely dedicated to removing Laser Towers. They might not be able to destroy a fleet on their own, but in a fight with another fleet, they could make all the difference.
While our forces rally to prepare a big assault on Xenon space, we need people to fly ahead and clear the way for our valiant fighters. Will you help us destroy the Xenon Laser Towers?

It is time to focus the Protectorate's entire attention on the Xenon stations threatening all citizens of Sol. We need you to destroy this station. Doing so, although admittedly a challenge, would greatly impact this war against the machines.

We have to get a team of scientists close to a Xenon station in order to conduct an investigation. The issue is that the station's defences would tear us apart long before we even managed to set up our equipment. If you could destroy the station's turrets in preparation for our arrival, we would be able to conduct our research, and potentially identify weaknesses in the Xenon stations' design.

Station: $STATION$
Number of turrets to destroy: $TURRETS$

ATF High Command has been monitoring a single Terraformer spacecraft traversing restricted space. Standard warning protocols have been ignored. Your directive: intercept and eliminate non-compliant vessel.
Multiple Terraformer combat units detected on trajectory toward restricted Terran space. Your directive: neutralise or redirect all hostile vessels before they reach civilian habitats.

page.title: Paranid Diplomatic Mission
page.t: (Story Name Short){30220,61}(same as story name before the branch)
My Other Ship Is RIGHT BEHIND YOU
The Exponent Of Nobility(exponent means a person who supports)
Partisan Of Enlightenment(the polearm, not the type of person)
No, Gantelios Hurilis Holigis II, I expect you to die(pirate ship name, maximum length with exactly this capitalisation, translate freely into something equally long or shorter)
Periodic Blasting(same as zone name in X Rebirth)
(Dal Busta HQ Conversation Paranid Story Menu)Paranid Civil War
(tooltip to explain what the player has to to do unlock the story)Improve your reputation with the Paranid.
(tooltip)Become allied with either the Godrealm of the Paranid or the Holy Order of the Pontifex, while staying at least neutral with the other faction.

(Description)Every political manipulator-in-the-making should know that pulling the strings in the background often requires some serious preliminary cultivation of contacts. The warring Paranid realms, especially, won't allow anyone to interfere in their internal affairs unless they have "well and truly demonstrated their geometric relevance in the aggregate constellation of sanctity". It also doesn't hurt to establish a degree of trust in case something unexpectedly goes wrong further down the line.

(Logfile)You managed to raise your standing with the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex enough to dampen their mistrust. Your mentor, Dal Busta, sees this as a golden opportunity to start conducting what he calls "diplomacy".
Give Me Equity Or Give Me Death
Annuity Is An Interest Of Mine
Fighting Me Is A Bad Value Proposition
My Company Is More Solvent Than Yours
This Isn't Even My Final Form
Apogee Is Just A State Of Mind
Wayward Carrion(the type of bird, not the rotting meat)

(Description)It's come to my ears that you're on good standing with both the False Godrealm and the Heretic Order, as they affectionately call each other. Well, it turns out that by not choosing a side, you might have created the opportunity for both of us to make history! Come and find me at our Headquarters.\n\n- Dal Busta

(Logfile)After meeting with Dal Busta, your self-proclaimed diplomatic advisor, you now have a starting point for your mission to investigate the diplomatic situation between the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex.
What have you been up to?
What do I need to do?

(Description)Dal Busta, your self-declared best and most reliable friend, has asked you to meet his informant regarding all things Paranid, under the highway in {20003,40001}(Nopileos' Fortune). In light of previous experiences concerning the predictability of Dal Busta's associates, you might want to prepare for action, just in case.

(Logfile)You met up with Dal Busta's contact, who goes by the name of Gride. After overcoming initial communication barriers and putting your fighting prowess to the test, she finally agreed to share insider knowledge on the Paranid.
Just tell me what to do.

(Description)Promising further information on the roots of the Paranid Civil War and hinting at a way to influence the warring factions, Gride tasked you to make a minor delivery for her: you're expected to find an old stash of explosives and to collect a piece of technology from one of her contacts inside the Holy Order. Dal Busta, on the meanwhile, has other plans. In his mind, this task is the perfect excuse for you to go and investigate some of the more enigmatic aspects of Paranid culture.

(Logfile)The monument that Dal Busta had you scout contained a handful of Paranid cocoons, meticulously preserved for some mysterious purpose. In the end, Gride was overjoyed to receive the Holy Order cipher, and didn't spare a thought about the lost stash of explosives.
Here's the cipher you asked for.
That's all I need to know.

(Description)Having received your swift and simple delivery, Gride appeared to be surprisingly eager to provide you with a hint towards another piece in the puzzle of the Paranid conflict. Your new map information is pointing you straight towards {20003,350001}(Lasting Vengeance), one of the more recently annexed sectors of the Holy Order. Whatever it may be that's supposed to be hiding out in that remote corner of the network, closely examining the indicated area will certainly prove to be vital in its discovery.

(Logfile)Gride's latest clue led you not to a piece of information, but to a Paranid by the name of Kromancketslat, who appears to be a former diplomat of some sort. During a talk behind closed doors, Dal Busta convinced him to resume his efforts to bring the Paranid Civil War to a close.

(Description)Kromancketslat, exiled diplomat and staunch advocate for Paranid unity, has grandiosely announced the continuation of his efforts to mediate between the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid. You are deemed worthy to follow respectfully, observe the negotiations from a distance, and prevent any potential interference.

(Logfile)Following a brief distraction by a spying Argon ship, the negotiations with the local Holy Order leadership were interrupted by fanatic opposition. You were joined in your hasty defence by a unit of Holy Order elite, led by Rikmanckassor, who claims to have been sent by the True Pontifex himself.
(Title, refers to {10351,30220611})A Matter of the Utmost Gravity

(Description 1)Somewhat expectedly, the negotiations with the Holy Order sector leadership failed in a spectacular fashion. However, in facing this opposition head-on, you and Kromancketslat have gained another ally: Priest Guardian Rikmanckassor, a warrior of great renown, and confidant to the True Pontifex himself. Kromancketslat has formally asked both of you to accompany him during the next, most crucial stage of the negotiations. A representative of the Godrealm impatiently awaits your arrival.

(Description 2)Again, Kromancketslat has tasked you with observing the negotiations from a distance and intervening on his behalf, should they proceed poorly. You are to make a report to his lieutenant, who is likewise waiting nearby, just out of sight. Meanwhile, Dal Busta is eager to put his long-considered plan into action, if only you could sneak away for a moment during the commotion.

(Description 3)The lieutenant turned out to be none other than Gride, who only referred to Kromancketslat as her 'Duke'. In an attempt to recruit you for her assault on Paranid unity, she openly laid out her plan: enter the monument in your spacesuit, place bombs at weak points, then return quickly so she can trigger the explosion. Dal Busta likewise recognises this singular opportunity to permanently sabotage the negotiations, but he urges you to first unlock the strange cocoon chamber you managed to spot during your previous visit.

(Description 4)Under the guidance of your mentors, you saved, or rather abducted, a number of cocooned Paranid high priest candidates from the monument vault. According to Dal Busta, you now have a decision to make: If you wish to follow Gride's plan to sabotage the negotiations and exacerbate the Paranid Civil War, you may further explore the monument to expose its energy cores and rig them with explosives. Alternatively, you have the option to leave immediately, and in return face Gride's wrath. This could open up the possibility of a future peace deal and allow Dal Busta to keep working on his plan to install a Third Pontifex.
(Description 5)The choice is made and the battle lines are drawn. Protect your key to victory and defeat your enemies to seize this opportunity for yourself!

(Logfile main)Your infiltration mission during the Paranid peace negotiations was an outstanding success. With the assistance of Dal Busta and Boso Ta, you managed to extract a number of cocoons which will prove to be vital for influencing Paranid diplomacy for your benefit.

(Logfile appendix unification)However, despite your best efforts to keep a low profile, Gride purposefully alerted the attending Paranid fleets. When the Godrealm ambassador turned on Kromancketslat, whom he had suspected to be fraudulent from the very beginning, Gride presented herself as a target to direct retaliation towards her Buccaneers instead.

(Logfile appendix escalation)The monument, a symbol of Paranid tradition, was rent asunder. In the ensuing action and with the help of Gride and the Duke's Buccaneers, you exterminated the diplomatic delegations and put a definitive end to the peace negotiations.
Hint: The locks you need to disable will glow green.
Hint: The locks you need to repair will glow red.

(Mail for unification change 1; written by Dal Busta, a male friend; "Kromancketslat" is a "male" paranid diplomat)Kromancketslat's mediators are worth every single Credit you spent on them! The Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex have agreed to a ceasefire. They still don't like each other, but at least the fighting has stopped for now.\n\n-Dal

(Mail for unification change 2; written by Dal Busta, a male friend)Hey there, great architect! And what a wonderful station you've built for the new Paranid government. So far, it seems like this new Realm of the Trinity has only been able to take over a single sector, but the effects of that "holy conciliation" can be felt all across Paranid space. The Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex have finally opened proper diplomatic channels and are freely allowing trade between their subjects.\n\n-Dal

(Mail for unification change 3; written by Dal Busta, a male friend)And there we have it, a united Paranid people under a trinity of pontifices. That's quite the superpower you've helped create, though it has ultimately led to peace, both within and without. As predicted, the former subjects of the Holy Order of the Pontifex have calmed down a little, and the war with the Argon Federation has subsided. Nice job, peacemaker!\n\n-Dal

(Mail for escalation change 1; written by Dal Busta, a male friend; "Gride" is a female pirate)Seems like Gride's plan has finally come to fruition! Under the new, or actually old, leadership of their Pirate Duke, the Buccaneers are starting to disrupt the economies of the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex. Let's see if we can turn a profit from that, shall we?\n\n-Dal

(Mail for escalation change 2; written by Dal Busta, a male friend)Beautiful, just beautiful! Once the Duke has consolidated his power within the system, his Buccaneers will be able to set up a proper defence and prepare their war economy for things to come. I can't wait to see what chaos they'll cause after the next step in our operation!\n\n-Dal

(Mail for escalation change 3; written by Dal Busta, a male friend)That went even better than expected! Not only have you triggered an all-out, no-quarter-given war between the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex, but there seems to have been a change of identity involving the Duke's Buccaneers. They're now calling themselves the Duke's Tempest and have vowed to wipe both the Godrealm and the Holy Order off the face of the Gate network. I bow to you, herald of war!\n\n-Dal

(Description)With the Paranid diplomatic delegations saved from Gride's attack, you've earned a moment's rest for yourself. Dal Busta suggests that both of you meet at your headquarters and discuss the path ahead.

(Description update)Dal Busta has put together a plan to facilitate the Paranid peace negotiations. The first step will be to provide Kromancketslat and his fledgling faction of mediators with a sizeable escort fleet.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info)Stopping the warring Paranid factions from invading each other's territory will relieve the Holy Order of the Pontifex on that front and allow them to focus their attention elsewhere. Meanwhile, the Godrealm of the Paranid will have less use for military equipment.

(Description update 2)Kromancketslat is eager to begin his diplomatic effort in earnest. The escort fleet is awaiting orders, and would certainly be able to defend against the occasional fanatic attack, but Dal Busta still recommends the removal of known threats beforehand. One such hazard is the infamous Xatenmanckett, a hardliner who would likely do everything in his power to sabotage the negotiations. You are tasked to intercept him on his route between the Godrealm headquarters and his own fleet.

(Description update 3)After your successful disposal of the troublemaker, Dal Busta has asked you to keep to the shadows for a while and let Kromancketslat work his magic on the Paranid diplomats. If everything goes well, there should be a significant decline in hostilities between the Paranid factions very soon.
(Logfile)The Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid have made a ceasefire agreement.
(Briefing header)Dal Busta's diplomatic and economic predictions:
(Conversation option to transfer the fleet)Accept fleet transfer
(Conversation option to not transfer the fleet)Reject fleet transfer
(talking to male friend)What exactly am I signing up for?
(talking to male friend)Let's wait until later.
(talking to male friend)As ready as I'll ever be.

(Description)Kromancketslat, head diplomat and spokesperson of the Paranid mediators, demands a meeting at your headquarters to discuss the next steps after the recently successful ceasefire negotiations.

(Description update)Dal Busta and Kromancketslat have determined that to progress beyond the stage of ceasefire the Paranid will need a new symbol of unity: A grand palace for their leadership, constructed in a central location.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info)True peace between the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid will facilitate trade between their territories and likely improve both of their economies. Given enough time, the stewards of the palace will attempt to create a fledgling economy of their own and create further trade opportunities.
(Hint in briefing)At least one of these modules requires a special blueprint.

(Description update 2)The palace foundation is complete, and an attack of saboteurs is imminent. Dal Busta urges you to muster your forces at the construction site immediately and prepare for the worst.
(Description update 3)The defence was successful. Dal Busta suggests that you enjoy a moment of peace while the Sacrosanct Conclave is being ceremoniously consecrated.
(Logfile)The Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid are now truly at peace.
(Conversation option to ask a male NPC for a suggestion)What did you have in mind?

(Description)Now that peace between the Paranid factions has finally been achieved, Boso Ta and Dal Busta are eager to commence with the final stage of the plan. Return to your headquarters to learn the details.

(Description update)Dal Busta and Boso Ta have revealed the final stage of their plan to facilitate Paranid unification. Firstly, the stewards of the Sacrosanct Conclave(same as {20103,2201}) demand a vast amount of construction wares and... related items to embellish its interior and turn it into a palace worthy of a Pontifex. Secondly, Boso Ta will require scientific supplies and a substantial amount of funding to continue with his research into the stolen Paranid cocoons and help Kromancketslat find the perfect candidate for Third Pontifex.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info)Unifying the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid under a Trinity of Pontifices will bring stability to the Paranid realm, strengthening it against potential rivals.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info 2)The dissolution of the geometric paradox will serve to placate the former Holy Order of the Pontifex, ending the war with the Argon and likely leading to an overall reduced demand for military equipment.
(conversation option to borrow a book)I've made a reservation.
(conversation option to not borrow a book)Never mind.
(conversation option to get get extra info)Hit me.
(conversation option to skip extra info)Absolutely not.
(conversation option to ask whether the NPC is worried about something)Anything on your mind?
(conversation option to ask about the next stage of the conspiracy)How do we proceed?
(conversation option to ask about extra objectives)What else needs to be done?
(Conversation option to ask a male NPC why a piece of info is important)What about it?
(objective.observe)The Holy Mending(Unification of the Paranid factions)
(Inventory delivery progress bar text for scientific supplies)Supplies delivered
(Title for resource delivery sub-mission)Supreme Interior Design
(Description for resource delivery sub-mission)The palace's stewards have requested a vast amount of resources to complete their preparations for the imminent moving-in of the Paranid leadership.
(Description for resource delivery sub-mission for female player){30220,8231}

(Description for inventory delivery sub-mission)Boso Ta has requested a number of extremely important scientific devices and a handsome sum of credits for his research into Paranid cocoons and indoctrination.
(Description for inventory delivery sub-mission for female player){30220,8234}

(Description update 2)The palace interior has now been sufficiently prepared and Boso Ta reports the success of his cocoon experiment. Kromancketslat has taken the newly hatched Paranid into his custody and asks one last favour of you: To convince the Paranid high priests to dissolve the schism by appointing a Third Pontifex, you have to fetch an especially holy scripture from the archives. The ambitious diplomatic leader has so far proven to be trustworthy, but Dal Busta is sceptical about this particular approach. Nevertheless, a librarian of the Alliance of the Word should be easy enough to find.
(Logfile)The Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid have unified under the Realm of the Trinity.

(Explanation to be appended to mission briefing)It is recommended that you set up a warehouse station with appropriate buy orders, to automatically gather the required wares. The final delivery may then be completed manually, in large batches.

(Description)With the Paranid peace negotiations successfully sabotaged, you've earned a moment's rest for yourself. Dal Busta suggests that both of you meet at your headquarters and discuss the path ahead.

(Description update)Despite your recent success, Dal Busta has come to the conclusion that one failed instance of negotiations will not suffice to permanently lock the Paranid in a state of disarray. To stop all such attempts dead in their tracks, now and forever, the Duke's Buccaneers will require a sizeable insurgence fleet.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info)An increase in activity of the Duke's Buccaneers in the Paranid territories will force the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid to partially divert their attention away from other centres of conflict, giving their rivals an opportunity to make headway.
(Diplomatic and economic effect info 2)This new source of piracy has the potential to create occasional outages in the Paranid trade network, begging to be remedied by opportunistic entrepreneurs.

(Description update 2)Kromancketslat has ordered his insurgence fleet to move out and convince a number of "unaffiliated individuals" to join the cause of the Duke's Buccaneers. Dal Busta suggests that you fully endorse this endeavour.

(Description update 3)With your help, Kromancketslat managed to defeat the scattered pirate fleets and partially convert them to his cause. Dal Busta has asked you to stick to the shadows while the remaining forces of the Duke's Buccaneers begin their operations in Paranid territory.
(Logfile)The Duke's Buccaneers have begun plundering the territories of the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid.
(objective.defeat, Paranid fleet name)Disciples of the Sleeping Pontifex
(objective.defeat, Scale Plate fleet name)Guardians of Solvency
(Description)Your indulgence in this new age of piracy was rudely interrupted by Boso Ta, who implied a most dire situation was unfolding at your headquarters.

(Description update)Gride Orrian, Lieutenant of the Duke's Buccaneers and advisor to the Pirate Duke himself, approached you to request an architectural feat of epic proportions. To continue expanding its operations and to replenish their corsair forces more quickly, the pirate faction will require a heavily defended ship-building facility close to Paranid space.

(Diplomatic and economic effect info)A foothold close to Paranid space will allow the Duke's Buccaneers to more effectively disrupt the economies of the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex, potentially weakening their position even further and creating additional opportunities for foreign investors.
(Diplomatic and economic effect info 2)To supply their new production facilities, the Duke's Buccaneers will likewise have to rely on external shipments.

(Description update 2)Construction of the Pirate Duke's new headquarters is complete, and Gride has asked one more favour of you: To ensure peak efficiency, you need to deliver the most skilled station manager you can find.
(Logfile)The Duke's Buccaneers now have a foothold close to Paranid space and are attempting to establish an economy of their own.
(Conversation option, male NPC, ask about a historical figure)Who was the Pirate Duke?
(Conversation option, female NPC who's somewhere she shouldn't be)What are you doing here?

(Description)Now that the Duke's Buccaneers have established themselves as a force to be reckoned with, Boso Ta and Dal Busta are eager to commence with the final stage of the plan. Return to your headquarters to learn the details.

(Description update)Dal Busta and Boso Ta have revealed the final stage of their plan to ensure the escalation of the Paranid Civil War. Firstly, Duke's Haven (same as {20103,1401}) requires a vast amount of ship-building material to construct a flagship worthy of the Pirate Duke. Secondly, Boso Ta will require scientific supplies and a substantial amount of funding to continue with his research into the stolen Paranid cocoons and help Kromancketslat indoctrinate them for his shadowy purposes.
(Diplomatic and economic effect info)Spreading dissent through indoctrinated officials will escalate the war between the Holy Order of the Pontifex and the Godrealm of the Paranid.
(Diplomatic and economic effect info 2)This will potentially lead to attacks on civilian assets and further weaken both factions' economic and military positions.
(Diplomatic and economic effect info 3)Combined with a further increase in the Duke's Buccaneers' military spending, this will add to the overall market demand in Paranid territory.
(Title for resource delivery sub-mission)A Fearsome Flagship

(Description for resource delivery sub-mission, Duke's Haven refers to {20103,1401})The ship builders of Duke's Haven have requested a vast amount of ship-building material to construct a flagship worthy of the Pirate Duke.
(Description for resource delivery sub-mission for female player){30220,9211}
(Title for inventory delivery sub-mission)An Ethical Challenge

(Description for inventory delivery sub-mission)Boso Ta has requested a number of extremely important scientific devices and a handsome sum of credits for his research into Paranid cocoons and indoctrination.
(Description for inventory delivery sub-mission for female player){30220,9214}

(Description update 2)The construction of the Buccaneers' imposing flagship is complete, and Boso Ta reports the success of his cocoon experiment. While the Pirate Duke is occupied with teaching his new followers, freshly appointed grand admiral Gride Orrian eagerly awaits your arrival at the staging point. Once you're ready, you may give the signal for the Buccaneers' assault.

(Logfile)The Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex are locked in an all-out war and the Duke's Tempest \(formerly the Duke's Buccaneers\) have entered open conflict with both factions.
(Conversation option to give the signal for the assault)It is time.
(Conversation option to wait with the assault)Not yet.
(Conversation option to remark that a male NPC might be worried about something)Something's bothering you.
(objective.deliver, Duke's Haven refers to {20103,1401})Ship-building Material to Duke's Haven
(custom objective, leaning back and enjoying something)Savour
(Duke's Haven refers to {20103,1401}, Await: )Reconstruction of Duke's Haven
(Visions of the future at the decision point of the Paranid Story)
(Sabotage generic info)Sabotaging the negotiations will exacerbate the war between the Godrealm of the Paranid and the Holy Order of the Pontifex.
(Sabotage diplomatic info)The military position of both factions will be weakened, potentially allowing their enemies to advance.
(Sabotage economic info)An increase in military losses and collateral damage will create economic opportunities for ambitious entrepreneurs willing to fill the gaps.
(Negotiations generic info)Letting the negotiations continue will leave open the possibility of a future ceasefire, or even a peace treaty.

(Negotiations diplomatic info)Reduced tensions between the two factions will allow them to focus their military attention elsewhere at first, and potentially lead to a decrease in hostilities against other factions as well.
(Negotiations economic info)Interconnection of the Paranid trade networks will increase economic stability, while the demand for military equipment will likely decrease over time.

(Description, written by Dal Busta, a male friend)It appears that all across the Gate network, producers of military equipment are banding together in protest at the peaceful resolution of the Paranid Civil War. This is a fascinating development indeed, if a somewhat unsurprising one. Let's talk it over.
(Logfile)You've selected a suitable next target for Paranid expansionism.
(talking to male friend)You wanted to talk?
(talking to male friend)Why not all of them?
(talking to male friend)Let me think about it first.
(talking to male friend)Yes, this is my final choice.
(talking to male friend)Let's talk about this later.
(talking to male friend)Let's talk about war.

Yu t'Knk(of Family Zyarth, formerly Gau)
Ghus t'Gllt(Historical Patriarch who introduced the 'Curb')

Tau t'Fnt(cover name for Fau t'Nnt)

(Player Choice - HQ Split Story Menu)Split Sightings
(Player Choice - HQ Split Story Menu)The Split Connection
(Player Choice - HQ Split Story Menu)Split Separatism

(Mission Text)Your trusted friend Dal Busta heard rumors of Jump Gate reactivations and Split ship sightings. While he asks the Alliance of the Word about the Split, your task is to investigate those rumours and try to find the reactivated Gates.
(Logbook Text)Following rumours of gate activities you found a reactivated Jump Gate leading to Split space!
(Player Choice)Will do.(Agreement on "You meanwhile investigate [..] and [..] find those gates.")
(Mission Text)Dal Busta requested a meeting to share his insights on the Split.
(Player Choice)You looked into Split politics?(addressing male character Dal)
(Player Choice)What did you learn about the factions?(addressing male character Dal)
(Player Choice)What's your plan?(addressing male character Dal)
(Player Choice)Ferry random Split to make friends?

(Mission Text)In order to influence Split politics and society, you need to be well connected within the realm. With the patriarchal court(translate 'patriarchal court' as royal court, not judicial) being too aloof and isolated to interfere, you aim to learn more about the Free Families.

(Mission Text)Dal found a Split who regularly travels to and from Split space, often under different names. He ought to be well connected and a helpful associate to have. Make contact and find out what he knows, and where his allegiances lie.

(Logbook Text)You questioned and transported a suspicious Split who was, just as Dal suspected, well connected with important Split. He, however, also used this opportunity to question you before reporting his verdict back to the Zyarth police.
(Logbook Appendix)As you showed interest in Split culture, he referred you to another Split you can discuss Split matters with.(Other Split female)
(Logbook Appendix)As you showed interest in Split culture, he referred you to another Split who might talk some sense into you.(Other Split female)
(Player Choice)Greetings! I will be your transport.(addressing male Split)
(Player Choice)I'd like to hear more about them.
(Player Choice)What kind of Patriarch is Zyarth?
(Player Choice)Are the Families opposed to Patriarchy rule?
(Tooltip for an unselectable Player Choice)Acquire enough information.

(Mission Text)Locating the contact that Fau t'Nnt gave you might be more troublesome than expected: news of the reactivated Jump Gates and the re-established contact with the Argon Federation have spread throughout the enslaved Argon population in Split territory. A group of these slaves have used this opportunity to finally make an escape, and took your Split contact hostage in the process. Track the hijacked ship down, and negotiate the release of this hostage.(Female contact/hostage)

(Logbook Text)You tracked down a group of escaped Argon slaves and rescued their Split hostage. As a token of gratitude you have been invited to attend the funeral of a Split war hero.(female hostage, male hero)
(Mission Text)As a token of gratitude for rescuing a Split life, Lae t'Shn, Curb of Family Tkr(female Lae t'Shn, Curb), invited you to attend the funeral of a Split war hero.(male war hero)

(Mission Append)The deceased is Patriarch Gau t'Pg, who fought the Zyarth invasion in a joint coalition with other Free Families' Patriarchs and lost his life at the Fires.(Sector Fires of Defeat/Victory)

(Mission Append var1)The deceased is your former Patriarch Gau t'Pg, who fought the Zyarth invasion in a joint coalition with other Free Families' Patriarchs and lost his life at the Fires.(Sector Fires of Defeat/Victory)
(Logbook Text)You attended the funeral of Gau t'Pg, a former Patriarch of the Free Families.
(Logbook Text)You attended the funeral of Gau t'Pg, your former Patriarch.
(Tooltip for an unselectable Player Choice)Insufficient Inventory
(Player Choice)Agreed.(Addressing male, Accepting Request to help with an investigation.)
(Objective - Wait:)Funeral Ceremony is about to begin

(Mission Text)Impressed by your success in tracking and negotiating the release of a Split hostage, Fau t'Nnt offers you to help another Split of the Free Families.(Split hostage is female, Fau t'Nnt is male, other Split/Patriarch Noa t'Hlp is male)

(Mission Text2)Patriarch Noa t'Hlp is on trial for withholding war reparations from the Zyarth Patriarchy. The Free Patriarch reported his financial records as stolen, and while he claims to not be wealthy enough for such demands, the financial records of his former business partners tell another story. They report large purchases of slaves from Patriarch Noa t'Hlp, which would warrant him a place among the financially well-situated Split.

(Mission Text 3)The stolen financial records are a dead end. However, Dal suspects that the Trading Station ought to also have recorded those transactions. With Boso's help, you should be able to access this data and potentially exonerate the Patriarch. And who wouldn't want to have a Split Patriarch in their debt?

(Logbook Text)Defiance in reparation payments is not a crime overlooked by the overzealous Zyarth Patriarchy. They brought Patriarch Noa t'Hlp to justice before you were able to review the trading records and confirm that he had been set up. Now, however, you know the culprit.
(Objective Scan)Signal Leak next to the Satellite
(Mission Title)Tax Evasion 101 - How to hide money from Zyarth

(Mission Text)Within the data you and Boso extracted from the Trading Station(Trading Station as in {20102,1051}), Dal found the transaction which allegedly benefited Patriarch Noa t'Hlp and forced a reaction from the Zyarth Patriarchy. From this you learned that the Slave Traders conspired against Patriarch Noa t'Hlp. Contrary to their claims, he did not receive any funds. However, they were not able to fake this transaction without processing one. Their true beneficiary, the Patriarchal Funeral Service, does not list any major assets nor wealth which would draw the attention of Zyarth taxation.
Thus, Dal suspects, the wealth has to be hidden behind their Funeral Accelerator('Funeral Accelerator' as in {20103,1301}). Which is exactly where he wants you to go.
(Player Choice)Perfect.(Acknowledge getting inventory from male for specific task)
(Mission Text)With technical help from Boso and a carefully planned distraction by Dal, you intend to to take advantage of the ongoing funeral in order to break into the coffin ship.

(Mission Text)With the technical help from Boso and a carefully planned distraction by Dal, you were able to take advantage of the funeral and broke into the coffin ship. Now, however, you have been caught. Seem valuable to avoid the worst.

(Logbook Text)You found the Funeral Service's assets, just as Dal suspected, right behind their Funeral Accelerator('Funeral Accelerator' as in {20103,1301}). Shortly after your little break-in though you got caught. Able to convince your captors of your own ongoing feud with the Zyarth Police, you were allowed to leave the sector and prove your worth for, and dedication to the separatist cause.
You decided to warn the Zyarth Patriarchy about this separatist movement.
(Player Choice)I was looking into a court case...
(Player Choice)It was a request by Fau t'Nnt!
(Player Choice)I wanted more lenience from their police!
(Player Choice)No ties, just trying to get by!
(Player Choice)I traced funds to the Funeral Service.
(Player Choice)At the Trading Station, but I deleted them!
(Player Choice)Why did you frame the Patriarch?
(Player Choice)I want to join your cause.

(Player Choice)How do I prove my dedication?
(Tooltip for an unselectable Player Choice)Your worth is already proven.
(Tooltip for an unselectable Player Choice)Your dedication is already proven.
(Tooltip for an unselectable Player Choice)You have already joined their cause.
(Mission Title)Report to Slave Trader 2(ship named as in {30221,205})

(Mission Text)Dal suggests you work your way up within the rebellion to get a sense of its scope. They asked you to report for duty on one of their Slave Traders.(Slave Trader named as in {20204,6601}) However, he also can set up a meeting with the Zyarth Police to inform them of the separatist movement.

(Mission Text)After you informed Fau t'Nnt, and thus the Zyarth Police, of the brewing separatist rebellion, they hired you to continue your investigations. You are tasked to work for them undercover and report your new findings. The rebels, meanwhile, asked you to report for duty on one of their Slave Traders.(Slave Trader named as in {20204,6601})
(objective.wait)Arrival at Hall of Judgement(Hall of Judgement as in {20103,2001})
Ghus' vision?(Ghus as in {30221,115}, genitive case)
(Player Choice)When can I meet your Patriarch?

(Logbook Text)You assisted in a major attack on the Hall of Judgement(Hall of Judgement as in {20103,2001}), which included a break-in on the highly restricted station, aiding a prison breakout, and aiding a slave revolt with their terrorist bombings. As a result, the station has been taken over by now-free Argon slaves. Now that you're a tried and tested field operator, the Curb should trust you enough to reveal the conspiring Patriarchs of this separatist movement.

Escaping the scene, Fau t'Nnt of the counter-attacking Zyarth Police force gave you the chance to disengage in order to honour your cooperation. You disengaged in time, which is noted in your favour with the Zyarth Police, but might reflect poorly on you with the separatists.

Escaping the scene, Fau t'Nnt of the counter-attacking Zyarth Police force gave you the chance to disengage in order to honour your cooperation. You did not disengage in time, which is noted in your favour with the separatist movement, but might reflect poorly on you with the Zyarth Police.
Escaping the scene instead of protecting the Slave Trader('Slave Trader' ship named as in {30221,205}), you left the battlefield. This might reflect poorly on you with the separatists.
(Reward)Certificate of Participation in Basic Military Black Ops
(Custom Objective)Await the Slave Trader's arrival at the Hall of Judgement(Slave Trader as in {20204,6601}, Hall of Judgement as in {20103,2001})

(Mission Text)Use your newly earned standing as a trusted field operator to gather information on the separatist movement in order to make a decision on which side you want to support.

(Logbook Entry)You discussed the possible outcome and decided to aid the separatist movement of the Curbs.
As you have learned all about the separatist movement, meet Dal in order to decide which side you want to support.

Having delivered the requested fleet, you now sabotage their declaration to put a serious dent in the number of Split who will decide to join them.
You have successfully sabotaged the Court of Curbs' declaration and put a serious dent in the number of Split who decided to join them.

Having delivered the requested fleet, you now attend their declaration.(public declaration)
You have successfully aided the Court of Curbs in establishing them as a regional power.

(Briefing)The Curbs are rallying support to fight the Zyarth Patriarchy. While they themselves are giving speeches to win over Split hearts and minds, the devoted followers are being asked to contribute financially. The efforts will be aimed at ending Patriarchy policing of Free Families sectors.
(Briefing)After once again proving your worth, you are being asked to prove your dedication and attack the Patriarchy directly.
(Logbook)You helped the Court of Curbs(as in {20203,1801}) to end Patriarchy policing of Free Families sectors.

(Briefing)The Patriarchy Secret Police is trying to get funds for anti-terrorism initiatives. Aiding them will help establish the Patriarchy deep within the rogue sectors to prevent similar incidents.
(Briefing)Thankful for your contribution, the Patriarchy Secret Police gave you intel on a rebel base. Act on it to support their endeavours.
(Logbook)You helped the Zyarth Patriarchy to act firmly on matters of law and order.
(Briefing)The Court of Curbs(same as {20203,1801}) are planning a major attack on Zyarth home sectors.
(Briefing)They are asking for a huge delivery for this purpose.
(Logbook)You aided in an attack on Zyarth home sectors. The Zyarth Patriarchy is no more.
(effect info CUB1)Giving the Curb Rebellion a fighting chance, both the Curbs and the Patriarchy will be heavily investing in securing the Free Families' space.
(effect info CUB1)The Free Families(Free Families same as {20203,1601}) have the burden of supplying both the Court of Curbs(Court of Curbs same as {20203,1801}) and themselves.
(effect info CUB1)This conflict in the Free Families' space could create opportunities for foreign investors.
(effect info CUB2)Driving out the Colonial Police(Colonial Police same as {20204,10050}) will decrease the Patriarchy presence in Free Families space.
(effect info CUB2)This will calm hostilities and establish the Court of Curbs(Court of Curbs same as {20203,1801}) as a regional power.
(effect info CUB2)The Court of Curbs will maintain fleets which protect the Free Families'(Free Families same as {20203,1601}) space against foreign intruders.
(effect info CUB2)With a decrease in military conflicts, the economy could eventually stagnate.
(effect info CUB3)After a final blow to their home sectors, the Zyarth Patriarchy(same as {20203,2001}) will be driven out of Free Families space.
(effect info CUB3)Patriarch Zyarth will be forced out of power and the Patriarchy will be left in shambles('in shambles' figurative, not much of the Patriarchy will remain).
(effect info CUB3)This will end the Split civil war and allow the remaining Split factions to recover.
