You, my faithful assistant, gracious provider, and, dare I say it, artistic muse - I ask you to ride this high with me, together. As long as you are by my side, there shall be no end to my supplies, no end to inspiration, and no end to Arthur's masterpieces, each grander than the one that came before!

(Description, addressing player)This last batch of... implements was truly divine, as were the creations I fashioned in its wake! You may begin to wonder how long we can continue down this route of self-sacrifice, but worry not! Bodily decay is merely a stepping stone on the path to greatness. As my old mentor used to say: until the end, and then onwards to kingdom come!

(Description, addressing player)No, I really can't say I'm feeling it. Your delivery was right on time, and you did a wonderful job, but something... something is still missing. Look at me. I can't even bring myself to respond to your graciousness with adequate eloquence. Oh, I merely forgot to re-increase the output! Now it all comes flowing back to me, oh viscous wisdom, entrancing foil of the stars, the universe at my fingertips! Quickly, venture out to replenish my occult reservoir, or the current may begin to dry up again!

(Description, addressing player)You know what they say is the enemy of creativity? The police. Wait, what answer did you expect? As my primary supplier, you should know full well the risks of the job, or did I not clarify that in our contract? There's no contract? Why is there no... oh, of course, we wouldn't want this to become official now, would we? And there's no reason why it should, since nobody else knows the true reason for my recent surge in artistic output... See, I'm already getting worked up over nothing, all because my supplies have run dry. You really should get going and bring me another batch!

(Description, addressing player)My dearest admirer, I must have spent the entirety of this last day in a trance! When I finally awoke, I watched my mortal body pandiculate from a distance, almost as if my mind was still floating freely in the copulative void between the world of cold, dead matter, and the realm of living, pulsating, writhing imagination. And what that body had wrought under the tutelage of my exuberant mind, now, let me tell you! Actually, no, this masterpiece was commissioned strictly as a private matter. Oh well. Have you taken care of the next delivery yet?
Information technology components are dropped by lockboxes and enemy ships.
(Title)Fwd: looking for new couriers, please forward

(Description, addressing male colleague, writes a casual mail in lowercase)FROM: Keter P.
SUBJECT: looking for new couriers, please forward
TO: Boger R.

hi boger,

can I ask you a favour? in today's meeting you stated that you are done with the high prio tasks, so I hope that this is not too much

we are running short on helpers in the producer's office, and the project is about to enter a critical stage. could you put out a job offer? they would have to take care of the usual deliveries, you know the details. I sent you some extra ideas in the attached file.

PS: please make sure you don't just forward this mail to the mission offer system this time

ATTACHMENT: New Text Document\(27\)

(Description, addressing player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app, "shinano" is a Japanese river, a pun on the Amazon shop)sorry for causing all that confusion with the original job posting. for what it is worth, I am extremely happy that we now have a new, capable courier that can take care of emergency tasks for my office. speaking of which, the first batch of supplies you delivered was certainly super helpful, but we are in dire need of more! when I said that the project was critical, that was an understatement. it is literally on fire. figuratively. pardon me, I have to go order a new extinguisher from shinano =\)

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)my bosses have decided that we are going to hold a big meeting soon, and my project is going to be on the dissecting table. if we want to make that deadline, I will have to get my entire team to work in unison. the problem is, that they are scattered across the nearby sectors, and it is almost impossible to get our timetables to match. that is, unless we get a new shipment of technical implements that we can hack together last minute! you go and take care of the equipment while we come up with a solution

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)it all broke down! complete disaster! this is not your fault, though. your delivery was right on time, and the quality was perfect. we booked the virtual augmented conference space, set everything up. the team was so motivated, and then we got hit by the mother of all sync errors. luckily, I was able to convince my bosses that this project is too complex for a simple meeting, and we ended up talking for hours in front of my own workstation while I showed them our best mock-ups. I really have to find a quiet moment to get to that conference room and clean up the mess, and I will need a new delivery to replace what was lost. could you help me out once again?

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)hi! we are testing a new automated customer support system, and one of our senior employees had the idea of recording temporary voice lines to serve as placeholders until we can contract professional voice actors. while setting up our own recording studio in the hallway leading to the office, we realised that we are utterly undersupplied in terms of equipment. would you please deliver another batch? maybe we can negotiate a barter deal with one of the other departments

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)do you have time for a task? my bosses are planning an in-office barbecue to celebrate meeting our recent deadline. getting the whole team together on the same day is proving to be impossible... again. luckily, though, I have found a new piece of software that will take care of the re-scheduling. unluckily, it does not run on my outdated workstation. could you deliver another batch of tech so that my system administrator can rig something up that works? beep bop bop =\)

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)I need to talk to you about your next tasks. what do you mean, your task list is empty? my team is constantly dealing with time pressure, so surely someone has asked you for help. your only contact in the department is me? now that you mention it, that may actually be true. well then, let me have a look at our stock levels... no, we have still not got through your last delivery. oh well. it certainly would not hurt to have a surplus, just in case. take care of it, please

(Description, addressing the player, writes in lowercase like in a chat app)I need your help with a task! one of our most notorious programmers is about to visit the office, and they are known to take great pride in customising their workstation. you know where this is going. we still have a few interchangeable bits left over from your last shipment, but there is no way that this amount will satisfy. please deliver with due diligence =\)

page.title: Supervised Mining
page.t: (Objective)Protect ships until they mine materials to completion

Due to an increase in Kha'ak activity in our territory, we are in danger of running low on certain critical wares. We need someone capable of scoping out a potential new source of Ore(Ore same as {20201,2701}) and, more importantly, we need them to guarantee the security of our miners while they go about their work.
Thanks to your capable supervision, our miners have safely found their way to our docks and we were able to shore up our ore supplies. Great work!

We are in danger of running run low on Silicon,(Silicon same as {20201,3501}) and a noticeable increase in Kha'ak incursions really does not help matters. In an attempt to stave off a shutdown in production, we are turning to experienced third parties to help us in scoping and securing potential mining zones.

You successfully ensured the safe return of our miners, and we are already allocating the Silicon(Silicon same as {20201,3501}) to various different productions. We are grateful for your service. Thank you!

Whenever our miners attempt to mine and ferry Nividium(Nividium same as{20201,2401}), they are beset by an agitated swarm of Kha'ak. We cannot ask our miners to go out without assured protection. This is where you come in. Scout a space with adequate Nividium(Nividium same as{20201,2401}) deposits and ensure our miners can harvest it without fearing for their lives, and we will reward you handsomely.

Despite the Kha'ak's intense attempts to intercept the mining convoy, you were able to secure safe passage to our station. Our faction appreciates your commitment to keeping us well-supplied and safe!

page.title: Pirate Investigation
page.t: (Mission title)Dark Figures(translate freely to something that alludes to uncovering the financial dealings of a shady organisation)

page.title: Xenon Khaak Crisis
page.descr: Text for the Xenon-Kha'ak player crisis
page.t: (Mission descriptions as written by Boso Ta)
An incident involving a rather large Xenon force is currently underway.
While Xenon activity in this area is not without precedent, there are reports of them launching the attack from the sector's outskirts, catching the defence forces unawares.

This warrants further investigation, as any major shift in Xenon tactics not only has the potential to throw the universe into turmoil, but it may also lead to a wonderous discovery about the evolution of synthetic life!
This is an urgent and time sensitive situation! Please meet with me and I will inform you of our impending peril.
Yet another Xenon incursion has been detected.
We are getting reports of Xenon approaching from the outskirts of this sector.
It appears that a sector will soon be hit by a substantial Xenon force.
We must make haste if we are to limit the potential damage.
The losses will be great if we cannot intercept them.
Defences must be strengthened, but time is short.
The sector is in a dire situation as a sizable Xenon fleet has descended upon it.
Local forces in the sector are being stretched thin as a Xenon fleet bears down.
The Xenon attack appears to coincide with the appearance of Kha'ak ships, which have also targeted the sector, attacking indiscriminately.

The Kha'ak also appear to have been induced into launching their own attack on the sector, attacking indiscriminately. This seems to be the Xenon's tactic of mass destruction, even at a high risk to themselves.
We have received an interesting ping from the Fleet-Wide Sensor Analytics(see {20216,3201}) which indicates a large, oddly-shaped mass in an obscure location. It may be worthy of our attention.
We have received an interesting ping from the Fleet-Wide Sensor Analytics(see {20216,3201}) which indicates a large battle in a far-off area of space. It may be worthy of our attention.

I, along with a number of specialists in the subject of the Xenon, have been analysing the data from these attacks. The initial findings are as fascinating as they are deeply troubling. The Xenon have employed a tactic to increase Kha'ak activity in the area.

It appears that they have found a way to poke the hornet's nest and direct their anger.

While understanding their methods is of vital importance to a successful defence, I am more concerned about how this tactic was devised. I simply must know more! I implore you to continue investigating these events as they occur.

We are making progress in understanding the Xenon strategy, as well as gathering clues as to the source of this devious scheme! I have so many theories, but this is not the time for conjecture! We must have more data so that we can better predict the next event and finally put an end to this harrowing ordeal.

There has been a breakthrough! We have intercepted a number of Xenon communications with an encryption protocol not seen for decades. We are currently debating its significance, but it does seem that we are close to a consensus.\n\nI will contact you in due course with our conclusions!
Please continue defending as you have been.
I hate to ask you to put yourself in harm's way, but we simply must have first-hand observations.
I will spend some time reviewing the data from the encounter with this mysterious ship. I have an ominous feeling in my waters.
I will spend some time theorising why the Xenon and Kha'ak have had this deep-space skirmish. It is probably nothing of note, but I have an ominous feeling in my waters.
Please continue with your business, and remember that increasing the size of your fleet will increase the coverage of our new sensor network.

I am glad to announce that a new path of research has opened up to us. Due to the size and distribution of your fleets, I have surmised that we can network their sensors more closely to help probe their surroundings with higher precision.

Who knows what treasures we may find? That said, there is also a chance we may instead stumble into an undesirable situation, such as a fleet of slumbering Xenon or a Kha'ak mega-hive!

Perhaps caution is in order.

It appears that the large object has disappeared and left us with little evidence that it ever existed. I will spend some time reviewing the data from this incident. I have an ominous feeling in my waters.
We will face them and stop them.
Let them come. We will stop them.

page.title: The Twins Plot
page.t: Tasmodeos Tasmodeos Tasmodeos III(Teladi Shady Saleslizard)
(Title)Tidebreak Operator(Flight Control Coms Operator from the Tidebreak Station)
Scrapyard(Location in space where stripped ship wrecks are dumped, a ship graveyard)
Bestowed in Perpetuity(Ch2 Fan Trader Ship)
Lone Sharks(group VIG fighters, shark names, objective:defeat this group)
Deep Blue C(VIG Pirate ship name)
Great White(referring to the shark, as a ship name)
(Mission Text)Aid the Promethean Spark's smuggling of food by fending off the VIG enforcers.(Promethean Spark same as {30251,204})
(Mission Reward)A Raker's Gratitude(Raker refers to the Riptide Rakers Faction Name)
(Logbook Text)You helped a Riptide Raker smuggle food to Avarice.
(Mission Text)The Teladi trading ship "Bestowed in Perpetuity" is stuck in transit, and threatened by a phenomenon known as the "Tide". Help the Teladi escape his misfortune.
(Logbook Text)You helped the Teladi escape his misfortune!
(Objective - Custom Action)Convince $NAME$ to abandon their ship
(Objective - Custom Action)Escape the looming Tide to:('Tide' same as {30251,1})
(Mission Text)As an experienced pilot, you will trespass onto a Syndicate Scrapyard to steal one of their dumped ships for your Teladi friend. Good luck on your journey!
(Logbook Text)You trespassed onto a Syndicate Scrapyard and stole one of their dumped ships for your Teladi friend!

(Mission Text)Your humble Teladi friend most politely requests your presence for trade negotiations at a Riptide station. You will benefit from valuable lessons on how to commence negotiations, as meticulously described in definitive guides such as "Reading Argon Facial Expressions" and "Dealmakers - The Uguras Tumulis Yooses Siblings' Fortune". As a partner, you will be involved in any deals that are struck, and will make a profit from the buying and selling of wares.
(Logbook Text)You helped your humble Teladi friend to strike a most bankable deal!
(Objective - Sell: $WARE$ for 100Cr profit)$WARE$ for maximum profit

(Mission Text)Stations in Avarice rely on Protectyon, a patented ware produced and distributed by the Northriver company, to protect themselves against the reoccurring Tide phenomenon. The recycling economy of Avarice relies on a steady influx of Scrap Metal(Scrap Metal same as {20201,6601}) to sustain its income, and fluctuations in supply can lead to stations being unable to afford a shipment of Protectyon, to brace themselves against the next Tide. Such stations may be willing to accept less favourable deals; a situation which you can take advantage of!

(Mission Text)Stations in Avarice rely on Protectyon, a patented ware produced and distributed by the Northriver company, to protect themselves against the reoccurring Tide phenomenon. The recycling economy of Avarice relies on a steady influx of Scrap Metal(Scrap Metal same as {20201,6601}) to sustain its income, and fluctuations in supply can lead to stations being unable to afford a shipment of Protectyon, to brace themselves against the next Tide. Such stations may be willing to accept less favourable deals; a situation which your humble Teladi friend knows how to take advantage of!

(Logbook Text)The invisible hand of market forces failed to ensure supply, and left a Riptide station defenceless against the Tides of Avarice! To prevent this from ever happening again, you will need to find a researcher capable of unravelling the mysteries of Protectyon and supporting your planned patent infringement.
(Objective - Talk to)the evil {20203,3301}(faction name: Vigor Syndicate)
(Objective: Fly to:)Syndicate Communication Beacon(Syndicate same as {20203,3304})
Boso Ta's Corporate Research and Espionage Department(Mission Title)

Assistant!\nThe current conditions in Avarice are categorically unconscionable. It seems that the Northriver Company is not doing enough to distribute their fascinating Protectyon. This substance intrigues me greatly. Should we be able to analyse the substance, I am confident that I will be able to come up with a solution that would help alleviate the existential problems facing the people of Avarice.(Mission Text)

You have made contact with Brantlee Northriver, and managed to get your hands on a Protectyon condensate sample. With the help of your aquatic friend, you have now analysed the sample, and are expecting to be briefed by Boso at the HQ.(Logbook Text)
(Await: )Protectyon collection(Custom Action Text - collection in the sense of picking up or gathering something)
Brantlee Northriver's Competition(Mission Title, competition a play on words, referring to hosting a contest and a business competitor - if translation not possible go with contest/race meaning)

Assistant, I have completed the research! Unfortunately, I have discovered some unexpected irregularities, which we need to discuss expeditiously! Some things are best talked about in person, though. Your scaly friend should also attend this meeting, as he will undoubtedly provide a fresh perspective!(Mission Text 1)

It appears that you have somehow goaded the Northriver CEO into a race for the secret of Protectyon. Make no mistake, if you do not make the proper preparations, his ship will beat yours. What the smug fool did not factor in, however, is my scientific brilliance! I am quite sure that we will find a way to make use of the experimental teleportation technology that I have been looking into.(Mission Text 2)
The ship that we stash close to the finish line does not need any modifications on it. It is not meant to race, after all.(Mission Text 3)
Use Long Range Scanner to find suitable target(meaning a pirate ship that's easy to defeat)
Note: if you are looking to change the selected ship, install a suitable engine mod on another ship.
The satisfaction of beating Brantlee in a race(Mission Reward)
That race did not go as expected. Something went really wrong, but neither you nor your companions are quite sure what.(Logbook Text)
Install any Enhanced Engine Mod(Custom Action)
(Install mod on: )fast M-sized ship(Custom Action Text)
(Deliver:)identical ship close to the finish line
Install mod on fast M-sized ship
Wait for the start signal(for the start of a race)
Deliver an identical ship close to the finish line
Enigmatic Avarice(Mission Title, "Avarice" same as system {20005,9033})

Regrettably, the race did not pan out the way we all expected it to. Perhaps with my help you can find out how Northriver beat you and, in doing so, maybe you can also uncover the secrets of their Protectyon product. Travelling faster than you can teleport should be absolutely impossible, so without question something else must be going on. The Avarice system is very unusual, so I hypothesise that there must be something we are missing. Assistant, you have plenty of investigating to do!(Mission Text)

You still don't quite know how Brantlee pulled off his win, but you have come across something even more intriguing. Thanks to clues left behind in an abandoned observatory, you now know that Protectyon is sourced from a system hidden away from prying eyes. Now you just need to make your way into this system for some answers.(Logbook Text)
(Deploy: )a Nav Beacon at each anomaly in $SECTOR$(Custom Action Text)
(Investigate: )remnants of a derelict observatory(Custom Action Text)
Answers in a Faraway System(Mission Title)

So, it looks like we just happened upon the Northriver Company's big trade secret. Their Protectyon is sourced from a system which can only be accessed during a short period after the Tide has hit a specific anomaly, so the window of opportunity is brief. I bet that making our way into the system and snooping around will clear things up significantly.(Mission Text)

You sat down with the two Northriver twins, and heard their offer. The decision you made will impact the Avarice system one way or another, and you came out of that meeting having made enemies. Now, you just need to try and wrap things up as neatly as possible.(Logbook Text, "Avarice" same as system {20005,9033})
(Investigate: )the unusual anomaly to access a hidden system(Custom Action Text)
Align with Northriver or forge your own path(Custom Action)
Wait for the next Tide(Custom Action, Tide same as {30251,1})
Be ready when the anomaly activates(Custom Action)
Fly through the unusual anomaly(Custom Action)

You went for it! You stole the distribution module blueprints from right under the Twins' noses! With this module, and the knowledge of where you can procure more Protectyon, you can build up a rival trade empire in Avarice, and lower the prices significantly should you so choose. But of course the Northriver Company will not sit idly by. It appears they have put a price on your head, and the Syndicate is looking to collect. Though, if you handle this right, you can surely get them off your back again.(Mission Thread Text - Fan Choice)

Now that you have agreed to our terms, we need you to ensure that what you have discovered does not become common knowledge. Our idea for the Syndicate to relinquish some power over Windfall is also encountering some resistance among the Vigor Leadership; we need to demonstrate that we are serious.(Mission Thread Text - Twin Choice)
Get the Vigor Syndicate off your back(Mission Reward - Fan Choice)
Syndicate assets and the opportunity to purchase a very special ship(Mission Reward - Twin Choice)
A New Way Forward(Logbook Title - The Fan)

You have convinced the Vigor Syndicate that it is in their best interests not to pursue matters further. With them off your back, you can now use what you have learned to make a profit yourself, or to help the people of Avarice.(Logbook Text - The Fan)
Part of the Club(Logbook Title - The Twins)

Falling in line with the Company has resulted in a significant boost to your wealth, and access to exclusive circles. Sit back and enjoy the wealth and power, or talk to one of the Twins again if you want to arrange the handover of a very special kind of ship!(Logbook Text - The Twins)
A Demonstration of Power(Mission Title - The Fan)

The Syndicate will not let up until you show them that you are a real danger if you are provoked to attack. Destroying a station crucial to their operations should do the trick!(Mission Description - The Fan)
Intimidating the Vigor Syndicate(Mission Reward - The Fan)
Reaching Out to the Enemy(Mission Title - The Fan)

Show the Syndicate that the Northriver Company are not the only ones around these parts with deep pockets, and they might be persuaded to back off. Buying their indifference will probably not be cheap, though.(Mission Description - The Fan)
Making Friends in Low Places(Mission Reward - The Fan)
A Change in Management(Mission Title - The Twins)

The current Vigor Syndicate management is resisting our suggestion to abdicate as the prominent power in Windfall. That is not surprising, but we need you to show them that they really have no other choice, now that you have entered the picture. Destroy a station important to their operations, kill their leadership, and it is a safe bet that they will return to our negotiation table.(Mission Description - The Twins)

If you have cooperated with any other partners so far, and they could give away our trade secret, you need to ensure their silence. There is only ever one way that you can be sure that they won't talk. You know what to do!(Mission Description - The Twins)
A Former Friend's Perpetual Silence(Mission Reward - The Twins)
Optional: Capture an Astrid(same as {20105,9013})(Mission Title - The Fan)

While snooping around in the internal systems, I could not resist fiddling with the automated security protocols. The pilots should now find themselves being forced to abandon ship if you put them under enough pressure. Assistant, do you fancy seizing a yacht from the super-rich?
Ownership of an Astrid(same as {20105,9013})-class ship

Construction of your Astrid(Astrid same as {20101,120101}) has finished! I am sure you are anxiously waiting to take control of your newest, most prized possession! Enjoy the great pleasures this luxury yacht has to offer, safe in the knowledge that you made the right choice!(Mission Text)
(Email Title)CBNN News - Troubling Developments Put Pressure on Riptide Rakers(Riptide Rakers same as {20203,3201})

(Email Text)A shortage of Protectyon, combined with a stagnating local economy in the Avarice(Avarice same as {20005,9033}) system, has resulted in a chain of events that tragically caused the destruction of several civilian stations. The system's unique environmental conditions make it an attractive target for scrap recycling businesses, but it has also proven a grave danger to the inhabitants. Recycling is a niche, which the Riptide Rakers were all too glad to fill once they realised that they were the only ones in the position to do so efficiently and on a large scale. They appear to have overestimated their own capabilities, however, as several stations which failed to turn a profit, and were therefore not able to afford station upkeep, have recently been decommissioned permanently. Whether this development will cause a chain reaction resulting in the depopulation of the entire system, or whether the scrappers are resourceful enough to avoid going out of business, remains to be seen.\n\nYoyunis Tertasobas Zusilas IV - Economics Correspondent, CBNN News
(Email Title - Twin Epilogue Finished)GalNet - A New Local Power Emerging in Windfall(Windfall same as {20003,5030001})

(Email Text)According to reports, the Vigor Syndicate has slowly but steadily lost some of its grip over the Windfall(Windfall same as {20003,5030001}) system. Due to the volatile conditions within the Syndicate, the situation has never been entirely stable, but now it appears that an outside force has made a move to challenge the Syndicate's control. Sources from within the Syndicate have said that several high-ranking members of the organisation have died in a station attack, which has left them rudderless. The outside power is said to have connections to the Northriver Company, which holds considerable influence over both Windfall and Avarice(Avarice same as {20005,9033}), and has been accused of working with the crime syndicate in the past. The hostilities seem to have ceased for now, but whether this new power and the Vigor Syndicate can operate out of the same system simultaneously remains to be seen.

Eron Alba
- Foreign Affairs Correspondent, GalNet
(Email Title - Twin Ending and Protectyon sold)CBNN News - Northriver Company Competitor Sets Up in Avarice(Avarice same as {20005,9033})

(Email Text)In a surprising turn of events, a new source of Protectyon has entered the market. Riptide Rakers have gratefully rushed to place their orders for the vital substance. The question of whether the product is the exact same substance, or some form of derivative of it, has not yet been answered. It is, however, important to stress that it has proven to be functionally identical to the product sold by the Northriver Company, keeping stations safe from the Tide phenomenon. As a result, the Northriver Company's stock prices have fallen significantly for the first time since the company went public.\n\nYoyunis Tertasobas Zusilas IV - Economics Correspondent, CBNN News
(Player Choice)I'm ready.(Answer to 'Ready to rummage?'/ready to go?)
(Player Choice)Not yet.(Answer to 'Ready to rummage?'/ready to go?)
(Player Choice)Can I pay in advance?(Player offering to pay)
(Player Choice)No, I don't.(Asked if knows any scientists)
(Player Choice)Yes, there is one...(Asked if knows any scientists)
I lost it...(Player Choice, in case inventory item was somehow lost)
Be proud of your achievements!(Player Choice)
I noticed your impressive ship.(Player Choice)
I refuse to back down!(Player Choice)
How did you find this?(Referring to secret system)

page.title: Criminal Plot
page.t: Empyrean Curs(Pirate Crew Name, 'Curs' refers to the dogs)
Chipmunk(Nickname given to the player after smuggling; for cheek pouch and belittling reasons)
The Arcadian Endeavour Contraband Connection(Mission Title)

This is Maestro speaking, captain of Arcadian Endeavour and leader of Empyrean Curs. Arcadian Endeavour has made name for itself by navigating far corners of Jump Gate network, breaking the laws and regulations of a vast number of governments and organisations. This posting is open to anyone not intimidated by oppressive authority crackdown on pirate activity. Experience in smuggling and avoiding law enforcement a plus. Must bring own ship with sufficient cargo capacity.\n\nCome talk on bridge of Arcadian Endeavour for further information.(Mission description, Arcadian Endeavour same as {30252,201}, Empyrean Curs same as {30252,10})

To prove that creature is capable of piracy and a good fit for Empyrean Curs, Split tasks creature with fulfilling delivery to client. Stay alert, as freight is considered contraband in most inhabited regions of network. Client is anxiously awaiting delivery of Spaceweed \(for medical purposes\).(Mission description, Spaceweed same as {20201,4101})
(Money )and the recognition of a crew of free spirits(Mission Reward)
Return with a larger cargo capacity(Custom Action)
As a first test of your resolve, and familiarity with illicit activity, the Maestro had you deliver Spaceweed on behalf of the Empyrean Curs.(Logbook Text)

Creature now member of Empyrean Curs. Congratulations! Next, Chipmunk should get to know fellow pirates and dip toes into different aspects of running extra-legal enterprise. Talk to Ace, Axiom and Split to set things in motion.(Mission Thread Text)
Facilitating the Empyrean Curs' ascent(Mission Thread Reward)
You have met all the members of the Empyrean Curs, and gained insights into various illegal activities that pirates can utilise to turn a profit.(Logbook Text)

Split needs to get hands on specific Woodworm Security Protocols, which are hard to come by because they were leaked illegally. Only option is to find new Black Market contact who would be willing to sell them. Split teach creature how to establish such contact.(Mission Text, Woodworm Security Protocols same as {20201,55401})
Making a Black Market connection(Mission Reward)

In order to fund our little organisation, we are quite dependent on the charity of others; traders of valuable wares for the most part. It will be your task to convince one of these traders to part with their cargo, even if it goes against their profit motive. But fret not, Chipmunk, I will accompany you every step of the way!(Mission Text)

When we're not holding up traders or conducting shady deals, we are usually pillaging a station in one form or another. While it might be tempting to just surround a station and make it surrender through sheer firepower, there are other, more subtle, ways to go about it. Allow me to teach you about station hacking. Fret not, for I shall guide your hand at every step.(Mission Text)
The forbidden knowledge of station hacking(Mission Reward)
(custom objective)Protect Arcadian Endeavour while its drones are operating

To establish relations with station black marketeer, creature sometimes required to provide contact person with certain illegal inventory wares. In this case, client demands Unstable Crystals, which are by-product of mining asteroids. Be aware, though, these crystals illegal in most space. So keep away from police!(Mission Thread Text, Unstable Crystals same as {20201,17001})

Empyrean Curs are turning into household name now, even outside of Windfall. Split looking to pull off even more ambitious project. One that involves multiple steps and plenty of preparation work. Talk to members of Curs to see how Chipmunk can assist in laying foundation.(Mission Thread Text, Windfall same as {20005,9057})
Laying the groundwork for an ambitious heist(Mission Thread Reward)
You helped all three Empyrean Curs with tasks that will ultimately further Maestro's schemes.(Logbook Text)

The Maestro's big plans seem to involve a Teladi station. In preparation, he has asked me to procure specific blueprints, and I thought this might be a good opportunity to take your counter-security skills to the next level. Disciple, come talk to me when you are ready to receive the holy knowledge of hacking.(Mission Text)

In our profession, there are few things as satisfying as seizing control over a massive ship. It is just what we do best. Usually we sell these new acquisitions for profit or, if the ships are combat ready, add them to our own little pirate navy. Not so the one that the Maestro asked us to procure for his next big plan. It is supposed to be as plain and unremarkable as possible. Now if that's not a unique opportunity to show the Chipmunk the ropes, I don't know what is!(Mission Text)

(appended to briefing)There are different ways to hire Marines. You can, for example, talk to someone in person on a station, hire them for a fee, and assign them to your ship. Alternatively, you can hire rookie Marines when upgrading a ship at either an Equipment Dock, Wharf, or Shipyard, depending on the size of the ship. On the Crew tab of your Ship Information menu, you can also move any existing crew member to a Marine role. Use the sliders to try out different job compositions for your crew.
(appended to briefing)The more Marines you send on a boarding operation, the better the chances of success. Marines with high Boarding and Morale skills are especially effective.

Empyrean Curs planning to raid station in Teladi space. Problem is Ministry of Finance fleet stationed close to target. Split needs creature to get fleet's attention and draw them away, so that Arcadian Endeavour can initiate pillaging. Talk to Split for further details!(Mission Text)
Insights into Ministry of Finance patrol fleet behaviour(Mission Reward)

Empyrean Curs looking to steal Ministry ship prototype equipped with new cargo spoofing technology.(Mission Text)

Ministry Science Division Prototype Hangar Access(Mission Reward)
You successfully infiltrated Mellerd's operation, and established access to the Ministry hangar.(Logbook Text)
You betrayed Maestro, and laid the foundations for an ambush during the prototype heist.(Logbook Text)
Report your successful infiltration to the Maestro.(Mission Text)

After learning that Lu t'Cca is a former Cur, and Maestro's brother, preparations for the heist have been hastened. Help either the Axiom or the Ace before moving to steal the Ministry prototype and free the Maestro's brother!(Mission Text)

Help Ace to seize a better ship.(Mission Text)

Help Axiom to bypass turret security configurations.(Mission Text)

Time for heist has come. Split plan was significantly shaken up due to unforeseen developments. As you know, Target is Ministry of Finance prison station helmed by former associate Kriss Mellerd. First priority now to rescue Split brother, but Curs still intent on following through with parts of original plan. Mellerd will expect us but Curs try to go unnoticed as long as possible, break out Lu t'Cca, and escape in experimental prototype. Mellerd not expect us pushing deeper into station, and will be caught off guard.(Mission Text)

Surviving the Battle of Woodworm Scrubs(Logbook Title)

You rescued Lu t'Cca from his cell, and swiped an experimental Ministry of Finance prototype while you were at it. Mellerd tried to ambush the Empyrean Curs, but her attempt failed due to swift and decisive measures on your part.(Logbook Text - Curs Side)
You stole the Ministry of Finance prototype, and in doing so drew the Maestro and his Empyrean Curs close to Woodworm Scrubs, where Mellerd promptly sprung her trap.(Logbook Text - Mellerd Side)

(Email Title)GalNet - Increase in Pirate Activity Results in Instability

(Email Text)Ever since the unfortunate reconnection of Windfall to the Jump Gate network, crime has surged in the neighbouring systems of this once-prosperous location. Consequently, several inter-network trading groups have issued trade and travel warnings, and one prospective Teladi developer has pulled out of promising trade contract negotiations. This increase in crime is driven partly by delinquents, drawn to the safe haven for criminals created by the Vigor Syndicate, but also by the various independent pirate groups that are known to operate from within the system. The Ministry of Finance is still predominantly occupied with the Xenon menace, but they have nonetheless vowed to put an end to any pirate incursions into the systems under their governance, and are looking to mobilise additional fleets. The Argon Federation has not yet commented on these developments, and experts suggest that this hesitancy to commit to any long-term operations may stem from their on-going struggles with other threats bordering their territories.\n\nMek Kharn - Crime Reporter, GalNet
(Email Title)GalNet - Daring Escape from Ministry of Finance Prison

(Email Text)In a shocking development, Woodworm Scrubs, a Ministry of Finance prison, has just been compromised. It appears that a highly dangerous criminal was sprung by a pirate group who are calling themselves the "Empyrean Curs". From what our sources tell us, the group utilised the interior of the prison complex to their advantage in the audacious heist. Not only did they succeed in breaking out their fellow member, a blood-thirsty Split, but they also managed to get their hands on experimental Ministry of Finance technology. Ministry of Finance officials have yet to issue a statement.\n\nMek Kharn - Crime Reporter, GalNet
(Email Title)GalNet - Escape Attempt Thwarted by Valiant Ministry of Finance

(Email Text)A group of criminals known as the "Empyrean Curs" have been caught attempting to break one of their members out of Woodworm Scrubs, a prison complex bordering Windfall. The prisoner, a male Split, had been apprehended by Ministry of Finance patrols, and was awaiting relocation to a different facility to be tried on charges of piracy and murder. Several other members of the criminal organisation forced their way into the station, only to be met by a Ministry of Finance patrol when they re-emerged from within the complex. "It was quite easy to stop the break-out in its tracks. The delinquents were ill-prepared and immediately folded when their pathetic attempt at a break-out was challenged", Kriss Mellerd said in a public statement. Whether any of the pirates managed to escape the altercation alive, remains unclear.\n\nMek Kharn - Crime Reporter, GalNet

page.title: Boron Plot
page.t: (Title)Leader of Lilac Fin(person is male, "Lilac Fin" is the name of a flight of ships)
(Title)Leader of Azure Fin(person is female, "Azure Fin" is the name of a flight of ships)
(Terran Diplomacy Ship named after some other mythological sword)Gramr
(Boron carrier ship named after Menelaus, a deceased Boron queen)Menelaus' Reminiscence(same as {20101,122601})
Mnemosyne(ALI Mission ship, name from Greek mythology)

(Mission Description)I am pleased and overjoyed that someone has stumbled upon my secret transmission! Should you wish to meet in person, o mysterious traveller, then make haste and journey to the location I have indicated. I will follow as soon as the inattentiveness of my Split captors allows.(the "location" is a sector that will be highlighted in the mission objective)
(Mission Reward)Access to the Greatest Scientific Mind of our Time(indicating that you will meet Boso Ta, who's a scientist)

(Mission Text)Our scientists were able to pick up unusual readings from an inactive Jump Gate. These readings, alongside messenger drone communication with the Queendom of Boron in Kingdom End, make us suspect that a Jump Gate reactivation is imminent. In response, the Alliance of the Word has dispatched an expedition to investigate these matters further. As this is a matter of grave importance, with implications for every inhabitant of our network, we cordially invite any interested parties to attend the investigation, and potential subsequent exploration.
(Mission Text Pt2 - Sandbox)Our expedition is mainly looking for capable pilots to aid our scouting effort, so we would advise anyone intending to join our endeavour to bring a nimble ship.

(Mission Text Pt2 - Boron GS1)As part of our expedition from the start, you have been assigned the task of scouting any unexplored areas. A suitable ship has been made available to you for this purpose.

(Mission Text)The recent Jump Gate activation has connected us to the Commonwealth at large. In response, I have instructed my charges to begin immediate construction of a new shipyard, but we are still short on several critical resources. Please, would you be so kind as to aid us in our undertaking in any way you can? Even small contributions would be greatly appreciated: $STORAGEPERCENT$%\n\n$REQUIREMENTS$

(Mission Text)The Jump Gate did indeed activate, and revealed a hitherto unknown system. Unfortunately, that also meant that our expedition was not received by our Boron allies, as we had hoped. Now you need to help investigate and map out the uncharted region. Stay alert, though, as we do not know what may lie in wait.
(Custom Action)Pass through the activated Jump Gate

(Logbook Text)During your exploratory outing you came across a Boron, who introduced herself as Nila Ti. She was very accommodating, and offered to acquaint your expedition with the the Royal Steward.

(Mission Text)Unfortunately, this pocket of the network is not connected to the Boron Queendom at large either, so we shall continue onwards. There are still several inactive gates in this region that we can conduct experiments on. To be able to do that efficiently, though, we need the blessing of the local administration.\n\nNila Ti has offered to introduce us to the Royal Steward, and I want you, explorer, to accompany me. This meeting is crucial to ensure that everyone is on the same page.
(Custom Action)Mediate between the parties to find a solution
(Logbook Text - Good result)You successfully cleared up all misunderstandings between the Alliance and Leda We, and secured a mutually beneficial agreement.
(Logbook Text - Middling result)After some back and forth, you were able to convince Leda We to let the expedition proceed, but he is far from enthusiastic about it.
(Logbook Text - bad result)The negotiations failed, and the expedition had to resort to leverage to force Leda We to go along with your plans. Still, you may proceed, but at what cost?

(Mission Text)Thanks to Leda We's assistance, we now know of three potential Jump Gates to investigate. One of them is located in Sanctuary of Darkness(Sanctuary of Darkness same as {20005,9005}), a Kha'ak-infested, hostile system. Before we commit our entire expedition to any one gate, we need to identify which one is the most suitable candidate, and find a safe way forward. This is where you come in, explorer.
(Custom Text, meant to be encrypted nonsense)**?*##-*!**##*
(Objective Text)Nav Beacons to map out a safe path between gates
(Appended Mission Text)In order to create a path between the gates, place your Nav Beacons inside of the guidance spheres indicated in yellow on your radar and your map.

(Logbook Text)Thanks to your valiant efforts, the expedition has identified a suitable candidate, and was able to swiftly make their way through the dangerous terrain. Now they are actively working on setting up the first experiments.

(Mission Text)Assistant! The Alliance of the Word are beginning their experimentation on the Jump Gate, but they have cautioned us not to expect actionable results too soon. That is tragic news, but perhaps I can conjure up another errand for you, to keep both of us busy. You see, ever since I first laid eyes on the Great Reef nebula, I noticed some... shall we say peculiarities? This discovery could turn out to be of significant importance, but I need you to independently verify my findings before I act prematurely.
(Logbook Text)Boso's hunch turned out to be true. You came across a unique distant stellar phenomenon that might hold the secret to interacting with Jump Gates.

(Mission Text)Boso Ta's findings are of great interest, and if our scientists' first projections hold true, they could vastly expedite our experiment timeline. Explorer, return back to our expedition and help us see this whole endeavour through to the end. We do not know what challenges lie ahead, so come prepared.
(Custom Action)Have an audience with Her Majesty

(Logbook Text)Thanks to the joint efforts of Alliance of the Word, Boso Ta and yourself, you were able to interface with a jump gate and establish a stable connection to Kingdom End. As a reward you were all invited to have an audience with the queen.
(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron decrees a shipment of BoFu to be shipped to a friend of the Queendom.
(Logbook Text)With the help of a ploy, Boso Ta managed to fill his BoFu reserves and will not suffer from inadequate nutrition any longer.
(Mission Title)The Queen's Herald(Queen's Herald same as {1021,1500})

(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to re-establish diplomatic relations with various governments in the Jump gate network. You are tasked with reaching out to various parties on the Queendom's behalf.
(Logbook Text)With your help, the Boron Queendom managed to re-establish its diplomatic relations with various governments in the Jump gate network.
(Mission Reward)Passing the Mission Manager 101(introductory course about the mission manager)
(Mission Text)Before you can embark on the Queen's missions, you need to receive your debriefing from Numanckaret.
(Logbook Text)You received your debriefing from Numanckaret and unlocked the Queen's missions.
(Mission Text)Complete this mission to conclude Numanckaret's debriefing and unlock the Queen's missions.

(Mission Text)Your first royal mission is a BoFu delivery to Boso Ta. BoFu is usually sold at BoFu Chemical Lab stations. Find a station with a lucrative trade offer to acquire the required amounts of BoFu.(BoFu Chemical Lab same as {20201,7104})
(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to provide Boron combat ships to the Hatikvah Free League. Your task is to provide a first fleet, while the Queendom negotiates further shipments.
(Logbook Text)With your assistance, the Boron Queendom secured an arms deal with the Hatikvah Free League.
(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to exchange dignitaries with the Paranid Empire to establish diplomatic relations. As the Paranid counterpart never arrived, an investigation is in order.
(Logbook Text)Following your rescue of a Paranid dignitary, the Boron Queendom secured diplomatic relations with the Paranid Empire.

(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to establish diplomatic relations with the Terran Protectorate. In order to construct a Boron habitat to house a diplomatic delegation, the Protectorate expects the delivery of a Nishala water sample, complete with all its salts and microorganisms. The delivery never arrived and the sample, now lost, is believed to be in a bar. You are tasked with recovering it, and completing the mission without drawing attention to its prior difficulties.
(Logbook Text)You successfully delivered the Nishala Water sample to the Terran Protectorate.
(Mission Title)Riptide Waters(Hinting at the Faction Riptide Rakers)
(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to help the Riptide Rakers of Avarice with water deliveries. You are tasked with delivering the first shipment. Be wary of potential adversaries.
(Logbook Text)You successfully delivered water to the Riptide Rakers.
(Mission Title)Diplomatic Outpost in Teladi Space(Diplomatic Outpost same as {20103,3701})

(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to establish a Diplomatic Outpost in order to stay in contact with the Teladi Company. You are tasked with initiating, overseeing and completing the construction of the new Boron station.(Diplomatic Outpost same as {20103,3701})
(Mission Reward)Forgiveness for Stealing(in case the player stole a ship in the ch8 carrier mission)
(Logbook Text)You successfully built a Diplomatic Outpost in Teladi space for the Boron Queendom.(Diplomatic Outpost same as {20103,3701})
(Mission Text)The Queendom of Boron seeks to thank you for your service. Head back to Queen Polypheides to receive your reward.
(Logbook Text)The Queendom of Boron thanks you for your service.
(Mission title)The High Road(this is an English idiom; translate freely to something that alludes to a highway being built through a dangerous territory, swarming with enemies, as a safe passage)

(Mission description)The carrier ship Menelaus' Reminiscence is operating around the Highway construction site in the sector Sanctuary of Darkness, to facilitate the fortification of a safe passage between the freshly reconnected Boron territories. Leda We, former Royal Steward of the Provinces Adrift, has cordially requested your aid in his defence against the interfering Kha'ak.(Menelaus' Reminiscence same as {20101,122601}, Highway same as {20001,401}, Sanctuary of Darkness same as {20005,9005}, Leda We is a male fleet commander, title Royal Steward same as {30253,152}, Provinces Adrift same as {20203,3401})

(Logbook entry - mission failure)The ship that commander Leda We has furnished you with has gone MIA. The carrier ship Menelaus' Reminiscence's mission in the sector Sanctuary of Darkness will have to continue without your help.(Leda We is a male fleet commander, Menelaus' Reminiscence same as {20101,122601}, Sanctuary of Darkness same as {20005,9005})

(Signature - GalNet - Foreign Affairs)

Eron Alba
- Foreign Affairs Correspondent, GalNet

(Email Text)This is an automated message.

The Alliance of the Word has recently become aware of an imminent Jump Gate activation in Heretic's End. Not only is this an exceptional opportunity to study the Jump Gate's mechanisms up close, but thanks to our communication with Kingdom End, we have reason to expect that we may make contact with the Boron Queendom upon activation. As the diplomatic centre for galactic collaboration and scientific progress, we extend an open invitation to anyone who wishes to join our expedition. Since we cannot anticipate what we might be faced with on the other side of the gate, we are primarily looking for flexible pilots with scouting experience.

Monisessas Yooses Yoyunis V - Head of Communications Office
Alliance of the Word
(Email Title)GalNet - Argon and Boron Announce Bilateral Battlegroup(Bilateral Battlegroup same as {20204,17101})

(Email Text)With the resumption of their alliance, the Queendom of Boron and the Argon Federation announce the adoption of two Bilateral Battlegroup fleets: a Boron fleet will be stationed in Federation space, while a Federation fleet will patrol Boron space. This accord is set to improve cooperation between both militaries, and project their commitment to their mutual defence pact.(Bilateral Battlegroup same as {20204,17101})
(Email Title)GalNet - Free League Signs Boron Arms Contract

(Email Text)In a surprising move, the Hatikvah Free League signed an arms deal with the Queendom of Boron. The Boron agreed to provide military ships and pilot training. The new ships will be used to patrol and protect Free League space, and installations, against intruders.

(Email Text part 1)Since its reconnection to Commonwealth space, the Queendom of Boron has worked to re-establish diplomatic ties with all major powers. The Boron are now maintaining cordial relations with most factions. Most notably, the Queendom of Boron reinvigorated its alliance with the Argon Federation.
(Email Text part 2, only if Split DLC is active)However, an attempt to end hostilities between Boron and Split failed.
(Email Text part 3)After its diplomatic outreach, the Queendom of Boron is now considered well established within the Commonwealth.
(Email Title)GalNet - Queen Inaugurates Sanctuary of Darkness Highway(Highway same as {20001,401}, Sanctuary of Darkness same as {20005,9005})

(Email Text)In an unusually decisive move, the Queendom of Boron unveiled the latest addition to its Highway network. This megastructure, the plans for which appear to have been drafted at speed after the reactivation of the Kingdom End Jump Gate, now spans almost the entirety of Sanctuary of Darkness, a notoriously dangerous and inhospitable sector that now lies at the heart of the Queendom's territory.

During her exhaustive inauguration speech, Queen Polypheides took the opportunity to recapitulate over the events leading up to the reunification, and to personally commend the commitment of several foreign actors who were instrumental in facilitating this "new era of entanglement". The address was delivered to members of the Boron press, select correspondents of the Alliance of the Word, and various guests of honour, including the Royal Council for Redevelopment of the former Provinces Adrift.

While the term "prestige project" has been bandied about, the overall tone of tonight's political commentary has remained optimistic regarding the promised effects on economic coherence and societal integration within the newly repaired Queendom.

In response to GalNet's enquiries, the Royal Press Agency was swift to clarify that the "careful and reluctant" actions of Boron military personnel, during the continued defence of the Highway structure, in no way confirm alleged plans for a systematic advance against the local Kha'ak population.(Queendom of Boron same as {20203,1301}, Highway same as {20001,401}, Sanctuary of Darkness same as {20005,9005}, Provinces Adrift same as {20203,3401})

(Email Text)Greetings, friend!

With deepest regrets and unfathomable disappointment, we noticed what appears to have been you appropriating Queendom property. As a result, the reward for your mission, to establish a diplomatic outpost with the Teladi Company, has been adjusted. While completing this task will no longer grant you a capable Boron ship to call your own, we offer forgiveness for your transgression.

With kindest regards and a wealth of hope, yours truly, Leda We.(Diplomatic Outpost same as {20103,3701})

(Email Text)The Wayfinder Expedition has arrived at its intermediate destination, an inactive gate in Sanctuary of Darkness which we suspect to be a suitable candidate for further experimentation. The gate's potential was confirmed by reading its cache which, while only allowing an incomplete reading, indicates a possible connection to Kingdom End.

With the assistance of the local administration, we are currently procuring the building materials required to begin construction on a Gate Link Terminal, an elaborate support infrastructure which will allow us broader access to the gate's mechanisms. It will also be used to funnel energy into the gate when we attempt to force an activation.

The blueprints for this terminal were supplied to us by our Kingdom End allies, but we will still need to conduct a series of tests to ensure that everything operates as expected. It is also not yet clear exactly how much energy needs to be supplied. Our scientists have a rough idea, but we do not know whether the required amount of energy is impacted by the supply on the Kingdom End side, or indeed whether the Boron on the other side have already covered some of the demand. Either way we expect the limited communication and immense energy requirements to present a challenge going forward.

As well as ensuring that these requirements are met, our experts have also begun the arduous task of decrypting the data that our team was able to read from the gate's cache. With the help of that recovered data, we expect to eventually be able to home in on the Kingdom End system's positional data, but we will still have to verify these coordinates independently.

Although all of this presents a significant challenge, our biggest obstacle is our inability to interface with the gate's operating system. Over the decades, many attempts have been made, but so far every one has drawn a blank. We are missing that one elusive variable; some sort of key to activate the system. While we have clear ideas on how to tackle all of the other obstacles, this one remains the most puzzling, and I suspect that overcoming it could well take several more decades.

Considering all of this, we expect to be able to begin our initial round of experiments in about four years, and to adjust our timeline according to the results.

In the meantime, with a safe path through Sanctuary of Darkness now established, we welcome anyone who wants to visit the Wayfinder in order to check on our progress. I would be glad to answer any further questions in person.

Numanckaret
-Commanding Officer of the Wayfinder Expedition

(Email Text)We did it!

Thanks to the initiative displayed by the scientist Boso Ta and one of our own expedition members, we were able to successfully conduct a Jump Gate activation on a much accelerated timeline. First of all, I wish to take a moment to congratulate everyone who was involved in seeing this expedition through to completion. Your contributions were invaluable.

Ever since we made contact, our science team has been in constant communication with the scientists of Kingdom End. Comparing our notes, here is what we can say with near certainty:

To make an activation possible, you require two inactive but compatible gates. Compatibility can be verified by reading the gates' caches. This can pose the first challenge, since these datasets tend to be incomplete and encrypted in various ways.

Furthermore, an activation requires a large amount of energy. Interestingly, however, that energy does not need to be supplied to both sides of the gate pairing equally. Luckily, Kingdom End provided the vast majority of the energy for our experiment. In order to actually activate the gate, you have to introduce a particular sort of signal to home in on the selected destination. We do not know whether that signal is derived from stellar phenomena, as a sort of navigational constant, or whether it is intended as some kind of passcode. We are also unsure if this signal will work on all gates, or if there are different ciphers for different gates. Further investigation is obviously necessary.

Finally, we do expect that others will pick up on what we have learnt. We have already put together a more in-depth report that we intend to share with our allies, in confidence. It is also of crucial importance that we share this revelation with as many of our lost colonies as possible. As you are all aware, however, messenger drones are not a secure means of communication. Inevitably this information will spread amongst hostile factions. While the level of possible manipulation seems to be very limited, and requires immense amounts of coordination and resources, it is my expectation that we will see attempts to replicate our success by various factions in the years to come.

Be proud, and take a moment to reflect on the implications of what we have achieved.

Numanckaret
-Commanding Officer of the Wayfinder Expedition

(Email Text)Hello everyone!

Expedition leader Numanckaret has asked me to put in writing my thoughts on the Jump Gate opening in Heretic's End, which, I confess, has unnerved me. I am preparing a summary of the scientific debates so far, for the expedition's final report. You, my fellow explorers, get to review my latest draft. So, please tell me if any of these talking points are overly tangential or sleep-inducing!

----------

First, a word on the general public discourse: signs of activity in Heretic's End, coming so soon after a communication from Kingdom End explicitly mentioning Jump Gate experiments, were met with widespread optimism. Media outlets across the Gate network gravitated towards the rather unscientific notion that the Boron were the only missing members of the pre-Dark era Community of Planets. Purely by a process of elimination, they assumed it had to be them on the other side of this Jump Gate.

At the other end of the spectrum, doomsday prophecies proliferated. Permanckress, one of Sacred Relic's more controversial figures, famously presented socio-mathematical calculations in an effort to "prove" that the collapse of Boron society had inevitably occurred mere months after the bespoke messenger drone's dispatch. According to his followers, we may well be listening to the calls of a long-dead, or at the very least economically depleted, civilisation.

"In all probability", Permanckress asserts, the Boron would not be in a position to start a Jump Gate experiment, send a messenger drone, and almost perfectly synchronise the successful conclusion of the experiment with the arrival of the drone, years later. This would be a vanishingly unlikely coincidence, and he suggests that the massive investment in Jump Gate research required would, in itself, catalyse Boron economic collapse.

Permanckress' most vocal opponent, Sibasomos Sissandras Lalundas II, on the other hand, has attempted to sway the discourse by characterising the Queendom of Boron as an exceptionally stable society, profoundly focused on technological advancement. If she is to be believed, Boron technology might not have advanced to the point of Jump Gate manipulation, yet may have triggered an interference signal strong enough to prompt a cascading reaction, ultimately reaching Heretic's End itself. Permanckress retorted that the only "cascading reaction" would have been the complete annihilation of Boron life due to a failsafe installed by the Gate's builders.

This remark was clearly a reference to Sihoban Tiago, former professor of the New Hewa Academy of Sciences, who, before her recent retirement, made waves with similar speculations about an omniscient observer monitoring technological progress. In one famous lecture, originally intended to cover the life cycle of magnetars, she claimed that "science is dead" and further discoveries are purely at the whim of unseen forces.

Evidence appears to support the theory that Jump Gate interference is indeed ultimately impossible. During the Dark, several sectors drained vast resources in futile attempts to end their isolation, in some cases triggering economic, political and social collapse sufficient to render them surface-bound. Since then, the dream of reactivating Jump Gates, especially to reconnect with lost sections of one's own civilisation, has defined countless scientific careers.

A glimmer of hope remains. The incredibly small amount of data from the Jump Gate nacelle that we have so far been able to access, has been theorised to be some kind of "cache" for remote access. For the Heretic's End Jump Gate, this cached data lists among its entries the coordinates of Kingdom End. Granted, so do at least 17 other Gates in the known network, but Watchful Gaze is the first successful confirmation of a coordinate data-sync between pre- and post-Gate opening nacelle cache readings. It seems reasonable to hypothesise that this coordinate data constitutes an affinity for other Jump Gates, either because the Gates were once connected in the distant past, or because the Gate builders, in their time, made a careful selection of auspicious Jump Gate network layouts. The logic behind the prioritisation of this cached data will have to be further investigated, by observing future Jump Gate connections.

Rick Feynman famously postulated that "one does not, by knowing and applying all fundamental laws as they are known today, gain any understanding of the Jump Gates". In this spirit, I infer from our findings the necessity of optimism. The petabytes of as yet undeciphered data within the nacelles are barely touched, and there is a distinct possibility that one of the Jump Gates ahead will add another breadcrumb on our trail to Kingdom End!

----------

How's THAT for an ending!? This has me all excited for my next mission. See you all among the stars!

Lexi Fieldman
-Mission Specialist(author is female, addresses a group of friends and colleagues in a somewhat informal way in the first and last paragraph, and writes a proper formal essay in the main body of text; "Numanckaret" is her male superior, same as {30253,101}; "Jump Gate" same as {20001,701}; "Heretic's End" is a system, same as {20005,9015}; "Kingdom End" is a system, same as {20005,2009}; the "Dark" is an era in history; "Sacred Relic" is a system, same as {20005,3002}; "Watchful Gaze" is a system, same as {20005,9009}; "Rick Feynman" is a male scientist, same as {30285,101}, but without the Dr.; "Lexi Fieldman" same as {30253,121})

(Email Title)Unlocking the Gates: The Computronium Connection

Hello everyone!

I trust you've been following the recent stirrings on the Jump Gate front with as much curiosity - and perhaps trepidation - as I have. As scientists, and indeed as citizens of this network of civilisations, it is impossible to overstate the implications of these unfolding events. So, let me indulge in a little elaboration.

Our long-standing assumption has been that the Queendom of Boron's understanding of the Ancients' Jump Gate technology was relatively superficial. Historically, the late research ethicist Nola Hi once managed to provoke a corrective response from the Sohnen by manipulating the Jump Gate connected to the so-called Terraformer Refuge. You may remember from basic history lessons the remarkable tale of Kyle Brennan, Elena Kho, and Nola Hi, who found themselves confined within that refuge for months, setting up a precarious base on Darehitorimo. After that episode, silence. No man-made, or shall we say, Boron-made Jump Gate network manipulation occurred again. Yes, the Terrans have gates, but if anything, they're even more secretive than the Sohnen.

It turns out we may have underestimated the QoB. Building on Nola Hi's foundational discoveries from the pre-Dark era, our brilliant friend Boso Ta appears to have unlocked insights into the cryptic architecture of the Jump Gates. As it turns out, these gates do not operate on conventional software or AI but are instead controlled by a computronium partial - a minuscule, almost sentient, computational element just beneath the threshold of awareness. Fascinatingly, this partial can "resonate" or communicate with an external computronium partial. Though we do not possess the ability to synthesize computronium yet, the QoB reportedly obtained a small sample of it in an expedition to the galactic abyss a few decades ago. Most astonishingly, it appears that they have discovered a way to use it to deliver a constrained set of instructions to a Jump Gate. Whether this is an intentional backdoor or a zero-eon exploit is still unclear, though one suspects the Sohnen may be fully aware of this and are permitting the access.

In short, the rumours are true: the Queendom of Boron has re-integrated two long-dormant gates into the network! Orbital injections are complete, and as I write, expeditions are already underway to uncover what secrets lie beyond. Forgive my excited ramblings, but the potential here is enormous. Imagine, if we could instruct and control any Jump Gate in the network! The possibilities for exploration, for discovery - they're nearly infinite.

So, what do you think? I, for one, am eager to continue this journey, whether through our shared written musings or in person, on the far side of some as-yet-unmapped Jump Gate route.

Until then, onward, my friends!

Lexi Fieldman
-Mission Specialist

page.title: Venture Missions
page.descr: Text used to describe missions to other players' universes
page.t: (no return)The venture team has failed to return!
Encountered person of interest during venture!

The discovery of this warp anomaly and the research that properly allows us to make use of it opens up countless literal realms of possibility. Send a ship out on a peaceful mission to explore one of these parallel universes so that we may better understand them.

Now that we have unlocked the path to parallel universes, we can send out scout ships to explore them. In doing so we may learn more about its inhabitants as well as what binds our universes together.

There is a great deal more to be learned from rocks and gas than many would have you believe - doubly true when they come from a different universe. If we are able to learn the chemical composition of anything mining ships we send abroad bring back, it can only benefit us. Not only will they provide us with a shower of new scientific knowledge, but as long as the minerals and gases we find are close enough to what is required by refineries here, we stand to profit too.

I am willing to guarantee that intelligent life will always trade, in one way or another. Whether or not we load up a transporter here and send it across a different universe to sell its wares, or send it to another universe with the order to stock up there, I would bet that a trader of any skill could bring back some currency of worth to us. Travelling from station to station or planet to planet will also give us the opportunity to map out more of these parallel universes, and may even provide some very necessary diplomatic relations.

There is definitely potential to sending an empty trading ship out into the multi-verse. Risk too; we cannot guarantee that any other universe is willing to accept our currency, we cannot guarantee that our traders can bring anything back that we can sell here. However, the multi-verse is... big. Very big. I am willing to bet that somewhere out there, there is a place, person or organisation that will accept our credits in exchange for something at least close enough to one of our economy resources that it is useful. Now we just have to find them.

Trading between universes is complicated. I find there to be a reasonable chance, though still small in the grand scale of things, that if we fill a transporter with resources here and send it across the multiverse, someone, somewhere will want to buy what we are selling. There is significantly less of a chance that said individual or organisation can give us something of worth in return, but in such situations we must trust in traders of all skill levels to be able to negotiate properly. What else are travelling salesmen for?

We have a good understanding of how dangerous and troublesome the Xenon are, having been almost constantly reminded of the threat they pose for several centuries, at this point. It is an almost mathematical certainty that someone in another universe made the same mistake as the Terrans once did, and so I am confident that we can find Xenon in other universes than our own. Sending pilots out on patrols against them could prove good combat practice for your pilots, and is almost a diplomatic service to those inhabiting these universes.

If we can seek out a universe in which there is intelligent life and a legal system, then it is almost certain that we will find piracy too. Perhaps we can lend a helping hand here; send pilots out to patrol against these pirates - not only will it help the other universes that we come across, but is also likely to be lucrative for us. I am sure local authorities will be pleased by our work, and of course we can keep whatever we can scavenge from wrecked or abandoned pirate ships.

If so inclined, you can seek out ships belonging to multi-verse equivalents of the factions present in our version of the Jump Gate network, to... negotiate with them, aggressively. It would give your pilots combat experience, with little consequence for us here, and of course comes with the chance of salvage. Do take caution though. I'm sure that any faction you choose to measure yourself against in a parallel universe would react just as unhappily to an attack as any of ours, and of course, should anyone have developed the same technology as us, we could open ourselves to retaliation.

With a countless number of universes at our doorstep, it is quite probable to run across someone else who has developed or discovered the same technology as us. They may be friend or foe, and will probably treat us the same way we treat them. And so, if you wish to make a name for yourself in the multi-verse, you can send ships out to target these individuals, and reap the benefits of doing so. Just bear in mind that with this technology, we may open ourselves up to counter-strike from them, and possibly their allies.

There are many things in this life better than conflict, but should you feel the need to train your combat pilots in an environment where they cannot possibly fall into trouble with our authorities, you can of course send them to other universes to target combat ships there instead. Naturally, this comes with its own risks; I am sure the entire multi-verse has access to equally skilled pilots, and there is a chance that one of your ships returns damaged, or does not return at all.

Though I don't usually condone violence, there are two advantages to targeting the transport vessels of other universes. Firstly, it disrupts economies; giving us a distinct advantage in any multiverse-wide conflict that might break out as a result of multiple universes having access to this technology. Secondly, it may give us the opportunity to study both the wares used in these universes, and the effect of cross-universe travel on these wares. If you do take this approach, do be careful however. I doubt local authorities will be too happy about this kind of behaviour.

During my captivity, I was often told that there is no greater show of force, of how far one is willing to go, than to target civilian ships. Split are rather barbaric, but it is a good point. Unable to defend themselves, I am sure if we were to target civilians of other universes, we would eventually be able to find something of worth to bring back to our own universe. Of course, we would not be breaking any of our own laws, but I must believe that authorities in these universes would not look kindly on such an attack.

My mind goes once again to the inevitability of conflict between universes, should more than one unlock the secrets of this technology. If we need an advantage in such a conflict, there is none greater than targeting the mining ships that fuel their economies. This slows down the production of combat ships that can be used against us, as well as affording us the opportunity to retrieve any resources they were collecting for ourselves. Of course, this could come at a great cost for our own pilots; should they be caught I fear the consequences would be rather dire.

page.title: Split Gamestart Mission 1
page.t: (Story Name Long){1021,600}(same as as gamestart name)

The quiet isolation after the battle has given you ample time to distil your overwhelming rage into a steady trickle of righteous malice. Your path is clear. To remove this stain on your honour, you must regain your strength and obliterate the unworthy Patriarch's expeditionary fleet. You might not yet have the necessary means, but as the Split say, revenge is a dish best served with the desperate screams of your mortal enemies, staring down your barrels in disbelief.

page.title: Split Gamestart Mission 2
page.t: The battle is nearing its underwhelming conclusion. As expected, the enemies of Zyarth failed once again to match the prowess of a true Split.

The hurdles that tradition places in the path of all female Split could never halt your rise through the ranks of the military. With your participation in the battle against the Fallen Families, you proved yourself to be a loyal subject of Zyarth, the oldest and most brutally cunning of the Patriarchs; at least for the moment. Now, a new opportunity arises. The campaign against the last remnants of the Argon Federation in these parts will undoubtedly bring glory to the Patriarchy. However, the fate of those soon-to-be-conquered territories is yet to be decided, and the Split were never known for their contentment.
Aid the Patriarchy in conquering these sectors or take them for yourself:

page.t: (Description; from the perspective of the player's male wingmate)Another cycle, another set of useless chores to work through. And what's worse, they've deployed us in Mars sector. I bet nothing exciting has happened around here since the end of the Argon Conflict. Personally, I'm almost hoping for one of these satellites to explode in our faces so that Mission Command has to check in on us for once.

page.title: Pioneers Gamestart
page.t:
Najia,

We would like to hire your services again to place satellites for some important scientific analysis. This involves sensitive equipment, and precise positioning is of the utmost importance, but with your track record this should not be a problem.

Pioneers Lead Scientist

P.S. Do not be late again!

This analysis is very important. We are noticing minor disturbances and need to investigate their cause and origin.

For that, it's imperative that you place several satellites in the designated positions for us to amplify our sensory capabilities.

Please get on with it as efficiently as possible. We don't know if there is a time-sensitive factor lurking behind these readings.
After noting some strange readings, a scientific expedition is tasked with placing a few satellites in a attempt to get to the bottom of the anomalous emissions.
